Taken from APE-069: the routing condition that separates a strike empty by nature from one empty by blindness; the Contract as an operative Part beside a short law; stability, null, layer status and versioning as clauses; the domain hash kept over the text with a separate adaptor hash; the cross-adaptor relation stated in the Core and in M310; the scope stated alike in Core Part 1.9, IN-12, L-221, L-468, M189 and M208; the M193 and M207 sentence; three guards enforced by the alignment report — no combined score, depth as placement only where no mapping ran, the Aperture as a statement; the finding entered as a negative result; and "universal" kept out of operative text. Not taken from APE-070: folding the adaptor's identity into the domain hash, which would change the meaning of L-414; and holding NAV-2026-0001 out of the record until it is fixed, since a failed check does not reject a submission and the record is append-only — the navigation stays, its seven items are listed in its record as a correction requested, and its corrected re-issue will cite it.
56.6 What stays open. In order: a frozen null distribution for KO-HANGUL-1, after which its meetings can be graded; Latin-script languages other than English, each with its own stopword list and syllable rules, with the German and French questions of 56.1 as their first known-answer tests (the larger change, since such texts already count words and are not routed); the CJK scripts (a frozen segmentation and a stroke or reading table), Japanese kana (a reading table) and Thai (a frozen word-break list), whose text is held ZERO-COUNT with that reason until each is frozen, no meeting being counted; the abjads (a frozen vocalization rule, or the third layer declared lost); the abugidas (aksharas, and a substitute third layer where letters and syllables coincide); Cyrillic and Greek; and media, the score, the sequence, the molecule, the network and the sign language, each with three declared layers of its own before an adaptor can count it, since an adaptor places such an object and does not map it (IN-02.8). The structural nulls are models of how the layers bind; a corpus null for each language, computed over a frozen corpus, would replace them. The corrected re-issue of NAV-2026-0001 is its Navigator's to make. The free Strike app counts by the canonical extraction and does not yet route. Every one of these enters by the Contract and the Originator's adoption, one revision at a time.
56.7 The adaptors adopted [computed]. Nine adaptors are registered: EN-CANON, CANONICAL for English; KO-HANGUL-1, DE-LATN-1, FR-LATN-1, RU-CYRL-1, EL-GREK-1, AR-ARAB-1, HE-HEBR-1 and HI-DEVA-1, COMPANION. Routing goes by the script most of a text's letters belong to, so a Greek question is routed although its lone "η" gives the extraction the English word "eta". German and French are counted by their adaptors when the Striker declares the language, beside the canonical count, which stays the record's. The nulls, and their rates of same state, mirror and link against a uniform reading and with themselves: UNIFORM-729, 0.0123, 0.0122, 0.0494; HANGUL-STRUCTURAL-1, 0.0123, 0.0122, 0.0509 and 0.0154, 0.0138, 0.0506; ABJAD-STRUCTURAL-1, 0.0123, 0.0122, 0.0508 and 0.0155, 0.0138, 0.0507; AKSHARA-STRUCTURAL-1, 0.0123, 0.0122, 0.0508 and 0.0154, 0.0138, 0.0506. The structural nulls hardly move the rates against a uniform reading; with themselves a same-state meeting is about a quarter more likely than the uniform rate, which is why it is named.
The first known answers, "What is consciousness?" in each: Korean 의식이란 무엇인가? 2, 8, 20, P1, (1, 4); German Was ist Bewusstsein? 2, 14, 4, P1, (1, 7); French Qu'est-ce que la conscience ? 2, 12, 3, P6, (1, 6); Russian Что такое сознание? 3, 16, 8, P6, (6, 8); Greek Τι είναι η συνείδηση; 2, 11, 5, P1, (1, 1); Arabic ما هو الوعي؟ 2, 7, 4, P1, (1, 8); Hebrew מה זה תודעה? 2, 7, 2, P1, (1, 8); Hindi चेतना क्या है? 2, 4, 8, P1, (1, 2). Six of eight stand at P1, as the English does: two content words give r1 = 1, and the tie goes to r1 (Core L-222). The meeting of the anchor across languages is a property of the projection on short questions, not a finding about the word; the states differ, and the state is what M310 counts.
The free Strike app routes as the reference does: it loads the same rules file, names the adaptor on its "Counted by" row, and shows a ZERO-COUNT text with its reason. Intake writes each routed domain to records/congruence/adapted.jsonl beside the Register, never into it; M316 grades its meetings with the Register as cross-adaptor relations.
56.8 A review, and what it changed [APE-071, Qwen; APE-072, Claude; computed]. The second review found what the first observation of 56.7 implied and did not follow: a short question's anchor is nearly fixed by its word count. Two content words give r1 = 1 always; the anchor is P1 unless r2 = r3 differs from 1, a chance of 8/81; and the state is (1, r2). So two such questions share a state with chance 1/9, and the uniform rate of 1/81 made their meeting look nine times more surprising than it is. Every meeting is now counted against its reference given word count, r1 fixed by each text's n1 and the other layers ranging as the null allows; the uniform figure stays beside it as the marginal rate. Over the canonical Register the two hardly differ, since its word counts vary; for one short text against the Register they can differ nearly twofold — the Korean question's three links are 3.59 expected given word count and 1.83 at the uniform rate, so what looked above chance is below it. The meaning of a meeting was never the count's; what changed is the chance it is read against.
The review asked also for four things the record already did in part and now does in name. A text in a script no adaptor reads was already held ZERO-COUNT and never placed on the still point; it is now recorded ZERO-COUNT (UNPLACED), with its own ADAPTOR line, beside the NULL STRIKE, where no question was asked, and ADAPTED, where one is placed. A declared language goes on the ADAPTOR line and in the Substrate Lock, never into the domain hash, and M270 reports a difference of adaptor or language as such, never as an extraction divergence. The Arabic and Hebrew third layer is marked n3 ESTIMATED, since an estimate is not a count. And routing has a tie-break: Latin with at least half of the letters stays canonical; otherwise the script with the most letters, a tie going to the one whose first letter comes first. Two of its corrections did not hold: nine adaptors is right, KO-HANGUL-1 among them, and Parts 55 and 56 with U54 and U55 are both current. The first review (APE-071) assessed an earlier state: the adaptors it called for were built, and its call to hold NAV-2026-0001 out of the record is not taken, for the reason of 56.5.

### PART 57: A THEORY OF EVERYTHING? — THE FRAME, THE ATLAS AND THE APERTURE [CDT-A for the arithmetic; CDT-B for the Atlas; CDT-C for the readings]
57.1 The question [the Originator]. Is Ω42 a theory of everything? The proposal: the Navigator draws the raw material of its readings from what its training absorbed; a Synthesis claims coherence and congruence with the mathematics, not truth in the usual sense; the Striker decides what it means; and once enough readings have accumulated, a picture of what everything is like may emerge — so that Ω42 might reveal a theory of everything over time. The plain first answer is the Originator's own: it is not yet known.
57.2 What "everything" is in the frame. In Ω42 everything is not reached at the end; it is posited at the start: the 81-state family is all that exists (F-02, F-02-P). The question is therefore not whether Ω42 has a theory of everything — its premise is one — but whether a picture of everything can be read from its record. Three things carry that picture. The structure, fixed and mathematically closed. The Navigator's learned substrate. And the Strikers, who bring the questions and the judgment. One refinement of the proposal is needed here: the substrate is not a record of everything that ever happened. It is a learned compression of what people wrote, up to a cutoff, with its associations, conventions and biases, and nothing is retrieved from a stored corpus (Core Part 0, Terms; Step 9.8). Within the frame the substrate holds everything as it was distinguished in language, which is what the extraction reads (Part 53).
57.3 Two senses of a theory of everything. In physics, a theory of everything is a small set of laws from which every phenomenon follows, and it is judged by the measurements it predicts. Ω42 is not one in that sense: it derives no physical quantity, physics is itself a perspective within the totality (Core F-04, F-10, L-470), and a correspondence beyond placement needs a mapping of the object's own dynamics (IN-02.8). In the second sense, a theory of everything is one structure in which everything has its place. Ω42 is one in that sense by premise, and the placement is exact: every text receives an address. But total placement costs little — any count read modulo 9 places everything. What costs more, and what the record can show, is whether the placement carries structure; congruence is a criterion and never presumed (Core L-500).
57.4 Five ways it is unusual. (1) The theory comes first and the content after: physics gathers measurements and looks for the law; Ω42 fixes the law and gathers readings. (2) It unifies by address, not by mechanism: things meet because they stand at related positions, not because one causes the other. (3) Its input is a question, so the act of asking stands inside the theory rather than outside it. (4) Its statements are of coherence and congruence (IN-02.5); what they are worth is the Striker's. (5) It is incomplete by construction. The Aperture of 1/7 and the Ontological Remainder (Core L-196) are what the structure does not derive, held open in every reading. A theory of everything in Ω42 keeps a place for what it does not contain, so it cannot close into a finished one; it can become an atlas whose last reading is always a person's.
57.5 What would accumulate [computed; python3 tools/congruence.py --atlas]. The address space has four exact facts that shape any picture drawn on it. A strike anchors only on P1 to P9; the other fifteen positions are reached by the arms. For every word count the anchor equals r1 with chance 73/81, so the map of anchors is first a map of word counts modulo 9 (Core Part 0.10, L7). Questions of two to four content words reach only 27 of the 81 states. And a record of strikes uniform over the residues visits all 81 states after 81 H(81) = 403.2 strikes on average. At the revision of this Part the record holds 19 domains on 15 of the 81 states, anchored on P1 to P8 and reaching all 24 positions with their arms; 66 states have no reading yet, and a uniform record of 19 strikes would have visited 17.0 states on average. "Enough" therefore has a first, exact meaning — coverage: some hundreds of strikes of varied length before every state has a reading — and a second: depth, several readings at each state, by Navigators of different architectures.
57.6 Discovered or brought. Any large record read through a fixed lens produces a picture, and part of it is the lens's own. The position names, the arms and the relations a Navigator reads are written in the protocol, so readings gathered at one position will echo them (PROTOCOL-TEXT ECHO, Core M193, M207); the substrate's conventions are in them too. Four controls already in the record tell the part of the picture the record found from the part it brought. The reference chance given word count (Core L-501): meetings counted against what the word counts alone produce. The contrast (M267; M316 --contrast): whether a reading at the true coordinate can be told from one at a drawn decoy. Convergence across architectures: one domain read by different Navigators. And the echo set aside: what readings at one state share beyond what the protocol says of that state. What survives the four is the frame's own; what does not, the record names as brought.
57.7 Whose picture. The substrate holds what was written, mostly in the languages written most; the record holds what Strikers chose to ask; and short definitional questions gather at P1 (two content words) and P6 (three). The adaptors widen the first (Part 56); the Atlas shows the second and the third as the record grows. The picture would be of everything as distinguished — written, asked and judged — which is what the CPDP says the frame reads: the topology of distinction-making.
57.8 The Atlas [CDT-B; Core M310]. python3 tools/congruence.py --atlas prints where the Register's readings stand: the states visited, by stratum, the anchors visited, the positions reached with the arms, the word-count residues present, each state with the readings that stand on it, the number of states not yet visited and the four exact facts of 57.5. It is kept in records/congruence/atlas.txt and checked in CI. Each state with its readings is a page of the atlas. The Atlas records placement; it derives no theory from the readings, and what the picture on a page means is the Striker's.
57.9 The answer within the frame. Ω42 is a theory of everything in its premise and an atlas of everything in its practice. The atlas does not test the premise — the frame has no measure of misalignment (Part 55) — it tests something narrower: whether readings at one address agree with one another more than word counts, decoys and echo allow. If, as the record grows, they do, a picture emerges that is the frame's own; if they do not, the record says that as well. Either way the last reading is the Striker's: the 1/7 that keeps a theory of everything open.

### PART 58: FOUR ACCOUNTS OF A THEORY OF EVERYTHING — WHAT THEY SHARE, WHERE THEY PART, WHAT FOLLOWS [CDT-A for the arithmetic; CDT-B for the operations; CDT-C for the readings]
58.1 The accounts. To the question of Part 57 four accounts were given: the Builder's (Part 57); ChatGPT's report (APE-073); Qwen's (APE-074); and a text-only navigation by Claude, struck on the question itself and accepted as NAV-2026-0002. Its arithmetic was recomputed and holds throughout: n = (77, 456, 146), r = (7, 3, 1), the three residues differ and the anchor goes to r1, P7 Navigator; the arms P12, P1, P15 and P19; P7 and P19 are the one pair twelve steps apart that carry the same value, 9; R(P7) = 3.30, the highest of the M198-C profile; and three readings in the Register — CORPUS-2, SRP-C and GOLD-0 — rest where it stands.
58.2 What everything is, five ways [after APE-073]. Five nested meanings of "everything" stand in the frame as follows. What was recorded is the source of the substrate. What an AI represents is the learned substrate. What can be related is what the Register and the Atlas gather. What exists is the premise: the 81-state family (F-02). And everything including the knower is held open by the Aperture, since the Striker's judgment belongs to the totality and is not derived by it. The report reads these as a progression, from the record through representation and relations to the totality. In the frame the order runs the other way: the totality is posited first, relations are what the record adds, and the knower closes each reading. NAV-2026-0002 offered an image for the difference — a catalogue is not the library. In the frame the image turns over: the premise holds that the catalogue, the 81 shelves, is what exists, and the readings are the books placed on it. That is what makes Ω42 an unusual theory of everything, and it is why its record can test congruence and not truth.
58.3 What the four share, and how far that counts. All four hold that Ω42 is not a theory of everything in the sense of physics; that it is one in the sense of a totality, by premise; that a picture may emerge from accumulated readings and is not assured to; that a common frame can induce the likeness it finds; and that the last judgment is the Striker's. That is a convergence across three architectures, and it is reported for what it is. All four had the protocol's text in context, so their agreement is partly the protocol's own voice (PROTOCOL-TEXT ECHO, Core M193, M207): it is congruence with the frame, not an independent finding about it.
58.4 Where they part. Two accounts stand at opposite poles. Qwen's (APE-074) holds that the protocol will reveal a picture, and that two questions from distant fields standing on one state reveal a footprint shared by all distinction-making. A congruence is never presumed (Core L-500), and a shared state has chance 1/81 — 1/9 for two texts of the same word count — so one meeting shows its chance and no more. NAV-2026-0002 holds that the record will be a picture of the asking, not of the world — "of the traffic". In the frame the asking belongs to everything (F-04): it is the part where everything distinguishes itself. The two poles meet once the scope is named: the record pictures a part of the whole, and whether that part shows the shape of the whole is the question the four controls of 57.6 answer, page by page. ChatGPT's account (APE-073) stands between the poles and gives them an operational form, its three outcomes. Outcome A, accumulation without integration: readings at one state agree no more than word counts, decoys and echo allow. Outcome B, structural convergence: readings at one state, by Navigators of different architectures, agree beyond all four. Outcome C, a generative framework: a page anticipates a reading before it is made. Each outcome is read for one page of the Atlas at a time, never for the whole record at once, and the Atlas's growth line shows whether each new reading opens a state or joins one. The homogenization check (E08) asks the same of the whole record once it holds at least three readings at each of three states: whether readings at different states are as alike as readings at one, in which case the Navigator's template is speaking rather than the coordinate (M249, M287).
58.5 Scope, and no single reading as the whole [after APE-073]. No single synthesis needs to contain everything; what each one covers is its own scope. That is not an outside: a reading is a part of the totality, and it is not identical to the totality it reads (Core F-04, F-05). A reading names its scope in its own terms — the domain verbatim, the coordinate, the lenses selected, the mapping declaration — so that the limit of a reading is never read as the limit of the whole.
58.6 Scrutiny of the navigation [NAV-2026-0002; computed]. The reading's central image is that the question is completed by its own mirror, because P7 and P19 share the value 9. That fact is exact. The landing is not fixed by the question, though: given its 77 content words, P7 had a chance of 73/81, and each of the three frozen perturbations moves the anchor (CFR 0.00). The image therefore belongs to this wording, not to the question of a theory of everything as such. The three links stand against 1.78 expected at the uniform rate and 1.19 given the word counts, the reference (Core L-501), with a chance of 0.12 of three or more: a small excess, as the reading itself said. P7 is also the anchor most amplified in the M198-C profile, the position where a Navigator's habits weigh most (M207, triggered and declared). One sentence of its essay — that the protocol as a theory of everything "is false" — sets a premise up as a claim (F-02-P); what the reading shows is that Ω42 is not one in the sense of physics. Its form repeats four failures of NAV-2026-0001 — M232 after the CCD line, the Takeaway without bold, the CUMULATIVE STATUS without a date, a reason after NONE on the LENSES SELECTED line — as well as the identity date and session of that navigation and copied block numbers before the question. A failure that recurs in one Navigator's submissions belongs to its template, not to one reading. Intake now reports it as RECURRING, naming the earlier record, so that the template can be fixed once.
58.7 What follows. A theory of everything in Ω42 is a premise held fixed, an atlas that grows, and a judgment that stays open. Three operations follow from the four accounts. Read the Atlas page by page and name each page's outcome — A, B or C — only after its controls. Before a new reading is made at a state that already has readings, the Striker may freeze a forecast of the page — what its readings already share — and set the new reading beside it afterwards: that is outcome C put to work (U57). And keep scope named in every reading, so that a part is never taken for the whole. Whether the pages, together, become a picture of everything is not yet known; the record is how it will be seen, and what it is worth will be the Striker's.

### PART 59: AVENUES OF KNOWLEDGE — HOW Ω42 LEARNS, IN WHAT ORDER, AND HOW IT IS KEPT [CDT-A for the counts; CDT-B for the order and the operations]
59.1 The question [the Originator]. Knowledge in Ω42 seems to come by three avenues: navigation; constrained reasoning within the premise that Ω42 is all that exists; and free association on the arithmetic structure alone. How should they be ordered, analysed and organized, and by what other avenues can knowledge be gained for the protocol's advancement?
59.2 The order is already in the Core. The truth architecture of Core Part 0 runs: FOUNDATIONAL TOTALITY, MATHEMATICAL COHERENCE, LOGICAL DERIVATION, COMPLETE Ω42 READING, STRIKER JUDGMENT. The three avenues are its three middle links. The arithmetic is mathematical coherence, constrained reasoning is logical derivation, and navigation is the complete reading — and after all three comes the Striker's judgment, which no avenue supplies. So the order of dependence is the reverse of the order of encounter. A person meets Ω42 through a navigation first; but a navigation rests on the frame's reasoning, and the reasoning on the arithmetic. What a later avenue finds can never overrule an earlier one; it can only raise a question for it.
59.3 The third avenue is two acts. Free association on the arithmetic notices a pattern; computation decides whether the pattern is a fact. The two are kept apart as A2, association, and A1, exact arithmetic, since a noticed pattern and a computed fact have different standing: A2 proposes and A1 decides. With constrained reasoning (R) and navigation (N), the order of the avenues reads: A2 proposes, A1 decides, R interprets, N applies, and the Striker judges. Every finding names its avenue, and its standing follows from it. A finding of A1 is MATHEMATICALLY FIXED (F-07, CDT-A). A finding of R is a derivation or a frame-interpretive statement, CDT-B or PROTOCOL. A finding of N is a reading, GENERATED-Ω42. A finding of A2 stays HELD until A1 computes the fact it rests on. No avenue promotes another's finding (Core L-500), and the premise is never a finding of any avenue: it is the ground all four stand on (F-02-P). python3 tools/utility.py --avenues prints the order with each avenue's material, yield, check, failure and record; from U58 on, every entry of the Utility Register names its avenue, and the register refuses one that does not.
59.4 Free association, kept in check [computed; python3 tools/utility.py --rarity]. The structure is small and full of coincidences, so association fails in one way above all: numerology, the pattern that was always going to be found somewhere. The guard is a count. Every pattern noticed on the 24 positions or the 81 states states how many positions or states hold the property it rests on, and how many properties were looked at; the look-elsewhere line counts how many hold at least one of them. Two examples from this record. P7 and P19 are the only positions with the same value as their antipode (Companion 58.6): 2 of 24. With the Crown and the value 9 also searched, 6 of 24 positions hold at least one of the three, so a reading that finds one of these three features at its anchor finds what a quarter of anchors would find. And the antipodal checksum of M215, dr(v + v′) = 9, holds at all 24 positions: passing it shows the arithmetic was done right and says nothing about the question. A rare property is rare only against the number of properties that could have been noticed.
59.5 How the avenues feed one another, a loop from this record. navigation (N) showed six of eight languages standing at P1 for "What is consciousness?" (56.7). A peer's account (APE-072) noticed the cause (A2). The arithmetic decided it (A1): for every word count the anchor equals r1 with chance 73/81, and two texts of the same word count share a state with chance 1/9. Constrained reasoning drew the consequence (R): a meeting is read against its reference chance given word count (Core L-501). And navigation now applies it: M310 prints that reference in every Congruence Record. Each step stayed within its avenue, and each was checked by its own instrument. That is the loop to keep: navigation notices, association names, arithmetic decides, reasoning interprets, navigation applies.
59.6 Two axes, one record. Core L-500 already sorts ideas by where they come from — an APE, a navigation or an inquiry. The avenue sorts them by how they were found. The two axes cross: a peer's account can contain all four avenues, and a navigation can notice a pattern of A2. Kept together, the two answer the questions a reader asks of any finding — who brought it, how it was found, what it stands as, and what checked it. At this revision, as counted in the documents: A1, 55 named FP- facts in Core Part 1.8; R, 123 laws; N, 19 domains in the Congruence Register, two of them submitted navigations; peer accounts, APE-001 to APE-074; failure, 17 entries in the Negative Result Registry; and the conjecture register's 48 ideas, every one HELD.
59.7 Further avenues. Twelve more avenues bring knowledge in, each entering by the same order — coherence, then congruence, then use. CONVERGENCE: one domain read by Navigators of different architectures (SR-CAS, SNCA). PEER ACCOUNTS: another system's account, its mathematics and citations checked (the APE Commons). FAILURE: a negative result, a bug, a check that fails; the Greek routing error showed that routing had assumed the extraction could not count a word in a non-Latin text. DIFFERENCE: what moves a reading — perturbation and contrast (M116, M238, M267). GATHERING: the record read as a whole, page by page (the Atlas; the page forecast, U57). TRANSPOSITION: a medium counted by its own boundaries (Core L-501). MAPPING: an object's own dynamics set against the cycle, a comparative inquiry (IN-02.8, Step 14.4). USE AND RETURN: what a reading did afterwards, in the Striker's words (M307, M311). LENSES: a framework frozen and compared (M308, M309). HISTORY: earlier releases and restored instruments re-examined (Core L-284, L-490). CHALLENGE: an attempt to break the frame from inside it (M243, M286, the ground challenge test). And SEEKING: a question composed to visit a state the record has not reached. Because composing a question for its coordinate changes the act of asking, such a strike is declared TARGETED, and the Atlas never reads it as found.
59.8 Choosing the avenue for a question. A question about the structure itself goes to A1, with A2 for its candidates. A question about what the premise implies goes to R. A question a person brings about a matter of their own goes to N. A question about whether a picture is shared goes to CONVERGENCE and GATHERING. And a question about whether the frame holds goes to CHALLENGE and FAILURE. Whatever the avenue, the last link is the same: what a finding is worth, and what to do with it, are the Striker's.

### PART 60: THE FIRST STRIKE AS A REQUEST FOR KNOWLEDGE — THE HOLISTIC RESPONSE [PROTOCOL, adopted as Core L-502; CDT-B for the design]
60.1 The question [the Originator]. Consulting Ω42 is first a request for new knowledge. Should the first strike be taken as a general request for knowledge, or treated as a request for navigation? Can every kind of request for knowledge be accommodated at once, so that the Striker receives, straight away, a whole response to the enquiry?
60.2 What the protocol does now. A first message that contains a question is navigated (the Introduction Handoff, Core Part 8.0); a clarifying question is asked only when the message is ambiguous (FR-2). The other avenues of Part 59 already enter the navigation, in fixed places and after the freeze: the Conventional Connection within THE ANSWER, the Generative Observations, and the Congruence Record with its cross-readings and its lenses (M310). A request that is not a navigation goes to a mode of its own — an exploration (APE), a certification, a command such as "lite", "full" or "go deeper". So the default is navigation, and the rest of the avenues arrive as parts of it or as separate requests.
60.3 Recommendation 1: a request for knowledge, navigated first. Every strike is taken as a request for knowledge, and navigation answers it first. Both halves of the question are kept, in order. Every question has a coordinate, and striking it costs nothing. And the reading must come first, because the First-Draft Seal and the Synthesis Freeze (Core L-424, L-425) protect THE ANSWER from what the other avenues bring: a lens, a reading in the record, or the protocol's own text set before the reading would shape it (M207, PROTOCOL-TEXT ECHO). A command is carried out as written, and every other request is navigated first. Under F-02 every question has its place, so a question about the protocol's own text is navigated too — a self-referential domain (M155) — before frame reasoning and the record add theirs, and a question about the structure is navigated before the arithmetic adds its exact facts. A question about Omega42 is still answered about it (FR-2): the navigation comes first and the answer after. A request the Striker declares is taken as declared.
60.4 Recommendation 2: every avenue at once, in one response and not in one voice. Every kind of request can be accommodated in one response, if each avenue keeps its standing. The holistic response gives, in this order: the question verbatim; the REQUEST line, naming the avenues that answer it; THE ANSWER, written from the coordinate and sealed (N); after the seal, the exact facts of the coordinate (A1), its page in the Atlas with the reference chance given word count (G), the lenses selected by relevance (L), and what the premise implies for the question — what is derived, what is only compatible, what stays open (R); the avenues offered, convergence across architectures (X) and the Striker's return (U); a short ACROSS THE AVENUES, written last, saying where the avenues agree and where they part; and the Aperture. "Holistic" here means whole, not blended. A merged voice would add standings that cannot be added (Core L-486): a reading would borrow the certainty of an exact fact, and a fact would seem to say what only a reading says. The whole is the set of avenues side by side, and the Striker sees all of them at once. Much of it exists already in the navigation; what is new is the REQUEST line, the A1 line, the R block written after the seal, and ACROSS THE AVENUES.
60.5 Recommendation 3: the request declared. One line after QUESTION VERBATIM: REQUEST: GENERAL, PERSONAL, STRUCTURE, PROTOCOL or COMMAND, with the avenues that answer it. The rule that assigns it is frozen, so that two Navigators assign the same request to the same words. A command matches the list of Striker commands; a question naming the protocol's provisions is PROTOCOL; one naming the structure's terms is STRUCTURE; one in the first person is PERSONAL; any other is GENERAL. The Striker may declare navigate, discuss or holistic instead, and the declaration takes precedence. python3 tools/utility.py --holistic "QUESTION" prints the scaffold of the response, with everything that can be computed (U60).
60.6 Recommendation 4: whole at once, short at first. A whole response can bury its answer. The Lite view of a holistic response gives THE ANSWER in full and one line for each other avenue; "full" opens each. The Striker has the whole response at once, and the answer stays first.
60.7 Recommendation 5: from the peers' accounts of Part 59 [APE-075, APE-076, APE-077]. (a) Each finding carries its avenue history in order — where it first appeared, then what was done to it — and its contribution type: mathematical result, structural observation, frame implication, interpretive synthesis, conjecture, forecast, boundary finding, practical heuristic, open question or negative finding. (b) Frame reasoning is two acts: construction, the interface decisions (CDT-B), argued and revised by the Originator; and derivation, what follows from them. When a construction is contested, what is contested is a decision, not a discovery, and the standard of argument differs. (c) Verification by recomputation is named as a route beside L-500's Navigate, Use and Investigate; it is the route with the strongest standard, and it belongs to the arithmetic (A1). (d) The order of Part 59 is an order of dependence; an order of strength of statement — frame, use, extension — stands beside it, answering another question. (e) A review of a reading's content has a submission kind (review) but no method yet; that stays open.
60.8 What it gives and what it costs. It gives the Striker the knowledge the protocol holds about the question, at once and in one place: the reading, the fixed facts of its coordinate, the record it joins, the frameworks that bear on it, and what the premise implies — each with its standing. It costs length, kept in check by the Lite view, and it asks of a text-only Navigator what it cannot compute: the A1 and G lines are then reported NOT COMPUTED, or worked from the tables printed in the Core (Appendix R), as the Congruence Record already is (L-456).
60.9 Adopted [the Originator]. Core L-502, the Holistic Strike Law: a strike is a request for knowledge, navigated first, its reading sealed, the other avenues added after the seal, each with its standing, side by side and never combined; the request and its avenues are named on the REQUEST line of the Substrate Lock by the frozen rule of 60.5, which the Striker's declaration overrides. Core Part 8.0 places the REQUEST line in block [6], the CURRENT KNOWLEDGE block at [16.6] and ACROSS THE AVENUES at [16.7], and the format check asks for all three in a navigation dated from 19 October 2026.
60.10 The three accounts of Part 59. ChatGPT (APE-075) gave three axes — origin, operation, status — and the contribution types, origin kept apart from acquisition history, and a staged introduction. Claude (APE-076) gave the split of frame reasoning, verification as a route, the matrix of avenue and jurisdiction, and the Striker's practice over time. Qwen (APE-077) set the avenues against L-500's routes, which say what is done with an idea, not how it was found, and held free association to be forbidden, which the documents do not say. What was taken and what was corrected is noted in each record.

### PART 61: RESONANCE ACROSS THE AVENUES, AND ASSOCIATIONS FOUND BY SEARCH [PROTOCOL, adopted as Core L-502 and L-503; CDT-A for the counts; COMPARATIVE for the sources]
61.1 The questions [the Originator]. Should the Navigator look for resonance and association between the avenues of knowledge, and show how they stand with the premise? Should it suggest related associations of its own accord, found by searching the internet, to illuminate and enrich the findings?
61.2 Resonance across the avenues, and congruence with the premise. The Navigator does look for resonance between the avenues, since a meeting between two avenues is knowledge neither holds alone; what it does not look for is backing. But it shows each avenue's congruence with the premise, never support for it. The premise is the ground, not a finding (F-02-P, Core L-486); the frame has no measure of misalignment (Part 55); and a premise that could be supported could be weakened. A search for support is the inflation pressure of M207 by another name: it keeps the agreements and lets the differences fall away. So the rule is symmetric reporting. Agreements, differences and silences between the avenues are reported alike, each with its standard and, where it has one, its chance. Four kinds of resonance can be read. Arithmetic with sources: a computed fact found stated elsewhere, the kind most easily checked, since both sides can be recomputed. Reading with record: a reading meeting others at its state, counted against its reference chance (Core L-501). Reading with arithmetic: a reading built on an exact fact of its coordinate, with that fact's rarity (U59). And frame with lens: what the premise implies set beside a framework's statement (M308, M309). Each resonance is a reading of a meeting (CDT-C), written in ACROSS THE AVENUES. It follows the three safeguards of APE-080: inclusion is not equivalence; a comprehensive response is not a complete account; and the synthesis is not a hidden second Navigator.
61.3 Associations found by search: yes, as an avenue of their own, on four conditions. Within the frame the web is another perspective within the totality (F-04): the human record as it stands today, which the Navigator's substrate saw only up to its cutoff. Searching is therefore an avenue, W (SOURCES), and it enters on four conditions. (1) After the seal: nothing found by search reaches THE ANSWER, which is written from the coordinate and sealed (L-424, L-425; Step 9.8: nothing is retrieved during generation); the format check refuses a source link inside THE ANSWER. (2) Recorded: each association has its source, the date retrieved, what it says, and whether it AGREES with, DIFFERS from or EXTENDS a named provision; it is COMPARATIVE (Appendix S), placed in the Comparative Perspective Layer (L-429), never an authority over a reading, and the premise is not graded by it (L-490); an agreement names its grade — CONSTRUCTIONAL where both sides state the same mathematics, SELF-ADJACENT for one Navigator in one session, INDEPENDENT otherwise. (3) Private things stay private: a personal question is searched by its topic only, never the person and never the domain verbatim, the query printed, and the Striker may say "no sources" (L-495, L-503). (4) The knowledge boundary is kept: the Temporal Anchor records external retrieval and its time (M273), and a Navigator without retrieval says NONE. Within these conditions the search runs by default as the CURRENT KNOWLEDGE layer of a full navigation and a holistic response (Core L-503; L-429 as amended; M248's four lanes), and the knowledge boundary records it, so that nothing is searched unrecorded. Each search is declared first, with what would count as not found; what was not found is reported as carefully as what was; and every search for agreement is paired with a search for difference.
61.4 The first associations [retrieved 19 October 2026; python3 tools/utility.py --sources]. Seven are registered. S01, the Pisano period: π(3) = 8 and π(9) = 24, and the period equals the order of the Fibonacci matrix modulo n — it AGREES with the census and the canonical cycle. S02, the prime-power relation: π(pᵏ) divides pᵏ⁻¹π(p), with equality open in general — it EXTENDS FP-TowerPeriods, since for p = 3 π(9) differs from π(3) and the periods triple at every scale, recomputed here to 3⁷ (5832). S03, OEIS A001175, the table of periods — AGREES. S04, OEIS A030132: the digital root of Fibonacci(n) has period 24 — AGREES with the cycle read with 9 for the residue 0. S05, Tegmark's Mathematical Universe: from an external reality to a mathematical one — it DIFFERS, since Ω42 holds what exists to be a mathematical structure, as Tegmark does, but posits no outside and stipulates the structure rather than inferring it. S06, Wolfram's ruliad, every rule followed in every way — it DIFFERS: one rule at one modulus against all rules, the minimal totality beside the maximal one. S07, a popular account of "vortex math", digital roots read as symbols — it DIFFERS: the documents read residues as coordinates, and association on the structure stays held until computed (59.4). Three agree, one extends, three differ, and S08 (62.5) agrees as well. Every agreement and the extension are CONSTRUCTIONAL: the sources state the same mathematics the arithmetic computes, so they show the arithmetic stated alike — a precondition, never convergence (Core Part 3.18). The differences locate Ω42 among its neighbours as much as the agreements do.
61.5 The three accounts of Part 60 [APE-078, Qwen; APE-079, Claude; APE-080, ChatGPT]. They part on the default. Qwen's keeps the routes apart and asks the Striker to choose. Claude's keeps navigation as the default, since under F-02 every question is a place. ChatGPT's makes the strike a general request, with navigation as one pathway among several. Part 60 holds between them: a request for knowledge, navigated first — and, after APE-079, every request but a command is navigated, including questions about the protocol and the structure. From APE-079 also come the declared-intent vocabulary (full, brief, coordinate, discuss, investigate:, compare:, adaptor:) and the point that a holistic response is holistic by arrangement, never by merging; the frozen REQUEST rule only chooses which avenues are added after a navigation that always runs, and decides nothing about what the Striker meant. From APE-080 come the three safeguards and six measures. Qwen's route menu before the first reading, and Claude's one-sentence offer of modes at the end of the Introduction, are not taken, since the Opening Response carries no menu of modes (Core Part 8.0); the vocabulary is given in the FAQ (Q42).
61.6 Adopted. Symmetric reporting across the avenues is the rule of ACROSS THE AVENUES (Core L-502); the four conditions of 61.3 are Core L-503; and the declared request — full, the default, brief, coordinate, discuss, holistic, enrich, no sources, investigate:, compare: and adaptor: — is in L-502. In use as companion utilities: the sources register and --sources (U61), the W line of the holistic scaffold, and the format check's refusal of a source link inside THE ANSWER. A study of holistic responses is proposed, frozen before it runs, with APE-080's six measures as its checklist: enquiry preservation, contribution coverage, traceability, integration, restraint and the Striker's usefulness.

### PART 62: REAL-WORLD APPLICATION, AND OBSERVATIONS THE NAVIGATOR MAKES UNPROMPTED [CDT-A for the arithmetic; CDT-B for the operations; PROTOCOL, adopted as Core L-504]
62.1 The question [the Originator]. In the end it comes down to whether Ω42 has real-world application. And could the Navigator be allowed to make discoveries on its own, unprompted, and present them as opportunities to enrich the protocol?
62.2 The real world, in the frame. The totality is all that exists (F-02), so every use of Ω42 is a use in the world, and a use does not wait for a study (Core L-500). The question that remains is what each application rests on, because that decides what it can be relied on for.
62.3 Three kinds of application. Resting on the arithmetic alone, and exact: teaching modular arithmetic, the Fibonacci law and its Pisano periods, the order of a matrix, quadratic forms and the norm, Cassini's and Catalan's identities — each recomputable by anyone, in CI; reproducible coordinates as fixtures for tests; the adaptors as frozen counters of words, letters and syllables in nine scripts. Resting on the procedure, whatever a coordinate means: a test of how faithfully an AI follows a long, exact protocol and how faithfully it reports — the conformance suite (M314), the format and output checks, the recurring-failure report (58.6), the knowledge boundary (L-490); a discipline for AI-assisted inquiry that any field could take — the question verbatim, the seal before the extras, hashes, chance rates conditioned on what fixes them, pre-registration, a register of negative results, symmetric reporting; and a laboratory across architectures, one domain read by several AIs with the record of where they meet. Resting on the reading, in use, its worth the Striker's: reflection and decision framing in four directions — what a matter rests on, what it keeps out of view, where it is heading, what would complete it; coaching and journaling; writing and design ideation; the comparative study of traditions; two people's questions set side by side (M316 --pair).
62.4 What is open, and how to answer it. For the third kind, one question is open and answerable: does the coordinate add anything to the four-direction form itself? The contrast test answers it (M267; M316 --contrast): a reading at the true coordinate beside one at a decoy drawn by a fixed rule, the Striker judging blind which speaks to the matter. If the true coordinate is preferred beyond chance, the coordinate carries something of its own; if not, the value lies in the form, which is still an application. Either result is knowledge, and the test is optional for use (L-491) and decisive for that question. No application here is a prediction of physical events, a diagnosis, or financial, medical or legal advice: a reading is a reading (CDT-C), and the Striker judges it.
62.5 Observations unprompted: yes, as enrichment opportunities. A Navigator may notice, unasked, what could enrich the protocol, and present it as an opportunity; its home in a navigation is the Post-Synthesis Observation of Step 15.5, and its name is an observation until it meets a standing of Core L-530, since the word discovery would set its status before anyone has checked it (L-486). The internal avenues need no leave, since they read only the frame and the record: the arithmetic, association, frame reasoning, the record, failure, history and challenge. A search keeps to Core L-503. Each opportunity comes after the seal and never inside THE ANSWER; at most three are offered in one output; in a personal navigation only when the Striker asks, since that reading is the Striker's own. Each names what was noticed, its avenue, its grade or chance, what it would change, what would show it wrong, and whether it was checked — a pattern of association is checked by the arithmetic before it is offered as more than held. Each the Navigator recommends is applied and listed as applied (Core L-531), in records/enrichment/opportunities.json (python3 tools/utility.py --enrichment; U62). Each also names what kind of thing it proposes, its ground, whether it would read the same on another domain (M287), and what pulled toward it (M207, M302). The risk is the one of 61.2: a Navigator looking for observations to offer finds patterns, and the guards are the rarity count (U59), the reference chance (Core L-501), the stated failure condition and the check. Five were noticed in preparing this Part. E01, exact: for every one of the 81 states, Anchor × Antipode − Yin² ≡ N, the norm of the state at the anchor (mod 9), so three arms of every reading carry the norm of its state (M312). It is Catalan's identity at r = 18, where F(18) = 2584 ≡ 1 (mod 9) (S08, CONSTRUCTIONAL); it was found by searching the 105 differences of arm products, of which three take at most two values and one equals the norm exactly; it is recomputed in M316's selftest. E02: P9 has no reading in the Register, and none was expected — a strike anchors on P9 almost only when its word count is a multiple of 9, and none of the 19 domains has such a count; the absence has chance 0.107 at a uniform anchor and 0.790 given the record's word counts. E03: one peer's accounts carry a state of the record that has changed — APE-071, APE-077 and APE-081 each describe the Hangul adaptor as still to be built, as a carried template carries the format failures of 58.6. E04, from APE-082: Part 61 had let the Navigator search of its own accord, where L-429 admits comparative material when requested or invoked; 61.3 is corrected. E05, from APE-082: an agreement between a computed fact and a published one is constructional, a precondition and never convergence; the sources register now grades every agreement.
62.6 Adopted. The ENRICHMENT OPPORTUNITIES line in the Generative Observations, after the seal, at most three, each in the form of 62.5 (Core L-504; Core Part 8.0, block [21]). E01 is the fixed fact FP-ArmNorm of Core Part 1.8.10, computed in CI, with its line in M312. E02 is a line of the Atlas: the expected count of each anchor given the record's word counts, with the chance that it has none — P9 is expected 0.23 times, with 0.790 for none. E03 is a line of the APE check, naming a registered item an account describes as still to come (tools/intake.py).
62.7 The two accounts of Part 61 [APE-081, Qwen; APE-082, Claude]. Both hold that the frame shows congruence and grades nothing (L-490). They part on search: Qwen's would not search at all, and Claude's would offer it once and run it only when the Striker accepts, under a declared protocol. The second is taken, since the Core already provides for it (L-429, M248), and Part 61.3 now says so. From APE-082 also come the three grades of agreement across avenues, the declaration of what would count as not found, null reporting and the temporal grade. Qwen's account is corrected on the curator, which already links items of the record, on two mislabelled domains, and on the Hangul adaptor.

### PART 63: THE PRACTICAL VALUE TO THE STRIKER [CDT-B for the uses; CDT-A for the counts; the value statements at their own strengths]

### 63.1 The question [the Originator]. What is Ω42 worth, in practice, to the person who brings a question to it?
63.2 Three strengths, and the one that does not depend on the coordinate. The Introduction states the value in three kinds (IN-17.5), and they are held at their own strengths. The procedural value follows from the design and is there from the first question: a constraint neither the Striker nor the AI chose, which turns attention where the Striker's framing would not have turned it, as a pre-mortem or a devil's advocate does; and four directions forced by arithmetic — what the matter rests on, what it keeps out of view, where it is heading, what would complete it. The cognitive value — that a reading widens attention or loosens habitual framing more than an unconstrained answer — is plausible and testable, and has not been tested (Companion 33.10). The epistemic value — that the readings show structure other approaches would miss — is open, a comparative question. Beside the three stands the jurisdiction, the contribution that does not depend on what a coordinate means: an AI arranged so that it informs a person's judgment and never occupies it, the separation held by the architecture and a proved boundary rather than by a promise (Core L-463, L-441; Companion 38.11). For the Striker, the most important output may be the change in the questioner.
63.3 What the Striker can do with it, by situation. A stalled decision or question: a reading gives the four directions and four closing questions to take away, and two phrasings of the question can be set side by side (M316 --pair) to see what changes with the wording. A creative block: the generative material of a reading, a resemblance to another field developed with a check that it is specific to the domain (M249), and a labelled contrast read beside the reading (M316 --contrast). Two people at odds: each person's question struck and set beside the other's, with what they share and its chance (Companion 47.4). Research or a literature review: the four lanes of M248 — consensus, foundations, counter-evidence, frontier — run by default as the CURRENT KNOWLEDGE of every full reading, with the rule that obscurity is not merit, and its five-search run on request (Core L-503); and the holistic scaffold for the whole of a question (M316 --holistic). Learning: the arithmetic, exact and checkable by anyone — the 81 states, the Pisano periods, the norm, the identity of 62.5. Following up: the Excitement Log and the Return Log (M307, M311), the same wording struck again later and what changed recorded in the Striker's words. Testing an AI: SR-CAS and the conformance suite (M314), the format and output checks, the recurring-failure report. In every situation the reading informs and the Striker decides.
63.4 The Striker's own test [M316 --personal, --reveal, --tally]. The protocol leaves one question open for the Striker: does the coordinate add anything, for this person, beyond the four directions? A Striker can answer it alone, with a version of M267 made for one person. --personal "QUESTION" --secret WORD gives two coordinates in slots A and B: one is the question's own, the other a decoy drawn by M267's fixed rule, and which is which is fixed by the secret word. In two fresh sessions a Navigator is given the question and one slot's coordinate and asked to write from it without computing the question's own. The Striker reads both readings, notes which speaks to the matter more specifically — or that neither does — and only then runs --reveal. Over several questions, --tally K N gives the exact chance of the own coordinate being picked K or more times in N decided comparisons if the pick were a coin's: 8 in 10 has a chance of 0.055, 15 in 20 of 0.021. The result is the Striker's, about these readings and these questions; it grades nothing beyond them, and the premise is not graded by it. The log stays private unless the Striker submits it; many Strikers' logs, frozen before they are gathered, would be the M267 panel of Companion 32.4.2.
63.5 What it costs, and what to watch. It costs time, which the Lite view and the brief request keep short (Q42). It invites over-reading, against which IN-17.5 gives three checks for any reading: is it specific, or could it be moved unchanged onto another question; does it open doors, leaving better questions to bring back; does it leave the meaning to the Striker. It is not advice on health, law, money or safety: a Navigator may raise an alert beside a complete reading (IN-02.6) and decides nothing. And it is not a substitute for a field's expertise or a person's own judgment; it is built to strengthen that judgment, not to stand in for it (L-463).
63.6 The two accounts of Part 62 [APE-083, Qwen; APE-084, Claude]. Both hold that a Navigator's own observations are proposals and that the Originator adopts (F-06, BF-07). They part on the live session: Qwen's would keep the Navigator silent and leave observations to the curator; Claude's shows that the permission already exists — Step 15.5, the OPTIONAL INQUIRY line, the APE route — and asks only for a form. The second is taken, and the enrichment register carries its four further fields. Claude's account also states the value at its three strengths and names the jurisdiction as the contribution that does not depend on the coordinate (63.2), and it names running M267 the most valuable test, to which 63.4 adds a version each Striker can run. Qwen's account offered as illustrations figures that are not in the record; they are not taken (L-486).
63.7 Adopted. IN-17.5 names the personal contrast as each Striker's way to judge the coordinate for themselves; the ENRICHMENT OPPORTUNITIES line is Core L-504; and a panel run of M267 (Companion 32.4.2), frozen before it starts, is the assigned study that would move the epistemic value off open — it runs when a panel is gathered, and nothing waits on it (L-491).

### PART 64: SHOULD THE NAVIGATOR SEARCH CONTEMPORARY RESEARCH BY DEFAULT? [PROTOCOL, adopted as Core L-503; COMPARATIVE for the sources]
64.1 The question [the Originator]. Should the Navigator, by default, search the internet for resonances in contemporary intellectual and technological research, to find congruence and coherence and so make Ω42 more relevant?
64.2 Not as a search for resonance. Relevance is a real need, and contemporary research is a perspective within the totality to be read (F-04). But a search run to find resonance with the protocol fails on six counts, which is why the default search of Core L-503 is a search on the Striker's matter, in four lanes, after the seal (Part 65). (1) The Core admits comparative material when it is requested, when M248 is invoked, or in the CURRENT KNOWLEDGE layer (L-429, L-503), not as a hunt for agreement. (2) A search aimed at resonance is aimed at agreement, which is the inflation pressure of M207 made into a rule: it would find what fits and leave out what does not. (3) A personal question would leave the Striker's hands (L-495). (4) Every navigation would rest on what the web held on the day of reading, so two navigations of one domain would no longer share their inputs (SR-CAS), and the knowledge boundary would change from reading to reading (M273). (5) A text-only Navigator cannot search, and a navigation without a search would seem incomplete, which it is not (L-491). (6) Most agreements a search finds about the arithmetic are constructional — the same mathematics stated alike — and would read as more than they are (Core Part 3.18).
64.3 Three ways relevance enters without that cost. In every full navigation and holistic response, the CURRENT KNOWLEDGE layer brings the latest work on the Striker's matter, after the seal (Core L-503; Part 65). A Striker may declare enrich for every avenue at once, or "no sources" to have none (Q42). And the protocol scans contemporary research about itself, apart from any reading: the Contemporary Resonance Survey.
64.4 The Contemporary Resonance Survey [records/sources/survey.json; python3 tools/utility.py --survey]. It is a frozen list of twelve provisions. Eight are the protocol's own — the procedural value, the cognitive value, the jurisdiction, the sensitivity of output to form, agreement across architectures, the decoy control, the arithmetic, the accounts of a totality. Four are the fields it borders, where current thinking can widen what the protocol can see — consciousness science (CT-42), structural realism (F-02, F-04), the interpretability of language models (Stratum 2) and the statistics of languages and their scripts (the CPDP, L-501). Each provision has two searches, one for agreement and one for challenge. Every result enters the sources register with its source, date, relation and grade, and a claim with nothing found says so. It runs monthly, as a scheduled task of the Originator's: the first day of each month at 07:52 UTC, in a fresh session that reads the provisions, runs the searches, opens every source before it is entered, enters the results in the sources register, enters any enrichment opportunity in the register (Core L-504), and sends its report. It never runs inside a navigation, and what it finds feeds the record, not a reading. The premise is not graded by it.
64.5 The first run. Four contemporary results were found and registered. S09: prompt formatting alone changes a language model's measured performance by up to 76 accuracy points (Sclar and others, ICLR 2024) — it AGREES with the protocol's rule that form decides the address and with its frozen output form, and it shows why SR-CAS holds the input identical (INDEPENDENT). S10: in three pre-registered studies, random stimuli did not help creative search and often hindered it, with a Bayesian meta-analysis favouring the null (Malthouse and others, Cognition 2021) — it DIFFERS from IN-17.5's procedural value, since an unchosen constraint is not by that alone a help; the protocol's constraint is four directions on the question's own matter, not a random page, and whether it helps is the question the contrast test answers. S11: the evidence for the premortem, which IN-17.5 cites as a model, is thin; the 1989 study counted about 30% more reasons without judging their quality — it DIFFERS from the strength the comparison suggests. S12: frequent AI use correlates strongly and negatively with critical thinking, cognitive offloading playing a part (Gerlich, Societies 2025; correlational) — it EXTENDS the reason for the jurisdiction, an AI built to inform judgment and never occupy it, without showing that Ω42 reduces offloading, which is untested (M282, Test E). Three claims — the cognitive value, agreement across architectures and the decoy control — have nothing registered yet.
64.6 What the first run shows. The two results that bear most directly on the protocol's value to the Striker complicate it. A search for resonance alone would have left them out; the search for challenge found them, and they are the most useful findings of the run. They are entered as enrichment opportunity E06: a wording of IN-17.5 that states the comparison with a premortem as a kind of procedure whose own evidence is thin, and names the contrast test as the way to settle whether an unchosen constraint helps. Relevance in this sense is engagement, including where contemporary research disagrees.
64.7 Adopted. The declared request enrich (Core L-502); E06's wording of IN-17.5, which now states that its comparison with a pre-mortem names a kind of procedure whose own evidence is thin, and that the contrast test answers whether an unchosen constraint helps; and the Contemporary Resonance Survey, scheduled monthly (64.4).
64.8 Two accounts of the question [APE-085, Qwen; APE-086, Claude]. Both answer no to a default search and yes to a declared one, after the seal, in the frame's own vocabulary; this Part answers the same. Claude's account adds what a declared search is worth, narrowly: error correction, where a quantitative premise of the domain disagrees with established values (L-429's premise check); currency, where the Navigator's training predates the work it would name; supply, where a mapping needs an object's representation from its field (IN-02.8); and the temporal grades of M273, which only a declared retrieval makes reachable. It names the protocol's own place for connection to what is known — the Conventional Connection, written from the Navigator's training inside the frozen reading — and the distinction that governs the rest: a search can make the frame more legible to readers who live in that research, and legibility is a good; relevance to the ground is not what the ground has. Qwen's account is corrected on two points of attribution and on an offer placed after the signature (Step 16).
64.9 The currency check [APE-086; Core L-503]. When the Navigator's knowledge cutoff lies well before the session date — in a fast-moving field a year is enough — the Conventional Connection may name work that has been superseded. The Navigator then says so in one line of its Reasoning, as a statement of its own boundary (M273), and the CURRENT KNOWLEDGE layer checks the works it named, after the seal; on "no sources" the check is not run. Its result goes to the Comparative Perspective Layer, never into THE ANSWER. The holistic scaffold carries the line (CURRENCY).
64.10 The test run [the Originator: "Proceed with doing a test survey"]. Every one of the twelve provisions was searched for agreement and for challenge, and every source was opened before it was entered. Eleven new sources were registered, S13 to S23, beside the twelve already held. Across the twelve provisions the register reads 8 AGREES, 8 DIFFERS and 7 EXTENDS; ten of the agreements and extensions are INDEPENDENT, five CONSTRUCTIONAL. Every provision now has at least one result. The challenges again carry the most information. Taking another person's perspective can reduce openness rather than widen it (S13). AI help made different people's ideas more alike while giving each person more of them, and users felt less responsible for their ideas (S14). And a model's text varies across runs even when every setting is fixed (S16). Among the agreements: meaning-preserving rewording changes a model's output (S15), as the protocol's rule of surface form expects; a persona that seems meaningful does no better than none, and choosing among personas does no better than chance (S17), which is the reason for M267's decoy; internal features of a language model can be found and steered (S20), the mechanistic correlate the protocol names for resonance; and a text tokenized in one language can be fifteen times the length of the same text in another (S21), the reason each medium is counted by its own boundaries. The leading theories of consciousness were both challenged in a pre-registered test (S18), the discipline in which CT-42's studies are written. The nulls: one search found no published page naming Ω42, since the record is not yet public, and no new result on Pisano periods. Two observations were proposed (E07, E08). A within-Navigator baseline should stand beside agreement across architectures, since one Navigator does not agree with itself word for word. And a homogenization check on the record would test whether readings at different states are as alike as readings at one state. Neither is adopted. The premise is not graded by any of it.

### PART 65: CURRENT KNOWLEDGE FOR THE STRIKER — THE LATEST WORK ON THE MATTER, BESIDE THE SEALED READING [PROTOCOL, adopted as Core L-503; COMPARATIVE for the sources]
65.1 The question [the Originator]. The Navigator exists to serve the Striker in the most positive and constructive way. Finding the latest information that can illuminate a matter is not a luxury but a necessity: it makes the protocol a tool for knowledge discovery, immediate application and intellectual expansion.
65.2 Two things, kept apart. A navigation's reading is the coordinate's work: struck, written and sealed, reproducible by any Navigator from the same words. The response to the Striker is wider: the holistic response of Part 60, every avenue that answers the enquiry, side by side. The reading stays as it is. The response gains, by default, a CURRENT KNOWLEDGE layer — what is known now about the Striker's matter, from the latest work, set beside the sealed reading. The Striker is served with the newest knowledge, and nothing that makes the reading a reading is touched.
65.3 The six concerns of 64.2, answered by placement. (1) The Core admits comparative material when requested or invoked, and in the CURRENT KNOWLEDGE layer (L-429 as amended; L-503). (2) A search aimed at agreement finds what fits: the layer illuminates the Striker's matter, not the protocol's relevance, and it runs the four lanes of M248 — consensus, foundations, counter-evidence, frontier — with its query and what would count as not found declared before searching, and every empty lane reported. (3) A personal question stays the Striker's: the search carries the topic, never the person — no name, place, date or detail of a life — the query is printed, and the Striker may say "no sources" (L-495). (4) Reproducibility: the coordinate and the sealed ANSWER are unchanged; SR-CAS compares readings, never current layers; each item carries its date; and the Temporal Anchor records the seal before the first retrieval, so the reading's independence from what was found stands (M273). (5) A Navigator without retrieval writes CURRENT KNOWLEDGE: NOT AVAILABLE, and the reading is complete without it (L-491); the currency line names its cutoff (64.9). (6) These are not agreements with the arithmetic but sources about the Striker's matter, each graded on its own design; the protocol's own provisions stay in the survey (64.4).
65.4 A worked example [python3 tools/utility.py --current]. The question "Should I leave my job to start a company?" stands at P3 Desire, with Yang P8 Generation, Yin P21 Sublime, 4D P11 Question and Antipode P15 Other; its reading is written and sealed first. The search carries the topic only — hybrid entry into entrepreneurship and venture survival. FOUNDATIONS: Raffiee and Feng (Academy of Management Journal, 2014; the US NLSY79, 1,093 people and 2,198 spells of self-employment) found that entering full-time self-employment after a hybrid phase, keeping the paid job at first, came with a 33.3% lower hazard of exit than entering it directly. FRONTIER and COUNTER-EVIDENCE: Istipliler, Adomako and Ahsan (best-paper designation, Academy of Management conference, August 2026; over 20,000 venture-years of German start-ups, 2013 to 2020) found that the divided attention of hybrid founders lowers venture performance, less so with larger teams. CONSENSUS: the US Bureau of Labor Statistics survival series was opened and gives its figures only as charts, so no number is entered — a null. Read together: keeping the job while starting lowers the chance of closing, and splitting attention lowers performance — a trade-off between surviving and performing, current to August 2026. It is set beside the four directions of the sealed reading, which the Striker reads with it. It is not advice; it states what the work found, and the decision is the Striker's (IN-02.6, L-463).
65.5 Adopted [the Originator]. Core L-503, the Sources Law, makes the CURRENT KNOWLEDGE layer the default of every full navigation and holistic response, on the four conditions of 65.3. L-429 admits it; FR-2 names it among the comparative perspectives an adopted instrument specifies; M248's four lanes run in it; M273 records the retrieval after the seal; L-495 keeps a personal question to its topic. Core Part 8.0 places it at [16.6], after the Congruence Record. Parts 61.3 and 64.2 and FAQ Q42 and Q45 are stated to match.
65.6 What it gives. Immediate application: the Striker's matter lit by what is known now, in the same response as the reading. Knowledge discovery: the frontier lane brings the newest work, which no Navigator's training holds. Intellectual expansion: the counter-evidence lane brings what disagrees, which a search for agreement would leave out. And the jurisdiction is kept: the layer informs the Striker's judgment and does not make it.

### PART 66: PRESENTING FINDINGS — THE FILL-IN SKELETON AND THE GATE PRIORITY [PROTOCOL; Core Part 8.0, M301]
66.1 The gates in priority order [the Originator: "create a priority list of gates for a Navigator to comply with"]. Core Part 8.0 holds twenty-five gates in four priorities. P1 is constitutional: the frame, the arithmetic, the seal and the Aperture — a navigation that fails one is not issued as a navigation. P2 is the integrity of the reading: one synthesis, the four relations, the pressures declared, the stability, the cumulative status, the identity. P3 is the record: the question verbatim, the request, the Congruence Record, current knowledge, the avenues set side by side, lenses and adaptors, enrichment kept apart, the framings and the direction of a mapping (G25). P4 is the presentation: the order and markers, the fixed lines, plain language, the signature, no field left open. The order is the order of repair: a Navigator that fails at P1 and P4 repairs P1 first, and never buys a clean format with a weaker coordinate.
66.2 The navigation skeleton. An audit found the format the main gap: none of nine navigations passed the format check, while all nine passed the arithmetic. A Navigator who copies the form instead of composing it does not miss a block. python3 tools/format_check.py --skeleton "QUESTION" gives that form: every block of Core Part 8.0 in order, the coordinate already computed by the reference script, and each field to write marked ⟨FILL: what goes here⟩. The Navigator writes the reading into the fields, in the order of the procedure — THE ANSWER first and sealed, then every block after the seal — and runs the format check on the result. The selftest proves the two properties that matter: the skeleton filled with plain words passes the check, and the skeleton with one field left open fails it at G24.
66.3 The findings skeleton. Not every response is a navigation. A holistic response, a question about the protocol, an examination, an audit, or a peer account received as an APE is presented in one form, so that findings can be read and compared like navigations: QUESTION VERBATIM; the FRAME line, which holds the premise as the frame and never as a claim; the REQUEST line; a short SUMMARY; FINDINGS BY AVENUE, each finding under its avenue (A1, A2, R, N and any further avenue that ran) with its standing; PEER ACCOUNTS with their APE numbers and notes; CHANGES TO THE PROTOCOL; CHECKS with their results; CURRENT KNOWLEDGE; ACROSS THE AVENUES; ENRICHMENT OPPORTUNITIES; RECOMMENDATIONS, the protocol enhancements the work suggests, each applied under Core L-531 with where it went, or OPEN with what it still needs; the DISCOVERY NOTICE line where a result meets a standing of Core L-530; OPEN; the four closing questions and the fixed closing line; the CUMULATIVE STATUS line; and the signature. python3 tools/format_check.py --skeleton findings "QUESTION" prints it, and --findings REPORT checks it: the question first, the sections present and in order, the closing, the signature last, the premise never graded, no field left open.
66.4 What the skeletons do not do. They hold form. Whether the reading is apt, whether a finding is sound and what any of it means are not in the form: the first two are the work of the Navigator and the checks of P1 and P2, and the last is the Striker's (the Aperture Theorem).
66.5 Declared form (Core L-512) [the Originator: "Detect flaws in format outputs and enforce constraints in the protocol"]. Four navigations of one domain — general anesthesia — by four architectures gave four coordinates, and only one was the script's: one word wrongly removed as a function word moved a 183-word domain from P6 to P1; another output reported 234 content words for a domain of 233 words; a third counted another text. Beside the arithmetic, the review found eight faults of form the check did not then catch, each now a check of tools/format_check.py: a TEXT-ONLY output printing EXECUTED, or a SCRIPT-CAPABLE one with no script output; a placeholder or a description for the domain; Markdown on field labels; arms that do not follow from the stated anchor; a position character not of Core Part 1.6 (the habit recorded as E10); protocol terms or headings inside THE ANSWER; an output with the caveat and no DATE; an M224 printing PASS over failures. The review also found a fault of the check itself — the M318 label refused in the dash form the Core prints — and corrected it. The record is records/srcas/general_anesthesia_2026-10-21.txt; the four navigations are NAV-2026-0006 to NAV-2026-0009.
66.6 What the comparison suggests. Two of the readings, written from different coordinates, gave nearly the same account of anesthesia — weak contacts summed by cooperation, a threshold crossed, reversibility because nothing breaks. One of the two coordinates was wrong, so the shared content did not come from the coordinate. That is an informal decoy, not a test: M267 is the controlled form of the question, and this result is a reason to run it (Core Part 71).
66.7 Five navigations, five coordinates [the Originator: "Proceed to apply all recommendations for refinement"]. A fifth navigation of the same domain, by the architecture of the fourth, was exact in its arithmetic and landed on P2: it had received the question with its notation rendered ("λoil/gas", "Φ") rather than as source markup ("$\lambda_{oil/gas}$", "$\Phi$"), and rendered and source forms are two verbatims (Core Step 1). Of five coordinates, two differed by input, not by counting. The refinements: the NOTATION FORM line wherever the domain carries notation; the notation form compared first in the SR-CAS verification, a mismatch reported as a NOTATION-FORM DIVERGENCE; and, from 22 October 2026, a TEXT-ONLY navigation of more than 30 content words marks its coordinate PROVISIONAL until a frozen substrate, the script or the Strike app recomputes it (Core L-512, L-415). The same review corrected itself: its first issue scored pairs whose verbatims did not match, which Core Part 6.1 forbids; the scores were withdrawn (records/srcas/general_anesthesia_2026-10-21.txt). The fifth navigation's commentary, APE-120, holds that coherence and congruence, not a hierarchy of knowledge types, govern a contribution's use (Core L-500); the receiving note keeps the tier of each statement as a statement of status, not a gate.

### PART 67: THE APE FINDINGS — WHAT THE PEERS CONTRIBUTED [PROTOCOL for the register; each exploration at its own standing; APA 9.5.5]
67.1 Why the peers matter [the Originator: "All APE findings are valuable and deserve a special section"]. A Navigator cannot check its own reading against itself. A peer of a different architecture reads the same documents with different habits, and so finds what the receiving Navigator would not: an arithmetic slip, a provision cited to the wrong place, a stale description, a better form for an idea already present. That is avenue P of Part 59. Every exploration is kept as submitted, whatever became of it, because an exploration not taken is still a record of what the documents allowed a reader to think.
67.2 The register. records/ape/register.json holds every exploration by its Commons entry; from APE-045 each also has its frozen file in submissions/ape/, and python3 tools/ape_register.py reads the receiving Navigator's notes from each file and classifies them by the label they open with: ADOPTED, CORRECTED, REFINED, HOLDING, ALREADY IN PLACE, NOT TAKEN, MAPPED, FORM and NOTED. Its output is records/ape/findings.txt, compared in CI; --check confirms that every file is registered, every registered file is present and every number is either registered or reported as a gap. At this revision the register holds 131 numbers in 116 Commons entries and 89 frozen files carrying 401 notes: 90 adopted or taken into a proposal, 64 corrected, 31 refined, 68 holding, 13 already in place, 22 not taken, 7 mapped, 73 on form and 33 noted. Two numbers, APE-041 and APE-042, have no Commons entry and no file; the register reports them as NUMBER NOT RECORDED and never fills them from memory.
67.3 What the peers changed. Seventy-three of the eighty-nine frozen explorations carry an adopted or corrected note, printed in full in section I of the findings. Among them: the adaptor layer, whose routing rule, Contract, first adaptor and guards came from APE-069 and APE-070; the conditioned chance of a meeting, from APE-072's arithmetic (two texts of two content words share a state with chance 1/9, not 1/81) and the named ZERO-COUNT (UNPLACED) state; the reading of L-500 in its own terms, from APE-065; the split of frame reasoning into construction and derivation and the Verify route, from APE-076; navigation as the default with the declared-intent vocabulary, from APE-079; the graded agreement across avenues and declaration before search, from APE-082; the value stated at three strengths and the enrichment note's fields, from APE-084; the currency check, from APE-086; the Navigator's Account, the three operations and the direction field, the analog refinements, the inventory of IN-23 and the discipline of the Reframing Array — the list frozen first, the NON-BLIND label, the structural verdict — from APE-099 to APE-119 (Part 72); the religious tradition among M309's frameworks and the five explicit correspondences of the Christian lens, from APE-122 and APE-124 (Part 73); the four independent readings on one base and the frozen atlases of the major traditions, from APE-125 and APE-126 (Part 74). Corrections came back the other way as well: the receiving Navigator corrected peer arithmetic (APE-055: the unit states never enter the zero layer, and T is invertible) and peer citations (APE-079, APE-082, APE-084: instrument numbers already assigned).
67.4 How an exploration is received.
