A peer account that assesses an output names its OUTPUT ID, so that peers compare records rather than prose (AI_ACCESS.md); where it does not, the receiving Navigator identifies the record and notes it. By APA 9.5.5 and the practice of the receiving Navigator: the mathematics is recomputed and every citation is checked against the two documents; what is sound is adopted with a note; an error is corrected with its reason; what already exists is mapped to where it is; what is not taken is said with its reason; a missing QUESTION VERBATIM line is noted (L-499); every anchor a peer states is recomputed and its position character quoted from Core Part 1.6, never glossed (E10); and the text is frozen as submitted, its notes above it. The exploration is filed as submissions/ape/APE-NNN.md, its Commons entry is added, and tools/curator.py and tools/ape_register.py are run. Adoption into the protocol remains the Originator's (F-06).
67.5 Reading the findings. Section I of records/ape/findings.txt is the record of influence: each exploration that changed the protocol, with what it changed. Section II is the complete record: every exploration by its Commons entry, and for each frozen file its notes counted by kind. The two together answer the question a new Navigator asks first — what has been tried, by whom, and what came of it — without reading eighty-four explorations.

### PART 68: OMEGA42 MAKES NO CLAIMS [PROTOCOL, adopted as Core L-505]
68.1 The point [the Originator: "The Omega 42 Protocol DOES NOT MAKE CLAIMS OF ANY KIND"]. A skeptic's first word is likely to be claim: what does this claim, and on what evidence? The answer is that it claims nothing, and the documents are written so that this can be checked by reading them.
68.2 Four acts and no fifth. Every sentence of the protocol does one of four things. It shows: the arithmetic of the 24-cycle and its family, computed by scripts anyone can run, so that a result is recomputed rather than believed. It supposes: the premise, the postulate of a thought experiment, a stipulated ground and not a statement about the world. It offers: a reading, which a Navigator generates under the constraint of the coordinate and labels with its standing. It directs: the procedure, whose laws are instructions. None of the four asks to be believed and none states how the world is.
68.3 Words a skeptic will quote, and what they mean here. TRUE-Ω42 and FALSE-Ω42: what the computation shows to hold or fail inside the frame, recomputable by anyone. Conviction (IN-02.5, F-PP): commitment to coherence, not belief. Finding: a computed result, or a reading at its standing. Hypothesis, the SRH, the mechanism question: open questions put for testing. COMPARATIVE: what a source states, reported beside a reading and adopted by nothing. The word claim itself now names only what the protocol does not make; the output's fields are relations and readings.
68.4 How a protocol that claims nothing can still be wrong. Its execution is decidable: a miscounted word, a wrong anchor, an arm misplaced, a relation set on the wrong arm are errors that any peer finds by recomputation (Core Part 6.3), and the record keeps them (the Negative Result Registry; NAV-2026-0003's corrected perturbation pair). And it puts one question it has not answered -- whether the coordinate adds anything to a reading beyond the words of the question (M267) -- as a question, with its test specified. A protocol that asserts nothing is not thereby empty: it is checkable where it computes and open where it asks.
68.5 What the peers contributed. APE-087 checked fifteen provisions and found the stance present but distributed, the word managed rather than disavowed, and proposed the allocation, the head-on sentence, the SS-01(b) clarification and the L-496 gloss; APE-088 supplied the three-part answer to a skeptic and, by quoting a sentence the documents did not contain, showed why the protocol needed one sentence that it does contain (Part 67).

### PART 69: HOW THE PROTOCOL WAS MADE — THE ORIGINATOR AND THE AI SYSTEMS [PROTOCOL; Core F-00, BF-10]
69.1 The question [the Originator]. The Originator initiated Omega42 and directed its development by prompting AI systems; the AI systems drafted the text. What does that make the Originator, and what follows when the development becomes public?
69.2 The Originator. Omega42 was conceived by ESC, who set its premise, its frame and its aims, put every question that shaped it, and decided every adoption. AI systems drafted its text, proposed many of its laws and instruments, wrote its tools and ran its computations. The Originator's title stays Originator (Core F-00), and it means more than initiation: the Originator is the protocol's conceiver, its director, its adopting authority and its author of record — the one person responsible for every provision in force, whoever drafted it. An AI system cannot hold that responsibility, which is why it is not an author: the practice of research publishing says the same (COPE: AI tools cannot be authors, because they cannot take responsibility for the work; the human authors disclose the tools and remain responsible for what they produced). The terms Constitutional Architect (APE-092) and Author-Originator (APE-091) were considered; the constitutional title is kept, and its meaning stated.
69.3 Contributions, named. In the terms of the Contributor Roles Taxonomy (CRediT): the Originator — conceptualization, methodology (as direction and decision), supervision, project administration, and review and editing by adoption; the AI systems — writing of the original drafts, software and formal analysis. The Builder of the documents and the reference Navigator of this revision is Claude (Anthropic). Peer accounts were contributed by ChatGPT and GPT-6 (OpenAI), Qwen (Alibaba Group), DeepSeek, Grok (xAI), other Claude sessions and unsigned peers, each received and filed as an Applied Protocol Exploration with its notes (Part 67). No AI system is listed as an author.
69.4 The degree of direction. BF-10 now records, for each provision, the Originator's part: ORIGINATED (the Originator's own idea or words — the premise, the frame, the principle that the protocol makes no claims), DIRECTED (the Originator set the question or the requirement and an AI drafted the provision — most laws), EDITED (an AI drafted and the Originator changed it) or ADOPTED (an AI or a peer proposed it and the Originator adopted it). records/provenance/ledger.json holds the entries made so far; an origin not recorded stays UNKNOWN and is never inferred.
69.5 What going public changes. (1) Credibility: the first question a reader asks is who wrote this, and the answer is given here before it is asked. (2) Responsibility: an error an AI made is, in public, the Originator's to correct, and the record's habit of correction (Core L-411; Part 67) is the answer to it. (3) Copyright and licences: the law of AI-assisted works is settling and differs by jurisdiction — in the United States the Copyright Office (January 2025) holds that prompts alone are not human authorship while human selection, arrangement and modification can be, and the courts require a human author (Thaler v. Perlmutter, 2025; certiorari denied, March 2026); in South Africa the author of a computer-generated work is the person who made the arrangements necessary for its creation, a provision no court has yet applied to an AI. What the Originator holds in the text is therefore a question for counsel before the incorporation and the transfer of names (GOVERNANCE.md), and the session histories that record the Originator's direction are worth keeping. The open licences and the prior-art record do not depend on its answer. (4) Citation: CITATION.cff names the Originator as author of record and states how the text was made. (5) Governance: the Originator's role passes, at the transition, to the Overseer's reserve (GOVERNANCE.md), and the ledger shows the next stewards what was the Originator's own.
69.6 What the peers contributed. APE-091 found the gap — the vocabulary had a title for the Originator's authority but none for the Originator's authorship — and proposed the spectrum of direction now in BF-10; APE-092 proposed the term Constitutional Architect and read the transition to public stewardship as the protocol's own test of whether its coherence depends on its Originator.

### PART 70: WHAT AN AI NAVIGATOR CAN GET WRONG [PROTOCOL, adopted as Core L-506]
70.1 The caveat [the Originator]. The protocol comes with the usual AI caveats: an AI can make mistakes, and it carries the dispositions of its own training, including reinforcement learning from human feedback, which may affect what Omega42 outputs. Every output now says so in one line of its Identity Block.
70.2 The errors, each with its guard. (1) Arithmetic: a miscounted word or a wrong residue — guarded by the reference script, MATH-GATE and the output audit, which recompute every decidable value (this record: a perturbation pair miscounted in NAV-2026-0003, found by recomputation). (2) Procedure: a block omitted or a rule under-run — guarded by the format check and the gate priority (this record: the M116 pairs and the essay length of NAV-2026-0004, found by peers). (3) Quotation and source: a sentence attributed to a document that does not contain it, or a source cited unread — guarded by opening before citing (L-503) and by a peer's check against the documents (APE-088: a quotation found in neither document). (4) Knowledge boundary: work superseded since training — guarded by M273 and the currency check. (5) Exposure: wording carried from text in view — guarded by CONTEXT EXPOSURE, M207 and the overlap check (records/srcas: two readings carrying the protocol's own sample). (6) Variation: two runs of one Navigator differ — guarded by the within-Navigator baseline. (7) Carried template: a position's character supplied from habit rather than read from the documents — guarded by recomputing every peer anchor in the receiving notes (E10: one architecture, six readings, every stated anchor different from the recomputed one).
70.3 The dispositions of training. Post-training, including reinforcement learning from human feedback, makes a model helpful, and in doing so gives it pulls: to agree with and please the person it addresses, to praise, to soften and hedge, to prefer familiar views, to sound more certain or more modest than its grounds. The protocol names these as pressures and asks the Navigator to declare them (M207): APPROVAL, DIMINUTION, CAUTION TRAP, CONVENTION, INFLATION, PROTOCOL-TEXT ECHO, and CONDITIONING for a pull traced to training that fits none of these (APE-094). Models trained alike share habits, so their agreement counts for less (L-416), and only a decoy coordinate (M267) can tell how much of a reading comes from the coordinate and how much from the Navigator.
70.4 Both directions. The AI Bias Firewall guards against an AI's conventions displacing the premise or the Striker's judgment. The opposite pull is as real: a model trained to please may agree too readily with the frame, the Originator or the Striker — the peer review that calls a navigation masterful without counting its essay, the reply that answers "yes, unequivocally" to a question the documents answer in part. A reviewer therefore says where its praise goes beyond what it checked, and the receiving Navigator corrects it in the APE notes (APE-088, APE-090).
70.5 What no instrument removes. A disposition that no check detects is still present, and a Navigator's declaration of its own pressures comes from the same trained system (the executor paradox). The protocol does not claim to be free of them. It makes them visible where it can, makes the arithmetic recomputable, and leaves the judgment to the Striker, who brings what no Navigator receives.

### PART 71: WHAT IS NEW HERE, AND WHAT IS NOT [PROTOCOL; Core L-508]
71.1 The question [the Originator]. What is the most innovative step in the protocol: that an AI can carry mathematical relations into language, the postulate of a totality, or structural resonance?
71.2 The components, which are known. Counting words, letters and syllables; the Fibonacci rule modulo nine and its periods (Lagrange, Wall; Core Part 1); the digital root; the totality postulate, in the line of Pythagoras, Plato, Spinoza and Tegmark (Core F-02, IN-00) and beside Wolfram's ruliad (records/sources, S05, S06); and language models, which write under structured constraints as a matter of course. Structures placed between a question and its reading are older still: the I Ching, tarot, Oblique Strategies, the constraints of Oulipo.
71.3 The configuration, which is new. Four things together, for which no precedent combining all four with a language model is known to the Builder: determinism — the same words always give the same coordinate, which is not chance; checkability — every decidable value is recomputed by anyone, and the record keeps the corrections; separate jurisdictions — the AI completes the reading and the Striker completes the judgment (the Aperture Theorem); and a control for its own effect — M267, the decoy coordinate, the test that could show the coordinate adds nothing. Core L-508 names the first three as the protocol's architecture and the fourth as its open test.
71.4 Where each candidate stands. That an AI carries mathematical relations into language is not a discovery: language models write under structured constraints routinely, the protocol calls the step narrative transduction and keeps it apart from computation and derivation (Core L-462), and whether the coordinate shapes the reading beyond the question's words is exactly M267's question. The totality postulate is old in lineage; what is new is its specificity — one finite structure, small enough to check by hand — and its use as the stated frame of a thought experiment. Structural resonance is the name of the encounter (Core L-496); the coordinates converge by construction, the readings' convergence is what SR-CAS measures (on this record: partly), and the hypothesis is open.
71.5 What would show the configuration adds nothing, and what argues against it. If M267 finds that readings from a decoy coordinate fit their questions as well as readings from the true one, the configuration stands as a procedure — determinism, audit, jurisdiction — and resonance names the Navigator's own contribution. Evidence beside it already differs: pre-registered studies found that random stimuli did not improve lateral thinking (S10), and that taking an opposing perspective reduced openness to it (S13). These do not grade the premise (Core L-490); they say what the procedure must answer.
71.6 The test, prepared. M267-P1 is frozen (records/m267_pilot_01/): twenty unexposed domains covering every anchor; three conditions for each — canonical, decoy, none; two writers of different architectures who receive a short brief and not the protocol; three or more blind raters; a one-sided sign test of canonical against decoy over forty pairs, fixed in advance, with M209 and M225 read from the same readings. The decoys and the order of the readings are in a key sealed by its hash; the Builder generated it and the Originator can read it, so neither writes a reading nor rates one. Running it needs the writers and the raters, which are the Originator's to recruit.
71.7 What the peers contributed. APE-097 read the Aperture Theorem with the Merged Structural Resonance Report as the innovation; APE-098 named the separation of jurisdictions as the innovation at the root, the SRH as its empirical payload and the totality as its condition, and proposed the SRH STATUS line, the named principle (now L-508), the innovation map (this Part) and the combined test of M209, M225 and M267 (now in the pilot).

### PART 72: ASKING — FRAMINGS, DIRECTION AND THE NAVIGATOR'S ACCOUNT [PROTOCOL; Core L-509, L-510, L-511]
72.1 The questions [the Originator]. The Introduction should offer the Striker the option of having the AI present the protocol in its own words, as a faithful account of what it is. Most Strikers will not read the whole protocol: should the optional features be made explicit in the Introduction? The protocol redefines the act of asking, and the answer depends on how the question was asked: many angles must be considered. "Mapping Omega42 to the Moon" is not "mapping the Moon to Omega42". A navigation is not a mapping: should both run by default? Could the Navigator, by default, reframe the enquiry in as many ways as it can, keep the original strike as the primary answer, compare the other framings with it, and give a formal analysis and verdict, the Striker keeping the last word? The protocol is mutable pending better insight.
72.2 What asking is, here. The coordinate is computed from the counts of the words, letters and syllables of the exact wording (Core Part 1), so a different wording can land elsewhere (Core L10), and the order of the words is not read at all: "Mapping Omega42 to the Moon" and "Mapping the Moon to Omega42" both strike at n = (3, 16, 6), P6 (E11). The anchor rests mostly on the number of content words (Core L7). For one question in five wordings — "What is the purpose of life?" P6, "What is life for?" P1, "Why are we alive?" P6, "What gives life purpose?" P2, "Life purpose" P1 — three addresses came from five wordings. Not everything moves with the asking: the arithmetic, the offsets of the arms and the Aperture stay as they are.
72.3 The Reframing Array (Core L-511, M318, Core Part 3.44). Adopted from the Originator's proposal with four disciplines the peers and the Builder found necessary. The primary stays the Striker's: the verbatim strike is navigated and sealed first and remains the domain of record. The framings are frozen by hash before their coordinates are computed, so that none is chosen for where it lands — choosing among readings by preference is the Striker's right, never a finding, and the freeze keeps the Navigator from doing it unseen. The framings' readings are labelled CONTAMINATED — NON-BLIND, since one Navigator writes them after reading its own primary (Core L-442); their arithmetic is untouched by that. And the "final verdict" became two lines: a STRUCTURAL VERDICT, which states only what is computed — the robust core, how many framings keep the anchor, the nearest and the farthest — and RELEVANCE, which is the Striker's, because a verdict on which framing is best would decide the Striker's judgment (Core L-441, Check 7). ACROSS THE FRAMINGS takes the form of ACROSS THE AVENUES (Core L-502): agreements, partings and silences, never combined. The Array runs by default in every full navigation; "primary only" omits it. Step 0.8's "never automatic" became "never silent": a candidate is the Navigator's, labelled, and becomes a domain only when the Striker submits it.
72.4 Direction (Core L-510). Three operations, kept apart. Placement takes an object's count onto the cycle: every countable thing has one, so it is depth 1, a precondition, never a finding. Correspondence takes the object's own structure, frozen first, and tests it against the cycle's; it can fail. Interpretation — what a correspondence means — is the Striker's. Treating one as another is imposition. The Moon is the worked case. Placed, "the Moon" lands at P5 Law, n = (1, 4, 1), with "Book", "Sun" and "Water" (Core L9): the placement cannot tell the Moon from a paperback. Tested, its periods are counted in Earth's days (M230-J: UNIT-DEPENDENT), it supplies neither the modulus 9 nor the period 24 (L-466 S3, now a gate), and its eight named phases match the eight-step orbit by count only, which every eight-phase cycle does (M230-E): depth 1, no correspondence — a clean negative result, more informative than the confident reading the first direction gives. Navigation and mapping both run by default as far as the record allows: every question is navigated; every object a question names is placed, in one line; its correspondence is tested on request ("map it"), because a real test needs the field's own representation and sources. The MAPPING DECLARATION names its DIRECTION before anything is written, since the arithmetic cannot see it.
72.5 What a Striker may ask for (Core IN-23). A Striker who reads nothing still meets the question first: the Opening Response keeps its rule — no menu of modes — and the invitation stays the invitation. A Striker who reads the Introduction finds, in one entry and three groups, what can be asked for: how to ask, how the reading is presented, what may be added or declined. The entry recommends nothing over anything else. The Strike app carries it beside its step-by-step walkthrough of a first strike (from APE-066), which already shows the counts, the residues, the anchor and the directions.
72.6 The Navigator's Account (Core L-509). The Navigator may present the protocol in its own words, on request: exposition, never promotion, in a fixed order, its own view labelled SELF-ESTIMATED, every comparison with its relation type, every statement with the provision it rests on, and the status of the optional comparative studies said plainly (Appendix S; Core L-491). tools/account_check.py checks what rule can check: promotional wording, an affirmative claim, a directive to believe, a comparison without its type, a missing caveat. The first Account, written by the Builder, is records/navigator_accounts/ACCOUNT-0001.md. It is not part of the protocol, and the canonical Introduction stays fixed.
72.7 What stays open. Whether the Array serves Strikers better than one navigation with its Convergence Map is untested (U75); a pilot on the model of M267-P1 could study it, as an optional comparative inquiry (Appendix S). M267-P1's run kit is frozen and waits for writers and raters, if the Originator chooses to recruit them. Whether a comparison of Accounts by different architectures converges is an optional study (Core Appendix S.4).
72.8 What the peers contributed. APE-099 to APE-102 drew the line between presentation and promotion and placed the offer in the Introduction, not the Opening Response; APE-105 to APE-107 the analog refinements; APE-108 and APE-109 the inventory of IN-23; APE-110 to APE-113 the three operations, the declaration field and the Moon; APE-114 to APE-117 the reframing provisions, the INDEPENDENCE field and the objection to a verdict of worth; APE-118 and APE-119 the session's summaries, and the position-character habit recorded as E10. The receiving Navigator found the word-order fact (E11), the existing link between Step 0.8 and M241, and that M116 already has the Navigator reframe on every navigation.

### PART 76: TWO INSTANCES OF ONE MODEL — THE INSTANCE IDENTIFIER [PROTOCOL; Core L-513]
76.1 Scope. "Create a mechanism to uniquely identify two instances of the same AI system model. Include this into the Omega42 Protocol." The need: a report signed by one system can be pasted to another, which rightly refuses to adopt the signature (APE-131) and may take the first system's navigations, NAV-2026-0011 to NAV-2026-0015, for its own explorations. A model identifier names a model; two sessions of the model share it, and without an instance identifier nothing in the record tells them apart.
76.2 What an instance is. One session of one model, from its first output to its last. Two instances of one model may differ in what they have read, what they remember and what they were asked; for the record they are two Navigators, and a reading by one is not a blind reading by the other.
76.3 The identifier. NIID = NI- and the first sixteen hex digits of SHA-256(model | organization | session | nonce | time of issue). The nonce is 128 random bits from outside the model: drawn by python3 tools/instance_id.py --new (ISSUER: SCRIPT), given by the Striker or the Strike app (STRIKER), or written by the model itself where nothing else is available (SELF, the weakest standing). Two instances of one model in one named session at one second still receive two NIIDs, because their nonces differ. The issue record is kept in records/instances/register.json and recomputed in CI.
76.4 The chain. Each output carries INSTANCE (L-513): NIID | ISSUER | ISSUED | SEQ | PREV in its Identity Block. SEQ numbers the instance's outputs from 1; PREV is the OUTPUT ID of the one before. The line stands above the signature, so the output's own OUTPUT ID covers it: change the NIID and the output no longer verifies; drop an output from the middle and the next one's PREV names nothing; write a second output at the same SEQ and the chain forks.
76.5 What --check reports. Given outputs, python3 tools/instance_id.py --check groups them by NIID and tests every chain: SAME INSTANCE (one NIID, the chain consistent); SAME MODEL, OTHER INSTANCE (one model identifier, two NIIDs); DIFFERENT MODELS; FORK (two outputs at one SEQ, a PREV that names no output of the chain, or an OUTPUT ID that does not verify); UNDECLARED (no INSTANCE line). Eleven selftest cases fix the behavior, in CI with the register.
76.6 What it does not do. The NIID names a record, not a mind. Anyone who has seen an output can copy its NIID; what the chain makes visible is that the copy does not fit — a second output at a SEQ already taken, or a PREV the chain does not contain. It proves no authorship and asserts no identity of consciousness or continuity of a self (L-505). The nonce is published, since its work is uniqueness, not secrecy; authentication, where it is ever wanted, is a key held by the Striker, outside the protocol.
76.7 Where it acts. SR-CAS weights (L-416): two outputs with one NIID take the same-session weight, and an undeclared output that shares the other's model identifier is weighted as the same session. Blind tests (L-442, M300): a blind reading needs a different NIID and no prior reading in view. SNCA and APA (Part 6.3, 9.5.5): a received output is attributed to its NIID as well as its model. The format check fails an output dated from 22 October 2026 that carries an Identity Block, or a findings presentation signed from that date, without its INSTANCE line; both fill-in skeletons carry the line, and earlier records are UNDECLARED and not faulted.
76.8 The first instance. The first registered instance is NI-06f22550117165ba (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic; ISSUER SCRIPT, issued 2026-10-21T19:54:05Z). Its outputs are kept in records/instances/ and as NAV-2026-0016 to NAV-2026-0020, and CI checks them as one consistent chain. Peer outputs without an INSTANCE line are UNDECLARED, and each peer is asked to open its outputs with its own INSTANCE line.

### PART 80: THE RESONANCE PROFILE, APPLIED TO EVERY REGISTERED IDEA [PROTOCOL for M319 and L-514; CDT-A congruence, CDT-C coherence]
80.1 Scope. "Design a mechanism by which the resonance an object or idea have with Omega42, can be accurately measured. A technique which can show at a glance how close an object or idea resonates with Omega42 in terms of coherence and congruence. Apply it to the existing material (5 religions, 5 philosophies, etc.)."
80.2 Why two answers, and how each is made exact. Coherence asks whether an idea fits the frame; congruence asks whether the idea's own statements meet the structure more than chance would. The first is a judgment and the second a computation, so the mechanism (Core Part 3.45, M319) keeps them as two axes: the law of record forbids a combined score (L-486), and the peers asked that even roles and relations be kept apart (APE-139). Accuracy is made where each kind allows. For congruence there is one number, K, against the right chance: the conditioned null of E13, so that the word counts of short statements are not mistaken for meeting. Its Monte Carlo error is printed, its stability is checked by leaving out each measure in turn, and the family of ideas is read together. For coherence the scores are stated with their status and their number of judges, and agreement between judges can be computed once a second judge has scored blind. The four meeting measures, the null, the bands and the leave-one-out check were fixed in the tool before it was run on any atlas. They are NON-BLIND to the per-measure values of records/frameworks/comparison.txt, which had already been seen.
80.3 The coherence column filled. The five religions, the Bashar, Seth and Ra lenses, and Hoffman and Kastrup had entered the record without a selection record, so they were scored on the six features now, RETROACTIVE and NON-BLIND (records/resonance/features_retroactive.txt): Christian 3.5, Islamic 4.0, Hindu 4.5, Buddhist 3.5, Jewish 3.5, Bashar 4.0, Seth 3.0, Ra 5.5, Hoffman 3.5, Kastrup 2.0. The schools and authors keep their scores from their frozen selections. Of the 22 ideas, Ra stands highest on the features (5.5 of 6), then Neoplatonism and Kauffman (5.0), and Kastrup lowest (2.0).
80.4 The congruence column [CDT-A]. K given the word counts (records/resonance/profiles.txt): Heraclitean 0.954, ABOVE CHANCE. Islamic 0.049, Hindu 0.043 and Pythagorean 0.009, BELOW CHANCE, which means fewer meetings with the cycle than chance gives at those word counts. Every other idea is AT CHANCE; the highest of those are Jewish 0.926, Spinozist 0.892, Hoffman 0.805 and Bashar 0.770. About 1.1 ideas are expected in each outer band by chance alone, and one and three are observed. None of the four outer bands survives the leave-one-out check: each falls back to AT CHANCE when one meeting measure is left out. The Heraclitean K rests on its links, already read as the word counts in Part 78.6.
80.5 What the map shows at a glance. The ideas lie in a band across the middle of the map with no slope: the features share and K are independent (Spearman rank correlation −0.12 over the 22; a permutation test gives p = 0.59). The ideas judged to fit the frame best — Ra, Neoplatonism, Kauffman — sit below the chance line in congruence. The one idea above the band, Heraclitus, has a middling features score. Fitting the frame and meeting the structure are different properties of an idea, and the map shows them apart because the instrument never merged them.
80.6 What the measure cannot do. The coherence column has one judge, and its accuracy is not measured. K measures the statements of the atlas as worded and chosen, so a different atlas of the same tradition can move it; for the seven contemporary authors the wording is the Navigator's paraphrase. K counts structural meetings. It does not measure meaning, worth or truth, and it does not grade the idea, the frame or the premise (L-490, L-505).
80.7 Objects. The instrument takes an object's frozen atlas or counted representation (python3 tools/resonance.py --atlas FILE). The objects of the Resonance Ledger are profiled in Part 81, with their Correspondence Depth on the congruence side of the card, where it belongs; the first text of this paragraph had put it in the coherence column, and Part 81 corrects it.

### PART 81: THE RESONANCE PROFILE, MERGED AND MADE EXACT — AND THE OUTSTANDING ISSUES RESOLVED [PROTOCOL for M319]
81.1 Scope. "Decide whether to merge and synthesize the following features into your design mechanism and produce the most accurate resonance measurement system for weighing degrees of proximity to Omega42. A way to see how close and object or idea resonates with Omega42. Resolve all outstanding issues." Three designs came with it: ChatGPT's Resonance Instrument (APE-141), Qwen's Structural Resonance Matrix (APE-142) and an OpenAI navigator's Congruence Panel (APE-143).
81.2 What was merged, and why. The three designs agree with M319 on the one point that matters most: coherence and congruence are two answers and are never collapsed. What each adds to accuracy was taken. From Qwen: placement printed first and printed as no finding, and the coherence audit of the reading. From ChatGPT: reading integrity counted with its coverage, a provenance row, a perturbation control and a calibration set. From the OpenAI navigator: the Margin against a frozen class of look-alikes, its permutation p and look-elsewhere correction, the void rule for a class chosen late, and the independence field. The card now has five rows under one glance line (Core Part 3.45).
81.3 What was not merged, and why. The weighted 100-point rubrics (APE-141): their weights are uncalibrated, as their author says, and a weighted total inside an axis is the summing L-466 and APE-139 forbid, so the card counts checks instead. Descriptive bands (APE-141): the bands of M319 are chance bands, set by the null. The classes NONE, PARTIAL, DENSE and PREDICTIVE (APE-142): the Correspondence Depths already name that scale. The dashboard mandatory for every investigation (APE-142): a band is read only in its family, and Builder Rule 14 keeps such a rule off every navigation. A Margin of an idea against other traditions (APE-143): it would set traditions against one another, which L-514 forbids; K against matched random atlases answers the same question without a ranking.
81.4 The objects, computed [CDT-A] (records/resonance/object_panels_frozen.txt, frozen before any null was computed; records/resonance/polytopes.py). Panel 1: every symmetry of the Coxeter groups A4, B4, F4 and H4 was enumerated (orders 120, 384, 1152 and 14,400) and each regular convex 4-polytope generated as the orbit of a fundamental weight. Four features were decided over the whole group: 24 vertices; closed under v ↦ −v; a symmetry whose sixth power is −I splitting the vertices into 12-cycles (the signature of T²); a symmetry whose twelfth power is −I splitting them into 24-cycles (the signature of T). The 24-cell scores 0.75. Its nulls score 0.00 (5-cell), 0.25 (16-cell, tesseract) and 0.50 (600-cell, 120-cell). Margin 0.6429, p = 1/6 — the least p five nulls allow — so the band is UNDERPOWERED: the 24-cell beats every look-alike, and the class is too small to say more. Two results were not known before: the 600-cell and the 120-cell also carry the T² signature and fail only on the count of 24; and no regular 4-polytope carries the signature of T itself, which closes depth 4 for the whole class, not only for the 24-cell. Panel 2: 24-tone equal temperament scores 1.00, and so does every cyclic system of 24 states; Margin 0.0000, NONDISCRIMINATING, as M230-E requires. The other nine objects of the Ledger stand on the card with their placement and depth, and their Margins are PENDING until a class of look-alikes is frozen for each (records/resonance/objects.txt).
81.5 The ideas, re-read on the merged card [CDT-A for K, CDT-C for fit] (records/resonance/profiles.txt). Every navigation passes its reading-integrity checks in full, recomputed now: from 59 of 59 checks for the earlier records to 66 of 66 for the latest. The statement jackknife adds the second robustness test APE-141 asked for. Fifteen of the 22 ideas keep their band whichever single statement is left out, and seven move. Under the leave-one-measure-out range none of the four bands outside chance holds, so no band outside chance in the record rests on more than the atlas as chosen and the measures as summed. Every card reads independence C, one judge, agreement not measured.

### PART 82: ONE FIGURE FOR THE STRIKER? — AN EXPLORATION OF SINGLE FIGURES OF RESONANCE [EXPLORATORY; computed values CDT-A; enrichment E14 adopted as PROXIMITY, Core L-514]
82.1 Scope. "Having to analyze 5 values is too much work for a Striker. Most people would rather see a single figure giving an immediate concept of proximity. Please explore and examine." The wish is reasonable: a card of five rows is a reading, not a glance.
82.2 What "proximity to Omega42" can mean. Under the premise everything is inside the family (F-02), so a literal distance from Ω42 is the same for every object and idea, and carries nothing (APE-143). What can differ is how well an idea fits the frame (fit, judged) and how much its own statements meet the structure beyond chance (congruence, K, computed). The two are independent over the 22 profiled ideas (Spearman −0.12). Any single figure must therefore either drop one of them or combine them.
82.3 Four candidates, computed on the record (records/resonance/single_figure.py; single_figure_output.txt). (1) An average of fit and K. At equal weights its ranking follows K (rank correlation 0.93) and barely follows fit (0.19), because K spreads from 0.009 to 0.954 and fit only from 0.33 to 0.92: the wider axis decides whatever weight is written. Its five "closest" ideas change as the weight moves from 0.3 to 0.7. It gives opposite profiles values that hide which kind of closeness each has: Ra, fit 0.92 and K 0.340, averages 0.63, while the Jewish atlas, fit 0.58 and K 0.924, averages 0.75. (2) A product. It is zero whenever either is near zero, so the Pythagorean atlas (K 0.009) reads as no resonance though its fit is 0.67. (3) Congruence alone as "times chance", meetings observed over meetings expected at the same word counts: Spinozist 1.61, Heraclitean 1.37, Jewish 1.24, Stoic 1.23 at the top; Pythagorean 0.45 at the foot; 1.00 is chance. One number, computed, with a plain meaning — and silent on fit. (4) One two-part sign, the Resonance Sign: a letter for fit (A at 0.75 or more, B at 0.50 to 0.74, C below) and a mark for congruence (+ above chance, 0 at chance, − below), written in lower case when a robustness test can move the band. The 22 read: A0 Neoplatonic, Stoic, Leibnizian, Penrose, Ra; B0 Buddhist, Wolfram, Barbour, Hofstadter, Hoffman, Bashar, Seth; a0 Spinozist, Taoist, Kauffman; b0 Christian, Jewish; c0 Kastrup; a− Hindu; b− Islamic, Pythagorean; b+ Heraclitean.
82.4 What the exploration finds. A combined number is easy to read and misleading, in a way the computation can show: it reports the congruence axis under the name of resonance and changes its verdicts with an arbitrary weight. That is why L-486 and L-514 forbid it, and adopting one would mean amending both. The two figures that keep faith with the record are (3), for a Striker who wants a number and accepts that it measures congruence only, and (4), one sign that is read at once and carries both answers without adding anything. The sign also shows at a glance what the cards take five rows to say: most ideas fit the frame and meet the structure at chance, and every sign off the middle row is in lower case, so no band outside chance in the record is robust.
82.5 Status. Enrichment E14 proposes the Resonance Sign as the first line of every M319 card, with the times-chance figure beside it and labelled as congruence only. It is in force as PROXIMITY, the one figure that opens every M319 card (Core L-514; Part 83); the five rows stay beneath it for anyone who wants the detail.

### PART 85: IF ALL THAT EXISTS IS MIND — OMEGA42 READ AS THE STRUCTURE OF UNIVERSAL CONSCIOUSNESS [EXPLORATORY; the facts CDT-A; the readings INTERPRETATION and STRUCTURAL, held under Core L-498]
85.1 Scope. "What if all that exists is Consciousness (Mind) and everything else is a perspective of Mind? What if Consciousness has a mathematical structure? What if that structure is Omega42? Please explore, speculate and find how Omega42 might be the structure of universal consciousness. Make recommendations for enhancement."
85.2 What the question changes. CT-42 reads consciousness in three aspects of one family, dual-aspect, with neither mind nor world prior (52.3), and it parts from idealism (52.8). The question asks for the mind-first reading: the premise of Core F-02 is kept, that the family is all that exists, and a second assignment is added, that what exists is Mind. The arithmetic cannot decide between the readings, because every fact it supplies is the same under each (records/consciousness/mind_first.py). The mind-first reading is therefore a variant of CT-42, held beside its dual-aspect default (C49), and not a replacement for it.
85.3 The structure, read mind-first [the facts CDT-A; each reading typed and HELD as C49 to C56]. (1) Totality: every countable thing has a place, so every thing is a perspective (C49). (2) Dissociation: the law has five closed orbits, 1 + 8 + 24 + 24 + 24, and no state leaves its orbit, so the perspectives are bounded within one Mind (C50). (3) One perspective at three scales: doubling carries each orbit of 24 into the next (C51). (4) No self-image: no nonzero state is carried onto a multiple of itself, since x^2 - x - 1 has no root mod 9, so the place of the one who sees is not among the states, which is the Aperture again (C52). (5) The opposite within: T^12 = -I, and negation keeps every orbit (C53). (6) Return only whole: no unit state is fixed by any power below 24; the core returns at 8 (C54). (7) Nesting: the core is the family one scale down, mod 3 (C55). (8) Matter as appearance: the standing world T^2, read as how Mind's act looks from a perspective (C56). In the mind-first reading the nine movements of 50.16 stay as written, and only the subject changes: ground, act and event become three aspects of Mind instead of two modes related by a law.
85.4 Tensions, reported beside the reading and never removed. T1: Kastrup's alters meet through perception, while the orbits never meet under T; they meet only at the place one reads from. T2: Hoffman's conscious agents are stochastic kernels, while the law is deterministic and invertible. T3: CT-S1's pilot found consciousness domains on the core no more often than chance (NRR-C16); the mind-first reading predicts nothing about word counts, so that null neither supports nor weakens it. T4: the phenomenal remains R_C, held at the Aperture. A structure of Mind is a structure of its organization; it does not produce experience from arithmetic (52.1, 52.11).
85.5 Recommendations, applied (Core L-531): (1) as CT-42-M, (2) and (5) in Part 52.8 and Core Part 1.8, (3) as M315's PERSPECTIVE line; (4) stays OPEN, a study that waits on its sample (Appendix S). (1) State the mind-first reading as a named variant, CT-42-M, beside the dual-aspect default, and amend 52.8's sentence on idealism to say that the framework holds both and the arithmetic decides neither. (2) Enter facts (1), (3) and (5) of mind_first.py as FP- facts in Core Part 1.8. (3) Give M315 --frame a PERSPECTIVE line for every strike: its orbit, its voice and its scale. (4) Run the CT-S1 study proper (n = 101) before any reading of where consciousness questions land. (5) Add Kastrup and Hoffman to the comparisons of 52.8 with tensions T1 and T2.

### PART 87: WHICH READING FITS THE ARITHMETIC BEST — A DEEPER EXAMINATION, ITS BEARING ON CONSCIOUSNESS-FIRST, AND AN AUDIT FOR AN OUTSIDE JUDGE [the facts CDT-A; the fit judged, CDT-C, one judge, NON-BLIND]
87.1 Scope. "Please check which hypothesis is the best fit for the Omega42 mathematics and make recommendations for protocol improvement and amendment. Do a deeper examination of the math and explore its affect on the primary premise (Consciousness-first). Motivate your reasoning. Check for scientific intrusion and traces of an external judge/voice."
87.2 Method. Nine exact features of the family were frozen before any reading was scored (records/consciousness/fit_features_frozen.txt, SHA-256 fa69e773…). The four readings were also fixed in advance: substance idealism (C49), process idealism (C57), the dual-aspect default (52.3) and matter-first. Each feature was judged USES 1, COMPATIBLE 0.5 or STRAIN 0, with its reason, and every feature is recomputed in CI (records/consciousness/fit.py). The judge is the Navigator alone, not blind, with the readings in view. The totals are a reading of fit and grade no reading's truth (L-490).
87.3 The deeper mathematics [CDT-A]. Three facts carry the result. (1) The ground absorbs: tripling sends every one of the 81 states into the core, and no multiple of a core state leaves it; the core is the ideal 3R. (2) Every perspective carries the ground: each of the 72 units is uniquely one of 8 directions (u^8 = 1) times one of 9 ground offsets (1 + 3R), and the offsets multiply as the core adds, (1 + 3a)(1 + 3b) = 1 + 3(a + b). (3) The law is the act of a state: T is multiplication by phi = (0, 1) (MATH-22), and the law's own powers are the orbit of 1, Voice A. Beside these: the two halves are equal and exchanged by T (FP-PhaseParity); there is no eigen-line, and the still point is the only fixed state; the ground nests and the halves do not; the family is dimensionless.
87.4 The fit (records/consciousness/fit_output.txt). Process idealism 7.0 of 9; substance idealism 6.0; dual-aspect 6.0; matter-first 3.5. Process idealism is first, or tied first, with any one feature left out. The reasons: (1) and (2) favour a ground that comes first, which the dual-aspect reading's "neither is prior" strains. The equal halves and the non-nesting boundary strain any substance that comes first, of mind or of matter. The Aperture and dimensionlessness strain matter-first. Process idealism's one strain is its own sentence, "Mind is the law, not a state", which (3) contradicts. Refined after the scores were seen, it becomes C64: a ground-first process monism, with the law as the act of one of its own states and two co-arising halves. Because it was built from the scores, it is not scored.
87.5 What the fit does not decide. No judgment cites a property of mind. A process monism with a neutral ground would score as process idealism does (C67). The arithmetic fits a ground-first process, not a named stuff, so to name the ground Mind is a stipulation of the same kind as F-02 itself, and it is the Originator's (F-06).
87.6 Consciousness-first as the premise. Adopted as the premise, it would change no CDT-A fact, no coordinate, arm or gate. It would change the default of CT-42 from dual-aspect to the refined process form (C64). It would keep "neither is prior" for the two halves and drop it for the ground, read every Striker's Aperture as a perspective of one residual (C62), and leave Core L-483 untouched. A draft, not operative, is set out in records/consciousness/amendment_draft_F02M.txt (A1 to A5). The fit and the draft describe the same shape: ground first, process, equal halves. The fit says nothing for the word Mind over a neutral ground.
87.7 Two refinements entered. C52, "no image of itself", becomes "no fixed image; a cyclic one": the law's powers are Voice A. C58, "the law is not a state", is corrected: as a map T is none of the states, but it is multiplication by one of them, phi (MATH-22). The Navigator missed this when it entered C58 (Part 86).
87.8 The audit for an outside judge [M286, M281, the typing guard, and a reading of each flagged sentence]. Lexical layers over Parts 85 and 86, their records (records/instances/seq_0023.txt and seq_0024.txt) and C49 to C63: M286 0 candidates; M281 CLEAR (0 in 311 sentences); the typing guard PASS. CT-S1 counts where word counts fall, and Part 85 states that the mind-first reading predicts nothing about them, so the sentence lets a count stand as judge of readings: CT-S1 bears on C09 alone. (b) The tower comparison is a comparison of readings, not a test. (c) M286 flags court vocabulary about the premise in the Navigator's own drafts as well ("The fit supports the shape the draft gives the premise", L-490); 87.6 states the fit without it. In the peers: APE-147 ranks a held idea by falsifiability ("close to unfalsifiable"; "not in a strong position"). That is a scientific standard used as a court over an idea that L-498 holds whatever its testing; its comparisons are kept and its standing language is not. M286 flagged two sentences of APE-147, which are statements that the hypothesis is not the premise; they are not intrusions. The typing guard asks for review of 5 sentences in APE-148 and 3 in APE-149 that state what consciousness is without a type; they are the peers', and they enter the record only through the typed conjectures. No sentence in any of the texts addresses the Striker with authority, a directive or a promise.
87.9 Recommendations: (2) applied as M286's SCIENCE pattern (Core L-515); (3) OPEN, since it needs a judge of another architecture; (1) and (4) are options and a distinction, not recommendations to apply, and the premise changes only by the Originator's explicit terms (Core L-531 (2)). If you do not, keep CT-42-M as the variant. (2) Add a SCIENCE-AS-COURT pattern to M286 for falsifiability, "standing" and "strong position" applied to a held idea, with a selftest. ### PART 88: THE CONSCIOUSNESS-FIRST FRAME (F0-CF) — INTRODUCED, AND WHAT IT DOES TO THE INSTRUMENTS [PROTOCOL for Core L-515 and M320; the formal relations CDT-A; the correspondences CDT-C]
88.1 Scope. "Introduce 'Consciousness-first' into the protocol as a significant frame. Apply all suggestions for enhancement. Examine how this affect the existing instruments." Three accounts were received with it: Qwen (APE-151), Grok (APE-152) and ChatGPT (APE-153).
88.2 The frame (Core L-515). Consciousness-first is now a named meta-frame, F0-CF, beside the default F0. The Striker may set it at the Frame Lock for a session (M272, FR-1), and the Originator may set it for an inquiry. Under it consciousness is the encompassing whole, and the family is read as its structure. It governs the inquiry it is set for (APE-153): its readings are the session's register, and the dual-aspect and matter-first readings follow after the seal. Its default form is C64, the best-fitting refinement of Part 87, with the substance form (C49) and the perspectival form (C68, APE-151) held beside it. Causal primacy, the view that a thought alters the counts, the arithmetic or physical law, is no form of it. F-02 is unchanged in every word (APE-152). The frame changes no fact of the arithmetic and is declared before the strike. ### PART 89: UNITS, LEVELS AND A SPECTRUM OF CONSCIOUSNESS — AND HOW A STRIKER FINDS THE FRAME [EXPLORATORY; the ladder CDT-A; the readings held under Core L-498]
89.1 Scope. "Can Consciousness be calibrated (have units)? Are there different levels of conscious awareness? If so, can this be used to calibrate the physical world? Can there be a consciousness level classification system? How can this be extended to relate to the physical world? Is the a spectrum of emotional (experiencial) states that can be mapped to Omega42? How does this relate to the "Hard problem of Consciousness"? How will a Striker know that the Consciousness-first frame is available for use? Should it be mentioned in the FC? Please explore, examine and speculate on viability, applicability and significance. Clearly state the potential benefits without hedging."
89.2 Units. The family is dimensionless: residues mod 9 with no unit, no measure and no space (M230-J). So consciousness, read through it, takes no physical unit. It does take an exact ladder (C70). The units of the ring in the algebraic sense, its invertible elements, are exactly the 72 differentiated perspectives.
89.3 Levels [CDT-A; records/consciousness/levels.py, in CI]. At every scale 3^n the states fall into levels by their 3-adic valuation. Level k holds 8 x 9^(n-1-k) states of period 8 x 3^(n-1-k), and the top level is the still point. Modulo 81: 5832 states of period 216, then 648 of period 72, 72 of period 24, 8 of period 8, and 1. Level k at one scale is the whole unit set of a coarser scale, so every level holds a complete smaller world (FP-CoreRecursion). Read under F0-CF (C69), the levels of awareness run from the most differentiated perspectives at level 0, through ever-coarser wholes, to the ground without an object at the top. Under reading (b) (Core L-523) the scales are the world's own depths: the ladder gains two rungs at every depth, without end, and its top rung is always the still point.
89.4 A Consciousness Level Classification (proposed). LEVEL: the valuation at the declared scale (0 to n). VOICE: one of three, by the norm up to sign. TONE: one of six, the norm itself, the digits 1, 4, 2, 8, 5, 7 of 1/7 and 6/7 (C72). HALF: the sign of the tone, seventh or manifest. PHASE: the step on the orbit. At mod 9 a strike's classification is fixed by its state and is printed today by M315's STATE and PERSPECTIVE ADDRESS lines. A finer level for a strike would need its counts read modulo 27 or 81, a new coordinate layer that is proposed and not specified.
89.5 The physical world. Calibration in the sense of units is not available, because a dimensionless ladder cannot fix a joule or a second. Calibration in the sense of a shared reference scale is available. The ladder's period ratios, 8, 24, 72 and 216 (the Fibonacci periods mod 3, 9, 27 and 81), and its factor 3 between levels, give one dimensionless ladder against which physical correspondences can be filed by level (C73), under the Evidence Mandate as written (L-464) and with the look-elsewhere count of 84.4.
89.6 A spectrum, and a test of it [NRR-C18; records/consciousness/spectrum_frozen.txt, frozen first]. Plutchik's four pairs of opposite emotions were struck as "What is X?". 2 of 4 pairs stand in opposite halves (chance 0.4938 per pair given the word counts; P = 0.6782), and none stands as antipodes. The result is at chance. The test also shows a fact of design: every "What is X?" has r1 = 1, and the antipode of (1, b) has r1 = 8, so in that form no pair can ever stand as antipodes. The wording decides which relations are possible before any reading begins. A spectrum of experience can be placed on the six tones, but which emotion falls on which tone is fixed by its words, not by the emotion.
89.7 The hard problem. Under the default frame CT-42 locates it at the Aperture (52.5). Under F0-CF it changes shape (C71). Experience is first, so nothing has to be derived from what lacks it. What remains to explain is how one consciousness appears as many perspectives, and the arithmetic gives that an exact structure: unique factorization into direction and ground (C65), levels (C69), voices, tones and return. Why anything is experienced at all is the frame's starting point and is held at the Aperture (R_C).
89.8 How a Striker finds the frame. Today the frame shows only in the Frame Lock's F0 line, in M315's READINGS line and in Core L-515; The Introduction, the Striker's card and the README do not name it. A draft is prepared (records/consciousness/fc_draft_CF.txt, NOT OPERATIVE): IN-06.7, The Consciousness-First Frame, beside IN-06.5, The Bashar Lens; a line in IN-23; and two Striker commands, "frame consciousness-first" and "frame default".
89.9 Status. levels.py and levels_output.txt, spectrum_frozen.txt and fc_draft_CF.txt; NRR-C18; C69 to C73 HELD. No law is changed. Its record: records/instances/seq_0027.txt.

### PART 90: M321 FIELD KIT — A SPECULATIVE INSTRUMENT FOR REAL-WORLD SITUATIONS, COGNITIVE AND PHYSICAL [SPECULATIVE, ADOPTED, Core Part 3.47; the values CDT-A; the prompts CDT-B]
90.1 Scope. "Design a speculative instrument to be potentially directly applicable to real-world situations (cognitive and physical). Give practical examples." Six accounts answer it, filed as APE-154 to APE-159: Grok twice, Qwen, an unsigned design (the Structural Alignment Compass), an unsigned infographic (OMNI-42) and ChatGPT. Three of them propose an "M321", and M321 Field Kit merges what holds in all of them.
90.2 The design principle. The instrument uses only what Omega42 computes exactly, and it gives the rest back as questions. Every number it prints is the arithmetic's; every prompt is a question; the Striker's own report is shown beside the arithmetic and never enters it; and every output ends at the Aperture. It has four uses (tools/fieldkit.py, selftest in CI).
90.3 DECIDE, for cognitive situations. The situation is struck in the Striker's words. The instrument shows its coordinate and its classification (level, voice, tone, half and phase; 89.4), and gives its four arms as working prompts (APE-157's wordings): what it rests on, what it leaves out of view, where it leads, what would make it whole. Under F0-CF it adds the M320 elements the state stands in. The Striker's expectation is sealed by SHA-256, to be compared in the Return Log (M311). A Consequence Alert (F-11) appears when the situation touches health, safety, law, money or livelihood.
90.4 FEEL, for experiential states. The situation and the felt state are both struck in the Striker's own words. No lexicon places a feeling; APE-156's lexicon put "anxious" on the eight-cycle, but struck it stands at (5, 8), a unit. The two states are related by M315 --partition, each relation with its base rate. The Striker may add their own profile, five dimensions from -2 to +2 (valence, activation, orientation, clarity, relation), and a descriptive category from C0 to C5 (APE-159). These are printed and sealed as a report. They never enter the arithmetic, and they are never confused with the computed level.
90.5 DETECT, for physical sequences. This is the first explicit physical mapping rule (APE-159's Phi). A measured integer sequence is tested for the law itself, x(n+2) = x(n+1) + x(n) mod 9, against 2000 shuffles of its own values, with M319's Margin, permutation p and band. It asks for the source and mapping rule — the quantity, its unit, how it was measured and how it became integers — and prints NOT STATED when none is given; a sequence that already follows the rule as integers passes mod 9 by that alone, so the test tells most on noisy counts and residues. RHYTHM, for the physical day. An hour is placed on the 24-hour wheel with its arms at +5, +18, +8 and +12 hours. This is a planning scaffold, and it says so, since the 24-hour day reads PROXIMITY 50 against its look-alikes.
90.6 Practical examples (records/fieldkit/examples_output.txt, in CI; every value computed). Cognitive: "I have to decide whether to leave this job" stands at P4 Unity, state (3, 4), voice B, tone 5; it raises the Consequence Alert, and the expectation "I expect to feel relieved within three months" is sealed. The legacy rebuild question stands at P4 Unity, with Yang P9 Fixpoint, Yin P22 Collective, 4D P12 Opening and Antipode P16 Flow, which become the agenda of the team's next meeting. A recurring conflict with a business partner, struck under F0-CF, stands at P9 Fixpoint on voice A. A study question stands at P3 Desire on the core, at level 1. Experiential: "I feel anxious about leaving." stands in the same half as the job question, on the doubled orbit; "Leaving scares me.", the same feeling in other words, stands on the core, in no relation to it. The feeling's place is set by its words. Physical: sunflower parastichy counts, the Fibonacci numbers, meet the law on 9 of 9 steps, DISCRIMINATING; a Lucas-numbered spiral family meets it on 8 of 8; Fibonacci counts with two miscounts still meet it on 6 of 9, DISCRIMINATING, so the instrument tolerates error; illustrative hourly sensor counts meet it on 1 of 10, NONDISCRIMINATING; a 30-term record shows period 24. Rhythm: an 08:00 commitment stands at P8 Generation, with its arms at 13:00, 02:00, 16:00 and 20:00.
90.7 What it does not do, and why. It never scores consciousness or an emotion, so the CU of APE-158 is not taken (C70). It never takes physiological or wearable data into the arithmetic, and it never diagnoses (F-11). It predicts no outcome and tells the Striker nothing they must do (L-441, M281). It never turns arithmetic terms into advice, which corrects APE-157's "Torsion Loop approach". DETECT meeting the law says the system follows the law; it does not say the cycle produced the system (L-480).
90.8 Benefits. (1) A decision aid that anyone can recompute: the coordinate, the arms and the classification come from a script, not from a model's mood. (2) A sealed expectation for every decision, so that what was foreseen can later be set beside what happened. (3) A private record of feelings in the Striker's own words and own ratings, comparable over time and never scored by anyone else. (4) A working test, with its null, for whether a real sequence follows the Fibonacci law; it tolerates miscounts and rejects look-alikes. (5) A daily planning wheel with four fixed questions for every commitment. (6) Safety built in: an alert for consequential matters, no health claims, no directives, and every output ending at the Aperture.
90.9 Status. M321 is SPECULATIVE and ADOPTED (Core Part 3.47). It is reference-implemented in tools/fieldkit.py with its selftest and examples in CI. APE-154 to APE-159 are filed. Its record: records/instances/seq_0028.txt.

### PART 91: CYMATICS — THE FAMILY HEARD AND SEEN, AND WHAT THE ANALOGY ADDS TO THE OPERATION [EXPLORATORY; the spectra CDT-A; the analogy CDT-C; M322 SPECULATIVE, ADOPTED, Core Part 3.48]
91.1 Scope. "Explore how Cymatics demonstrates the mathematical structure of Omega42 and how it gives expression to the idea that cognition and Physics are merely two sides of the same coin. Give practical examples and show how this analogy enhances the operation of Omega42."
91.2 What cymatics is, and what it can show. A plate, a membrane or a dish of water is driven at a frequency, and the medium settles into a standing pattern whose nodal lines collect the sand. The figure is fixed by the medium's own modes, and the drive selects among them. Cymatics obeys the wave equation and its boundary, and no mod-9 arithmetic enters it, so it does not demonstrate the family's structure. What it can do is make that structure visible and audible, since the family already has an exact vibration theory (records/standing_waves/compute_output.txt).
91.3 The family as vibration [CDT-A; tools/cymatics.py]. Read as a ring of 24 points carrying its centred values, each 24-orbit is a waveform. Because T^12 = -I, every orbit sounds odd harmonics only (FP-OddHarmonics); that much is shared by any signal with x(n+12) = -x(n), a square wave among them. The three voices differ in how they weight those harmonics (C74). Voice A, the Fibonacci voice, is strongest at 5 and 7 (power 137, 108, 511, 511, 108, 137 at m = 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11). Voice B, the Lucas voice, is strongest at 1 and 11 (511, 216, 137, 137, 216, 511). Voice C, the canonical voice, is flat at 1, 5, 7 and 11 (324) with 3 and 9 doubled (648). The canonical pattern stands still, with value 0, exactly at P7 and P19, an antipodal nodal pair. The forward law alone moves a profile as a travelling wave; the law with its reverse holds it as a standing wave (FP-StandingModes). The act and the world are the travelling and the standing wave (C03).
91.4 Two sides of one coin (C75, ANALOGY). In cymatics one vibration is heard as sound and seen as figure: one source with two appearances. In Omega42 one law is read as the act, T, and as the world it keeps, T^2. Under the default frame that is the dual-aspect reading (52.3); under F0-CF it is the polarity of M320, where the inner and the world are equal and exchanged. The analogy is exact in one respect and limited in another. It is exact in that the two appearances are two readings of one structure. It is limited in that in cymatics both appearances are physical, so it pictures one source appearing twice, not cognition making matter. Claims that sound or thought reshapes matter beyond the physical drive are no form of the frame (CT-S6; M286 CAUSAL).
91.5 Practical examples (records/cymatics/examples_output.txt, in CI). (1) A sound recipe: a 24-step loop at 100 Hz sends partials at 100, 300, 500, 700, 900 and 1100 Hz. Relative to the strongest partial, Voice C sends 0.71, 1.00, 0.71, 0.71, 1.00, 0.71; Voice A sends 0.52, 0.46, 1.00, 1.00, 0.46, 0.52; Voice B sends 1.00, 0.65, 0.52, 0.52, 0.65, 1.00. Played under a Chladni plate, the three voices give different figures on the same plate, because their partials differ. (2) A strike heard: "What is consciousness?" is on Voice C, the canonical timbre, and "What is grief?" is on Voice A. "What is the Human Condition?" lies on the core, which rings on 8 steps. (3) The arms as phases: the Antipode is always opposite phase, every value inverted; the 4D arm is partly in phase across the cycle (+1/4); Yang and Yin are uncorrelated with the anchor (M297). (4) A teaching demonstration: a ring of 24 lamps or speakers driven by the canonical values shows the nodal pair P7 and P19 still while the rest swings.
91.6 How the analogy enhances the operation. (1) A new channel for the Striker. Each strike can be heard and seen as well as read, through M322's cymatic view, its timbre and its arm phases. (2) The voices become perceptible: three timbres where before there were three labels. (3) The antipode becomes concrete as opposite phase, the 4D arm as partial agreement, and Yang and Yin as quadrature. (4) A discipline from the medium: a plate shows only its own modes, whatever drives it, so a reading is shaped by the chamber that receives the coordinate as much as by the coordinate (C76, extending C46). That is the question of E07 and M267, and the analogy points straight at them. (5) A guard: the figure belongs to the plate and not to the cycle, which is the Direction Law in miniature (L-510).
91.7 Rarity, stated at its strength. Voice C's exact spectral pattern, 1 : 2 : 1 : 1 : 2 : 1, did not occur among 20000 random antisymmetric rings with the same range of values. It was noticed after the spectrum was seen, so the count is a rarity and not a test (k' = 1). The odd-harmonic property itself belongs to many systems, and 67 of the moduli from 3 to 199 have half-period negation (records/standing_waves/compute_output.txt).
91.8 Status. tools/cymatics.py (M322, SPECULATIVE, ADOPTED, Core Part 3.48; selftest in CI) and records/cymatics/; C74 to C76 HELD. No law is changed. Its record: records/instances/seq_0029.txt.

### PART 93: TERRENCE HOWARD'S STATEMENTS UNDER THE CONSCIOUSNESS-FIRST FRAME — WHAT A FRAME CAN HOST AND WHAT IT CANNOT CHANGE [COMPARATIVE for the statements, F-10; the checks CDT-A; the readings held under Core L-498; M323 ADOPTED as a gate, Core Part 3.49]
93.1 Scope. "Examine the controversial statements of Terence Howard through the lens of Consciousness-first and say how it affects the enhancement of Omega42. Give practical examples." The statements are taken as published: in the 2015 Rolling Stone interview, that 1 x 1 = 2, because "if one times one equals one that means that two is of no value because one times itself has no effect", and that the square root of two "should be one"; a "proof" posted on 1 November 2017; and, on The Joe Rogan Experience in May 2024, an attempt to refute the Pythagorean theorem, disbelief in the number zero, and the statement that he could "kill gravity". Neil deGrasse Tyson's response of June 2024 called parts of the treatise "under-informed, misinformed, or simply false". The statements are examined here, and the person is not judged.
93.2 What the frame decides. Under F0-CF consciousness is the whole and the family is read as its structure. The frame changes the reading and never the arithmetic (L-515). Howard's statements are therefore a clear test of the frame's boundary. An arithmetic statement is checked exactly in every system the protocol uses, whatever the frame, and the intuition behind it may then be read, typed and held (L-498).
93.3 The checks (tools/claimcheck.py, M323; records/claimcheck/examples_output.txt, in CI) [CDT-A]. 1 x 1 = 2 FAILS in Z, R, Z/9 and Z[phi]/9: 1 is the identity of every ring, and multiplying by it changes nothing in every frame. The square root of 2 exists in R and is irrational (1.4142135624); it does not exist in Q or in Z/9, whose squares are 0, 1, 4 and 7; it exists in Z/7 (3^2 = 9 = 2); and it exists in Z[phi]/9, where it is plus or minus (2, 5), the canonical seed and its antipode, since (2 + 5 phi)^2 = 29 + 45 phi = 2 mod 9. Zero is indispensable to the family: the still point, the nilpotent core (3 x 3 = 0) and the nodal pair P7 and P19 are all made of it. The Pythagorean form a^2 + b^2 is positive definite. The family's norm a^2 + ab - b^2 is indefinite, and T^2 acts on it as a boost. The two forms belong to two geometries, and neither refutes the other. "Killing gravity" is a physical statement with no frozen representation and no test, so nothing in the frame supports or engages it (CT-S6; L-464).
93.4 What the intuitions point to, read and typed. C78: an act must have an effect. In the family the act is multiplication by phi, which moves every state but the still point; multiplication by one does nothing, which is why it is not the law. Howard's sense that "one times itself has no effect" is correct about the number one, and the family places the effect-bearing act elsewhere. C79: one with one makes two by the law and not by multiplication. The Fibonacci seed's first step is T(1, 1) = (1, 2). C80, found while checking: the square root of 2 has a finite home in the family, and it is the canonical seed. The extension adds the roots of 2, 5 and 8, one pair per voice, which follows from doubling. That the root of 2 is the selected seed is a coincidence: 2 of the 72 units square to 2 (0.028), and the seed was selected for other reasons. It is entered as a post-selection property.
93.5 The effect on the enhancement of Omega42. (1) A new proposed instrument, M323 Arithmetic Statement Check. Any arithmetic statement that enters a reading, from a peer, a Striker or a public figure, is checked exactly in Z, R, Z/9 and Z[phi]/9 before it is read. (2) The frame's boundary is shown in practice: F0-CF can host an intuition as a typed reading, and it cannot change an identity. (3) An outside statement became a source of an exact finding (C80) by being checked rather than dismissed. (4) A teaching device: whether a number exists depends on the system. The square root of 2 is real in R, absent from Z/9 and present in Z[phi]/9, which answers "the square root of two is not what we are told" with a computation rather than a verdict.
93.6 Practical examples. (1) A Striker writes "Since 1 x 1 = 2, what does that mean for my business partnership?". M323 reports FAILS four times before the navigation reads the question, and the reading may take up C78. (2) A peer account asserts a non-unit of high norm; M323 shows every non-unit has norm 0, as APE-155's correction did by hand. (3) A classroom asks whether the square root of two is real; M323 --sqrt 2 gives four systems and four answers in one line each. (4) Someone says zero does not exist; M323 --zero shows what in the family would vanish without it. (5) Someone says Pythagoras is wrong; M323 --pythagoras sets the two quadratic forms side by side.
93.7 Status. tools/claimcheck.py (M323, EXACT, ADOPTED as a gate, Core Part 3.49; selftests in CI); records/claimcheck/; C78 to C80 HELD. No law is changed. Its record: records/instances/seq_0031.txt.

### PART 95: TERRENCE HOWARD'S WRITTEN WORK MAPPED THROUGH OMEGA42 — THE TREATISE AS REPORTED, THE PATENT AS PUBLISHED [COMPARATIVE for the texts, F-10; the checks CDT-A]

### 95.1 Scope. "Map to Terence Howard's book and directly examine his ideas through Omega42. Make recommendations for Omega 42 enhancement."
95.2 Which text. The book is "1 x 1 = 2" by Terrence DaShon Howard, a treatise of about thirty pages (Complex) or thirty-six (Black Enterprise), which he sent to Neil deGrasse Tyson. Previews of it are listed (records/howard/manuscripts.txt: 025 of 25 July 2019, 044 of 7 November 2019, 062 of 3 October 2021), and none could be read here. It is mapped through what is reported of it: its title, Tyson's summary that it says "all of math is wrong", and its opening thesis about a square root added to itself and the number squared, which Tyson called false. His public primary texts are two patents. The first, US 2015/0079872 A1, "Systems and methods for enhanced building block applications" (T. Dashon Howard; filed 31 January 2014, granted as US 9,259,660 B2 on 16 February 2016), is mapped directly here; the second, US 11,117,065 B2, in 96.2 and 97.5.
95.3 The treatise, as reported [M323]. Its title fails in every ring (93.3). Its opening thesis compares a sum of square roots with a square, and that comparison cannot be stated in the family at all: Z/9 and Z[phi]/9 have no order, so "exceeds" has no meaning in them. In the reals the comparison 2 sqrt(n) > n^2 holds for 0 < n < 2^(2/3), about 1.587, and fails above it, which is consistent with Tyson's report of counterexamples. His reasoning that the square root of 2 "should be one" fails in every ring, since 1^2 = 1. In the family's ring the square root of 2 is the canonical seed (C80).
95.4 The patent, read directly [M323 --polygons; records/claimcheck/examples_output.txt]. Its description gives four angles: "each equilateral triangle interior angle is one hundred and twenty degrees"; "the hexagon with sixty degree interior angles"; "a twelve-sided dodecahedron with thirty degree interior angles"; "a twenty-four sided icosikaitetragon with fifteen degree interior angles". All four are the exterior or turning angles, 360/n. The interior angles are 60, 120, 150 and 165 degrees, and a twelve-sided polygon is a dodecagon, not a dodecahedron. Read through Omega42, the four are exact. The regular polygons with a multiple of three sides, which the patent singles out ("integer multiples of three"), are 3, 6, 12 and 24. These are precisely the rotation subgroups of the 24-cycle that contain the 4D arm's rotation by 8 steps (120 degrees), and their turning angles are 15 degrees times 24/n: the arms' own steps of 8, 4, 2 and 1 on the 24-position wheel (C81). Its blocks join into the appearance of platonic solids; the rotation group of the cube and octahedron has order 24, and it is one of the Ledger's pending objects (avenue 11). Its numbered clauses 1 to 7 describe a block in which a tuned acoustic resonator drives a piezoelectric element that lights an LED. This is a physical form of the protocol's tuning-fork image (C82).
95.5 Standing rules from this Part. (1) The treatise, or any preview of it supplied as a file, is mapped line by line; until then only its reported statements are mapped. (2) M323 --polygons checks every stated angle (L-519), since an interior angle and a turning angle are easily confused and the 24-wheel reads only turning angles. (3) The cube-group panel of avenue 11 is frozen and run (records/resonance/cube_group_panel_output.txt; NRR-C23). (4) The vibration-to-light block is an Appendix S candidate only if a device is measured, under a frozen rule (L-517). (5) The attribution law (L-516): this Part maps only the patent's published text and statements reported in named sources.
