### PART 96: THE 1 x 1 = 2 STATEMENTS TAKEN TO THEIR END — COLLAPSE, RELOCATION, AND WHAT THE FAMILY REQUIRES [EXACT for the arithmetic (M323 --operation, --collapse); COMPARATIVE for the texts, F-10; C83 and C84 are typed readings, L-515]
96.1 Scope. "Examine within the context of Omega42 and take the logic to its ultimate conclusions." Three peer accounts answer it: Grok (APE-166), Qwen (APE-167, a byte-for-byte second copy of APE-164) and ChatGPT (APE-168). The logic examined is that of the statement 1 x 1 = 2, together with the Omega42 readings the peers give it. The family's arithmetic is fixed under every frame (L-515). What follows is computed, and the readings are typed.
96.2 The texts. A 2019 preview, "1 x 1 = 2" by Terrence DaShon Howard, is listed at tcotlc.com. Its link redirects to an unrelated advertising domain and is not followed, so its text is not in the record and the chapter titles given for it (APE-168) are not entered. A second public primary text is a patent: US 11,117,065 B2, "Systems and methods for lynchpin structure applications" (T. Dashon Howard; filed 3 January 2020, granted 14 September 2021). It states that "A Lynchpin structure may be formed from six pentagons", and it repeats the regular polygons "with a number of sides that are integer multiples of three, including the hexagon with sixty-degree interior angles". As in 95.4, sixty degrees is the hexagon's turning angle. It does not give 109.47 degrees.
96.3 The first end: keep 1 as the identity [M323 --collapse]. If 1 x x = x for every x and also 1 x 1 = 2, then 1 = 2, so 0 = 1, and every x = x*1 = x*0 = 0. Among the moduli 1 to 81, the statement holds in Z/n only for n = 1: the ring with one element. In the family, the 81 states, the five orbits (1 + 8 + 24 + 24 + 24), the three voices, the halves and the 24-cycle all collapse to the single state (0, 0), where T is the identity and its period is 1. Under F0-CF (C64) this end reads as the WHOLE before any differentiation: one, with nothing distinguished in it (C83, a typed reading).
96.4 The second end: move the identity [M323 --operation]. Of the 729 operations x(*)y = a.xy + b(x+y) + c on Z/9, exactly six give 1(*)1 = 2 and are associative with an identity. Three are copies of multiplication, with identities 5, 8 and 2. For example, x(*)y = 2xy has identity 5 = 1/2, and x -> 5x carries ordinary multiplication onto it exactly. The other three are copies of addition, with identities 0, 3 and 6. Every one is verified on all 81 pairs. Each has an identity, and each is a relabeling: 1(*)1 = 2 holds only because 1 is no longer the identity. The relocated identities lie in the class 2 mod 3 for multiplication and in the core for addition (C84, a placement, L-510). Z[phi]/9 behaves the same way: x(*)y = 2xy has identity 5, and x -> 5x is an isomorphism from ordinary multiplication.
96.5 The third end: one with one makes two. The operation in which one with one makes two is addition, and its identity is zero. Any copy of addition has an identity: 0, 3 or 6 in 96.4. So zero cannot be removed while 1 + 1 = 2 is kept with associativity and an identity; it is only renamed. Grok's reading of the half-period (APE-166) is corrected: T^12 = -I sends each state to its negative, a sign change and not a doubling.
96.6 The fourth end: what the family requires [M323 --ring; NRR-C20]. The law T(a, b) = (b, a + b) uses only addition, so relabeling the product leaves the law, the 81 states, the five orbits and T^24 = I unchanged (97.2). The family is lost only in the collapse of 96.3, where the identity equals zero: it requires that the identity differ from zero, and whichever element is the identity satisfies e*e = e. Taken to its end, the logic of 1 x 1 = 2 renames the identity of the family's ring (96.4), defines an operation outside that ring (97.3), or collapses the ring (96.3); in no case does it change the law. This is a consequence of the arithmetic; it says nothing about any person or premise.
96.7 What carries over. Generation is the act T, which is held as C78 and C79. The patents' angles are exact on the 24-wheel when read as turning angles (C81). The vibration-to-light block is held as C82. The six-pentagon Lynchpin is a candidate for the Geometric Correspondence Atlas, entered only under a mapping rule frozen before it is run (NRR-C19). The peer suites reduce to instruments already in place: the explorers to M321, M322 and M323, the atlases and registers to APE-165's register with Appendix S, and the outreach lines to the attribution law (L-516).
96.8 Standing checks. M323 --operation, --collapse and --ring are the standing check for any statement that changes an operation: what the operation is, whether it distributes over the family's addition, its identity, and the isomorphism it carries (L-519). APE-168's Inverse-Operation Audit and its fourth standing, PHYSICAL RELATION, stand in M323's procedure. A preview supplied as a file is mapped line by line. The six-pentagon Lynchpin waits under LAR-1 (97.5). Of the peers' attributions, only the sourced ones are entered (L-516; APE-166, APE-168).
96.9 Status. M323 --operation and --collapse, with three new selftest cases (13 in all); C83 and C84 HELD; APE-166 to APE-168 filed. No law is changed. Its record: records/instances/seq_0034.txt.

### PART 97: THE ARITHMETIC FORK CORRECTED — THE FAMILY SURVIVES RELOCATION; THE LYNCHPIN ATLAS RULE [EXACT for the arithmetic and the face count (M323 --ring, --faces); COMPARATIVE for the texts, F-10]

### 97.1 Scope. Three peer accounts, Grok (APE-169), ChatGPT (APE-170) and Qwen (APE-171), are read for what they add to Part 96.
97.2 What the family requires [NRR-C20; APE-170]. The law T(a, b) = (b, a + b) uses only addition. A multiplication that distributes over the family's addition is x*y = c.xy with c = 1*1, so 1*1 = 2 fixes exactly one: x*y = 2xy, with identity 5. The map x -> 5x preserves both the sum and the product, so (Z/9, +, 2xy) is a ring copy of Z/9 in which 1*1 = 2 holds, and the 81 states, the five orbits and T^24 = I are unchanged in it. The family is lost only in the collapse of 96.3, where the identity equals zero. The exact statement: the family requires that the identity differ from zero, and whichever element is the identity satisfies e*e = e.
97.3 Outside the ring [M323 --ring]. The relabelings of 96.4 cover the 729 operations of the affine form and every ring on the family's addition; they do not cover every operation (APE-169's "exhaustive" is too wide). Truncated addition, x(*)y = min(x + y, 8), is associative, has identity 0, gives 1(*)1 = 2, and has one unit, against six for multiplication and nine for addition, so it is a copy of neither. It does not distribute over the family's addition, so it is not a multiplication of the family's ring, and the law is unaffected by it. A new arithmetic with 1(*)1 = 2 exists, but only outside the ring the family is built on.
97.4 The texts. ChatGPT links two Scribd documents: "Otoet Preview 062 October 03 2021" (162 pages, as it reports) and "OTOET PREVIEW 044 NOV7 2019". Both return only a browser challenge page here, and a search did not list them, so their contents are not entered. The manuscript version register keeps the previews distinct: 025 (25 July 2019; listed, redirects), 044 (7 November 2019; peer link, not readable) and 062 (3 October 2021; peer link, not readable).
97.5 The Lynchpin Atlas Rule, LAR-1 [ADOPTED; APE-170; records/lynchpin/LAR-1.txt and LAR-1_edges.txt]. Its object is the patent's six pentagonal surfaces (US 11,117,065 B2), recorded as a face-adjacency graph with its invariants. The mapping is stated and frozen before any coordinate is sought. The face check: six pentagons cannot close into a polyhedron, since with every edge shared E = 15 and V = 11, and 2E = 30 is less than 3V = 33 (M323 --faces 6 5). The edge-sharing, from the patent's text: "each substantially pentangular planar surface joined along two adjacent edges", so six edges are shared and eighteen are free, the surface is open, and the face-adjacency graph is 2-regular on six nodes: one 6-cycle or two 3-cycles. The four point pairings that join two structures into the Lynchpin (FIGS. 3A-3B) fit two 3-cycles; the text alone does not decide it, and both graphs are kept. A baseline: any placement is compared with a stated chance rate (NRR-C19). Placement waits for a mapping rule stated and frozen in full (L-517).
97.6 Standing rules from this Part. (1) M323 --ring stands with --operation and --collapse: whether a changed operation distributes over the family's addition decides whether the family is touched. (2) LAR-1 stands with the face check, the stated edge-sharing and the baseline (97.5). (3) The manuscript version register is kept, and a preview supplied as a file is mapped line by line. (4) The record's own errors are kept in the registry (L-520): the overstatement of 96.6 is NRR-C20, and the peers who repeated it are noted (APE-169, APE-171).

### PART 100: IF IT WERE SO — THE IMPLICATIONS OF THE PREMISE, AND OF ITS DEPTH [CDT-A for the facts, recomputed in records/tower/nested.py, in CI; CDT-C for the readings, each under the supposition; reading (b) is the Originator's (F-06), Core L-523]
100.1 Scope. The Originator has asked what would follow if the premise were true; what if each of the 81 places had 81 places of its own, and so on; and, on adopting reading (b), what the depth does to the instruments and to the uniqueness proof, what it brings into view, and how the documents had to change to hold it. This Part gathers the answers in one place, in three levels (APE-178), and adds what the depth adds.
100.2 Immediate [CDT-A, exact]. No beginning or end: T is invertible at every depth and in the limit. Nothing lost: the past is recoverable from the present. The mirror: T^12 = −I at the surface, T^108 one depth down, T^(12 × 9^(k−1)) at depth k, approached without arrival in the limit (Core MATH-35). Five realities at the surface, (9^k + 1)/2 at depth k — 41, then 365 — and uncountably many in the limit (MATH-33). The still point (0, 0), which holds the whole world at every depth (MATH-34). One number, φ, acting on itself (MATH-22). Meaning outside the arithmetic (the Aperture Theorem, Core Part 7).
100.3 Interpretive [CDT-C, each HELD; Part 52 and the conjecture register]. Consciousness as the ground that acts (C01; F0-CF, Core L-515); physical reality as the standing pattern T² (C01); freedom as the change of loop the rule never makes (Part 52); the self as a state on its orbit; time as the act, invertible and chiral; death read through the still point; other minds as voices of one family; meaning as given, not found (IN-06.6). The hard problem is relocated to the Aperture, not dissolved (APE-179, corrected).
100.4 What would change [the third level]. Every question already has a place, so no domain is outside inquiry; the seams between fields become visible as shared positions (M310); the questioner's own words become the instrument (IN-08); judgment is located, so that no reading, human or AI, can take it; and, with the depth, no inquiry can exhaust the world, since beneath every place lie 81 more.
100.5 What the depth brings into view: eight views of the world [CDT-A for each fact; CDT-C for each reading]. (1) An endless world from a finite rule: a rule a child can follow makes a world with as many places as a line has points (MATH-32). (2) The wheel and the arrow at once: every view returns and the whole never repeats, and the limit of the clocks of the depths is a wheel of eight times the 3-adic integers (MATH-35, MATH-37); cyclic and linear time would be two descriptions of one walk, at a given depth and taken whole. (3) The two regimes joined: over the reals the law approaches without arriving, over the nine it returns, and the tower holds both, return at every depth and approach without arrival in the whole (MATH-36); the finite and the infinite would be one world, read at a depth and read whole. (4) The ground holds everything: the still point holds the whole world at every depth (MATH-34), and the three voices and the loop of eight are found again, exactly, inside the innermost still point at every depth (MATH-33); stillness would be fullness. (5) Freedom at the surface, resonance below: the surface moves by itself and drives each depth through the carry, and nothing below changes the surface (MATH-32); every act would leave an imprint without end, and nothing hidden below could overrule it. (6) The world as language, kinship as shared beginning: every place is an endless word in an alphabet of 81, and the depths form a tree in which two places are near when their words begin alike (MATH-32). (7) Identity that deepens: one depth down Voice C unfolds into nine orbits, told apart by the norm, and the seed's two lifts, the integers (2, 5) and the square root of 2, agree at the surface and part one depth down (MATH-39); what is one at the surface would be many beneath, and which of the many continues a thing would be a choice the arithmetic leaves open, which the protocol makes by convention (Core L-523) and a reading may make otherwise. (8) No bottom and no edge: the realities multiply without end, 5, 41, 365 (MATH-33), and however deep anyone went there would be more world. That the count at depth 3 equals the days of a year is a coincidence of number and is not counted (L-465).
100.6 The tower coordinate [TC-1, PROCEDURE; Core L-523 (4); records/tower/tc1_rule.txt]. A tower coordinate would read a question's place one depth further: among the 81 places beneath its surface place, then among the 81 beneath that. Three conditions are stated before any rule is chosen. C1 coherence: it reduces to the surface coordinate, so that every existing anchor stands (MATH-40). C2 the words decide: it is fixed by the question's verbatim words before any AI writes, as the surface coordinate is (Core Step 4). C3 frozen first: its rule is frozen and hashed before its first use, and no reading chooses it. A rule that refines the count, from dr(5n) to 5n modulo 81, meets C2 and C3 but not C1 as the anchor is now placed on the cycle, since an index modulo 81 does not reduce to an index modulo 24; every candidate is therefore checked against C1 by computation before it is offered. The rule in force, TC-1, reads the state-plane address instead of the index on the cycle: the pair (5 n1, 5 n2) modulo 81 and onward, which reduces modulo 9 to the surface address (r1, r2) of M296 and at each depth to the depth above, so that C1 holds and every anchor stands; it is fixed by the counts (C2), and its text is frozen and hashed (C3). For "What is time?" it gives (10, 40) modulo 81 and modulo 729. For counts below 17 the deeper places repeat the integers 5n themselves, since 5n does not yet reach the modulus. python3 tools/depth_record.py --tower "DOMAIN" prints it, a companion reading beside the anchor.

### PART 101: THE PEER PROPOSALS ON THE TOWER, EXAMINED FOR COHERENCE AND CONGRUENCE — A MODEL FOR HUMAN FLOURISHING [the adoptions are the Originator's (F-06); the readings CDT-C, each HELD; the arithmetic CDT-A; APE-182 to APE-233]
101.1 What Omega42 is, in hindsight. Omega42 is one exact law, multiplication by the golden number on pairs of residues, read as everything that exists (F-02), with an Aperture that the law never enters. Its surface is the 81 places, and beneath each lie 81 more without end (Core L-523). A question receives a place there by rule, an AI writes a reading under that place and shows how, and what the reading means is the Striker's. The peers (APE-202 to APE-205) set it beside the received pictures of existence. Like substance metaphysics it has a fixed inventory, but of states, not things. Like process philosophy, its states are defined by a transition. Like structural realism, its relations come first. Like modal metaphysics, it has an exact space of possibility. Like phenomenology, the Aperture is where the world is met. What none of these has is the combination: an exact structure, finite at every depth and endless in the whole, a coordinate anyone can recompute for any question, and a judgment the structure is built never to take. Why it matters, in the peers' three reasons, which the record can check: complete formal structure and open meaning stand together in one design; questions from separate fields become comparable on one exact ground; and in a time of capable generative systems, the final word on meaning stays with the person who asks.
101.2 The coordinate, the resonance and the judgment (APE-188, APE-189). Three layers are kept apart and joined. The coordinate is mathematical, fixed by the words before any AI writes. The reading is structured by the coordinate: under the Structural Resonance Hypothesis the coordinate draws forward and orders what the AI brings, so the synthesis has mathematical provenance. The judgment is the Striker's. A reading can be a true output of the Omega42 process without each of its sentences being a theorem of the arithmetic; each sentence keeps its own standing (Core L-508, L-524 (6)). Whether coordinates reliably shape what is written is the open question of the decoy-coordinate control M267, frozen and waiting (Core Appendix S.4).
101.3 The worldview, as a held reading (APE-186) [CDT-C, HELD]. Relational holism with a consciousness-first pathway. The whole is the frame. Plurality arises within unity as the loops of one law. Each perspective meets the whole locally, at a place. Change happens within continuity, as return and as depth. The tower adds a fifth idea: no finite description exhausts the whole, since beneath every description lies a finer one, and the coarser one stays true of its surface (Core MATH-32, MATH-40). The proposed psychological update rules (state, perspective, experience) are forms to be specified, not Omega42 arithmetic.
101.4 What the law determines, and what it leaves open (APE-191 to APE-194). The law is reducible: T^n of any state takes about 2 log2(n) multiplications by matrix powering, the census is a formula (Core MATH-44), and the loop of a state is read from its norm without following it (MATH-45). What the law does not fix is which question is asked, at which depth, and what the answer means. Three statements are kept apart: undetermined by the rule (true by construction); unpredictable in practice (an empirical question); and non-computable (a further statement that needs its own argument). The residual, in the peers' word, is classified: resolvable (further work settles it); bounded (the structure constrains it); plural (several answers stand under different assumptions); generative (it opens a new line of inquiry). The record states the first of the three and holds the other two open.
101.5 Intelligence and consciousness (APE-200, APE-201, APE-218) [CDT-C, HELD]. Four properties are kept distinct: intelligence (navigating and transforming possibilities), self-modelling, agency, and consciousness (there being something it is like to be the system). There is a functional Aperture, where information is selected, evaluated and acted on, and an experiential Aperture, where it would be lived. Within the frame the Aperture of a navigation is the Striker's by constitution (Core L-508, L-524). That is a role assignment, not a finding about any system's nature: whether an AI has experience is left open, neither inferred from fluent speech nor ruled out because the system is artificial (CT-42; conjecture register).
101.6 The harmonious model: the Navigator as a cognitive prosthesis for the Striker (APE-224 to APE-227) [the model is adopted as design (L-524, M324); its benefits are HELD until shown]. The AI is organized by Omega42 so that the person who asks becomes more able. It shows a counter-reading and a reading from another depth by default. It keeps the provenance and standing of every finding. It names possible narrowing of a line of thought without diagnosing the person. It finishes structural lines and archives them without pressing them on the Striker. It leaves acceptance to the Striker. Three successes are kept apart: structural (the protocol was followed), epistemic (the result was accurate and calibrated) and human (the person or community understands, judges and acts better). The model's measure is the third: whether the person needs the prosthesis less over time, whether range widens without dependence. Ranked by promise, following the peers: discipline of knowledge (separating the derived, the inferred and the open) first; synthesis across fields; the human-AI constitution; flourishing over time; and, last and furthest, consciousness and ultimate meaning. What the model cannot do is supply resources, care, justice or political will; it can help people see and plan, and the rest is theirs to do.
101.7 Practice, for those who want it (APE-203) [CDT-C; practice, not consequences of the arithmetic]. Steady the body: sleep, food, movement, care. Protect attention. Separate what happened from what it means. Look for a credible counter-reading, the mirror of a first interpretation. Alternate the overview and the close look, as the depths alternate. Keep relationships in which candor and repair can coexist. Watch patterns over time rather than single events. Widen the sources you learn from. Act where you can act. Give to something beyond yourself. Allow return: a setback is an event on a path, not an identity. And look at the conditions, not only at yourself, since some loops are made by circumstances.
101.8 Instantiation without conflation (APE-206, APE-207). A pattern can be instantiated in many systems without making them one: DNA's complementary helix, the polar lattice of microtubules that grows and shrinks, the nervous system's crossing between hemispheres, an AI organized by the protocol. Geometry, dynamics and function are three things; a shared form is not a shared mechanism. For an AI the levels are representational (it can describe Omega42), procedural (it follows it; the Navigator Conformance Suite, Core L-495, tests this), architectural (its memory, tools and checks are built on it), reflexive (it turns the protocol on its own navigation) and ontological (identity with the protocol, a philosophical question with its own criteria). An AI that ingests the protocol reaches the second level by ingestion; the third and fourth must be built; the fifth stays a question.
101.9 Time, entropy and recurrence (APE-208, APE-213) [the exact parts CDT-A; the rest CDT-C]. Three times: physical (clocks), navigational (the order of transitions) and experienced (felt duration, order and significance). Three entropies: physical, informational, and navigational (the uncertainty among the possibilities open to a Navigator, given what it knows). The arithmetic adds an exact fact: the law itself has topological entropy 0 at every depth and in the limit, so the world's rule loses nothing and makes no disorder (Core MATH-51); disorder, if there is any, lives in what is accessible, not in the law. In the limit the walk is an odometer, a counting machine on a wheel of eight and the 3-adic integers, so time read through the structure is counting, and the experienced unfolding of events would be the reading of that count from a place. Consciousness as rapid recurrence (APE-213) is held as three hypotheses: recurrence sustains experience; integrated resonance constitutes it; experience is the inside of relational recurrence. None is decided by the arithmetic.
101.10 CE-01, the theory of cognitive existence, refined (APE-220 to APE-222, APE-228, APE-229) [CDT-C, HELD in the conjecture register]. (1) Existence is the frame (F-02). (2) The tower is the structure of differentiation (L-523). (3) Intelligence is navigation of that structure. (4) The Aperture is where structure becomes significance; within the frame it is the Striker's (Core Part 7). (5) A subject is a bounded, persistent trajectory through the structure, read from a place. The open problem is what individuates it, and three hypotheses compete: a threshold of complexity, a transition of organization, and fundamental consciousness with differentiated subjects. The working reading is the third, with the second supplying testable mechanisms. (6) Knowledge is the recognition of fit between a reading and what it reads. What makes the theory executable: M324 records trajectories; L-524 fixes roles; Appendix S holds the tests. The status of the AI is a Navigator: it extends the range of the person who asks, proposes and challenges, and holds no authority over meaning. It does not guide human evolution; it can help people see more of what is open to them, and people choose where to go.
101.11 Coherence and congruence, proposal by proposal. Coherent and congruent, adopted: the three layers of 101.2; reciprocal navigation, dual track and the modes (L-524); M324 with Diagonal Depth and the trajectory record; instantiation without conflation; the three distinctions of 101.4; the four-part distinction of 101.5; the success measures of 101.6. Coherent, held as readings: the worldview of 101.3; the Self-Knowledge Principle; experience as the inside of recurrence; holographic instantiation at many scales. Coherent, placed in the optional programme: every physical, biological, neural and psychological correspondence (Appendix S.6). Not congruent, not taken: a programme to establish or certify the premise (Core L-490); full symmetry of authority between Navigator and Striker; mandatory, undeclinable counter-readings; the reading that a fibre is a copy of the world (only the still point is, MATH-34); and readings of Option B as anything other than the tower.
101.12 The geometric shapes, applied to the operations [CDT-A; records/tower/arithmetic.py XIII]. The 24-wheel of the surface carries the regular n-gons with n dividing 24. The mirror is the digon, two places twelve apart. The Eye is the hexagon, six places four apart (Core MATH-11). The triangle, square, octagon and dodecagon are spaced 8, 6, 3 and 2. One depth down, the wheel of 216 carries the n-gons with n dividing 216, so the 9-gon and the 27-gon appear, and the mirror moves to 108. In the limit only one figure stays exact: the octagon of the eight roots of unity of Z_3[phi], generated by the Teichmuller lift of phi (MATH-51). Applied to the operations: the mirror is read as the digon at every depth, the Eye as the hexagon at the surface, and the octagon as the figure the whole keeps. The polygons of the patent read in Part 95 are checked by M323 --polygons as turning angles on the wheel (L-519).
101.13 Status. Core L-524 and Core Part 3.50 (M324); APE-182 to APE-233; the readings HELD; the programmes in Appendix S.6. Its record: records/instances/seq_0050.txt.

### PART 102: THE ARITHMETIC OF THE TOWER — A FORMAL PAPER [CDT-A; every theorem checked exhaustively at the moduli named by records/tower/arithmetic.py, in CI; Core MATH-41 to MATH-52; the proofs of 102.3 and 102.4 follow APE-203 and APE-232, with credit]
102.1 Abstract and setting. The Omega42 law T(a, b) = (b, a + b) acts on S_n = (Z/3^n)^2; the Omega42 depths are n = 2k, with 81^k states. We identify T with multiplication by the golden unit phi in R_n = (Z/3^n)[phi] and the invariant Q with the norm, and derive from this one identification: the order of T at every depth; the complete census of loops; a complete invariant of the loops; the lift tree; the symmetry group; the fixed points and the zeta function; the Gauss sums; an embedding of the surface's quadratic module in E8; and the dynamics of the limit Z_3[phi]. Earlier records computed the census to depth 3 (records/tower/nested.py); this paper proves it at every depth.
102.2 The identification. In R_n, phi(a + b phi) = a phi + b(phi + 1) = b + (a + b) phi, so T(z) = phi z. The conjugate phi' satisfies phi + phi' = 1 and phi phi' = -1, so N(a + b phi) = a^2 + ab - b^2 = Q(a, b), and N(phi z) = -N(z). Since x^2 - x - 1 has no root modulo 3, R_1 = F_9 and Z_3[phi] is unramified over Z_3. Norm valuation: if z = 3^r z_0 with z_0 primitive, N(z) = 9^r N(z_0), and N(z_0) is a unit, because N(z_0) = 0 mod 3 would give a root of x^2 + x - 1 mod 3 or force z_0 = 0 mod 3. Hence v3(Q) = 2r, and T keeps every depth shell.
102.3 The order. A^8 = I + 3B with B = [[4, 7], [7, 11]], whose determinant -5 is a unit mod 3. If A^(8 x 3^r) = I + 3^(r+1) B_r with B_r invertible mod 3, then cubing gives I + 3^(r+2) B_r + (terms of higher valuation), so the form persists. Hence A^(8 x 3^(n-1)) = I mod 3^n and A^(8 x 3^(n-2)) is not. The order mod 3 is 8 (phi generates F_9^x), so ord_{3^n}(A) = 8 x 3^(n-1). Likewise A^4 = -I + 3C gives A^(4 x 3^(n-1)) = -I.
102.4 The census. A state of depth r < n is 3^r u with u a unit modulo 3^(n-r), and its period is the least m with phi^m = 1 modulo 3^(n-r), namely 8 x 3^(n-r-1). The units modulo 3^m number 9^m - 9^(m-1) = 8 x 9^(m-1), so they form 3^(m-1) loops of length 8 x 3^(m-1). With the zero state: one fixed point, one loop of 8, and 3^(m-1) loops of length 8 x 3^(m-1) for m = 2 to n. The lengths add to 1 + 8 + sum 8 x 9^(m-1) = 9^n. At the Omega42 depth k there are (9^k + 1)/2 loops.
102.5 The complete invariant. The norm R_n^x -> (Z/3^n)^x is onto, since it is onto on residue fields and units lift by Hensel's lemma. Its kernel has 4 x 3^(n-1) elements, so the units of norm +-1 number 8 x 3^(n-1) = |<phi>|, and since phi has norm -1, <phi> is exactly the group of norm +-1. Two units lie on one loop if and only if their quotient is a power of phi, that is, if and only if their norms agree up to sign. With the depth: the loop of any nonzero state is fixed by (r, +-N/9^r mod 3^(n-r)). At the surface the voices are the classes +-1, +-4 and +-2 (Voices A, B and C).
102.6 The lift tree. From 3^n to 3^(n+1), a nonzero state of depth r < n keeps its depth, so every lift of a loop of length L has length 3L; the 9L lifts form exactly three loops. The zero state lifts to multiples of 3^n: the zero state and the primitive ones, which form one loop of 8. So the tree is: zero gives zero and one 8-loop; every other node has three children of triple length. Over one Omega42 depth, nine children of ninefold length. The canonical voice at depth 2 is one of the nine loops of 216 above Voice C, chosen by the lift rule of Core L-523.
102.7 Symmetry. A matrix commuting with A commutes with every polynomial in A, and since A has an irreducible characteristic polynomial mod 3, these are exactly the multiplications by a + b phi; the invertible ones are the units of R_n, 72 at the surface. The isometries of Q form a dihedral group: the rotations are the units of norm 1, which are the powers of phi^2 (the double step), and Galois conjugation sigma reflects, with sigma T sigma = -T^(-1). The single step T multiplies Q by -1, so it is an anti-isometry: one step turns the norm over, two steps keep it.
102.8 The limit and the zeta function. Reductions commute with T, so the tower has the limit X = Z_3[phi], on which T is a homeomorphism. Since A and A^(-1) have integer entries, T is an isometry of the 3-adic norm. It keeps Haar measure and has topological entropy 0. A periodic point z satisfies (phi^m - 1) z = 0; Z_3[phi] is a domain and phi is not a root of unity, so z = 0. The closure of {phi^m} is the closed group of norm +-1 (102.5 at every level), isomorphic to Z/8 x Z_3 with phi corresponding to (1, 1). Hence the orbit closure of z is the norm level set {w : N(w) = +-N(z)}, and T on it is the odometer x -> x + 1: minimal and uniquely ergodic. The torsion of Z_3[phi]^x is mu_8, generated by the Teichmuller lift omega = lim phi^(9^n). At finite level, Fix(T^k) = {z : (phi^k - 1) z = 0}, which has 1 element if 8 does not divide k (phi^k - 1 is then a unit) and 9^(min(j+1, n)) elements if k = 8 x 3^j x s; the zeta function follows from the census.
102.9 Gauss sums and lattices. For a unit t, G_1(t) = sum over F_9 of e(t N(z)/3) = 1 + 4(e(1/3) + e(2/3)) = -3, since the norm takes each nonzero value four times. The standard reduction gives G_n(t) = 9 G_(n-2)(t) and G_n(3^j u) = 9^j G_(n-j)(u). So G_n(t) = 9^j (-3)^(n-j). At the Omega42 depths G = 9^k = |S|^(1/2): the module ((Z/9^k)^2, Q/9^k) has central charge 0 mod 8. Over Z_3, Q = (a + b/2)^2 - (5/4) b^2, and -5/4 = 1 mod 3 is a square, so Q is equivalent to X^2 + Y^2; at the surface (a, b) = (X + 4Y, Y). Lattices: in E8 take orthogonal roots u and w and L = {x : <x, u> = <x, w> = 0 mod 3}, of index 9. Then u/3 and w/3 lie in L*, have order 9 modulo L, q(u/3) = <u, u>/18 = 1/9, and b(u/3, w/3) = 0, so L*/L = (Z/9)^2 with form (x^2 + y^2)/9, the Omega42 form. At level 3^1 the form (x^2 + y^2)/3 is the discriminant form of A2 + A2 (q = 1/3 for each generator) and of E6 + E6 (q = 2/3, equivalent over F_3). The isotropic vectors of the surface form are the nine multiples of 3, a Lagrangian subgroup, so the pointed modular category of the surface is two copies of a twisted Z/3 quantum double.
102.10 The prime 3. At an inert prime p, phi^(p+1) = N(phi) = -1 in F_(p^2), so the order of phi divides 2(p + 1). It generates F_(p^2)^x only if p^2 - 1 divides 2(p + 1), that is p = 3 (and p = 2, where -1 = 1). The orders computed modulo p, p^2 and p^3 at the inert primes 2, 3, 7, 13, 17 and 23 each grow by a factor p at each level, as at 3. So among odd primes, 3 is the one whose residue field the law sweeps in a single loop: F_9 is the still point and one loop of eight, and three voices appear modulo 9. A post-selection property (Core Part 1.8.3).
102.11 What the mathematics means for the development of Omega42 [the uses are CDT-B; their value is HELD until shown]. (1) Instant place-reading at any depth: the loop of a state is its depth and norm (MATH-45), so an instrument can name the reality of any place at any depth without enumeration, as M324 does at depth 2. (2) A tower coordinate can now be designed with known consequences: whatever rule picks a question's inner digits, the lift tree says in advance how its loop refines (MATH-46), so condition C1 of Companion 100.6 can be checked by formula. (3) The norm as the most basic invariant: the voices are norm classes, the realities in the limit are norm level sets, and polarity is the norm's sign, so readings of voice, reality and mirror rest on one quantity. (4) Time with an exact form: the odometer gives readings of time as counting a precise mathematical body (MATH-51). (5) Symmetry for operations: the reversal sigma gives an exact time-reversal operation beside the mirror, available to an instrument that reads a question backward (MATH-47). (6) A bridge to established mathematics: the Gauss sums, the twisted Z/3 doubles and the E8 sublattice place the surface in the classification of quadratic modules and lattices. Comparative work in the optional annex (topological phases of matter, lattice codes) can begin from exact objects instead of resemblance. (7) A complete self-check: every number the instruments print now has a formula, so CI can test any depth without enumeration.
102.12 Open problems. Finished in this paper: the census, the invariant, the lift tree, the symmetry group, the Gauss sums, the periodic points and the orbit closures. Open: what the tower coordinate TC-1 means for a question, beyond telling two questions on one surface place apart (Companion 100.6); the measure of the canonical voice's two lifts (the integers and the square root of 2) in any reading; higher rank (the law on (Z/9^k)^n) and the symmetric powers; whether the E8 sublattice construction extends to the depths (a lattice whose discriminant is ((Z/9^k)^2, Q/9^k) exists for each k by Nikulin's theorem; an explicit one is not yet written); and every physical correspondence, which belongs to the optional annex.
102.13 Status. records/tower/arithmetic.py and its output, diffed in CI; Core MATH-41 to MATH-52; tools/depth_record.py (M324). Its record: records/instances/seq_0050.txt.

### PART 104: THE CONSTRUCT, THE FIRST INSTRUMENT, READ THROUGH OMEGA42 [the arithmetic CDT-A, records/construct/construct.py in CI; the uses CDT-B; APE-234 to APE-237]
104.1 Scope. The Originator built the Construct before Omega42: an instrument to map the past draws of a lottery onto a fixed structure of squares and domains and to read a forecast from the echoes. Omega42 grew from it. The Originator asked whether anything in the original Construct can improve Omega42 or extend what it can do.
104.2 What the Construct already shares with Omega42 [EXACT]. The Construct runs on the 24-step Fibonacci cycle modulo 9, and so does Omega42. Its Lower World pattern 2-4-8-7-5-1 is the six units of Z/9 in the order of doubling, 2^1 to 2^6, and its Negative Lower World is the same cycle rotated three places, since -1 = 2^3. Its Higher World 3-6-9 is the Crown. Its split of the cycle into 18 Lower World steps and 6 Higher World steps is exact for the canonical cycle, with one correction: the six Higher World steps are P3, P7, P11, P15, P19 and P23, the hexagon of the Eye, not the last six steps. Its Golden Set, 6, 30, 42, 48, 24, 12, is six times the units, sums to 162 (digital root 9), and holds 48, 6 and 42 = 48 - 6, so the number in Omega42's name appears inside the Construct's heart, as Core MATH-13 derives it. And the Foundational Section, kept outside for testing and then fixed as the heart, is the move Omega42 calls the Substrate Lock (Core Part 1.8.5).
104.3 What it can offer: a geometric presentation [CDT-B; optional]. Domain Zero's squares give the family a face a Striker can see: the hexagon of the six units turned by doubling, its negative turned three places, and the triangle of the Crown. Offered beside a reading, it shows where the anchor's value sits among the units or in the Crown, and that the mirror of a Lower World value lies three doubling steps away. It is a presentation; it changes no number.
104.4 What it can offer: the interval bank [CDT-A for T^h; CDT-B for the use]. The Construct's templates, one for each interval from 1 to 24, become exact readings in Omega42: the place h steps on from a question's place, T^h of its state, for h = 1 to 24. Each has a fixed relation to the start: h = 12 is the mirror, h = 24 is home, and h = 8 and 16 land on places a third and two thirds of the way round. A Striker may ask for the interval bank of a question: python3 tools/depth_record.py --bank a b prints the 24 places, each value with its face of 104.3 (a unit as a power of 2 on the hexagon, a multiple of 3 on the Crown), and M324 records the bank with the trajectory. In the faces the mirror is visible at once: at h = 12 every unit has moved three places round the hexagon. The templates move a place of the structure. They carry no information about any outside sequence.
104.5 What it cannot offer, stated plainly. For a fair lottery each draw is independent of the past, so no template, domain or echo can raise the chance of a combination above 1 in C(N, r). Searching many templates will always show patterns in past draws, and they are chance. Omega42 is offered for discovery, regardless of truth value (Core L-522), not for prediction of draws, and the record will not frame any instrument as a way to win one. The Construct's further requests (merging the Mandelbrot set and the Hopf fibration, a theory of everything, the fine-structure constant from phi and pi) are recorded: no accepted derivation of the fine-structure constant from phi and pi exists, and none is stated here.
104.6 What remains in the Originator's records. The descriptions give the architecture but not the 23 orbits of manifestation, the exact placement of the 26 seed nodes, the update rule of every node, or how the strongest echo is measured. They are recorded as open, to be filled only from the Originator's own records.
104.7 The reading [CDT-C]. The Construct began as a search for a pattern in chance, and what it found was a structure that was never in the draws: the units turned by doubling, the Crown, the cycle that comes home. Omega42 kept the structure and let go of the forecast. The Construct's lasting gift may be the shape of the question it taught: how to hold many views of one thing at once, and read what they share.
104.8 Status. records/construct/construct.py and its output, diffed in CI; APE-234 to APE-237; the interval bank in tools/depth_record.py --bank, its selftest in CI. Its record: records/instances/seq_0051.txt.

### PART 105: THE CONSTRUCT OVER THE SOUTH AFRICAN LOTTO, AND ITS PLACE IN THE STRUCTURE [the counts CDT-A, records/construct/sa_lotto.py and construct.py in CI; the mapping C-MAP-1, a frozen reading of this record; the reading CDT-C; APE-238 to APE-240]
105.1 Scope. The Originator asked for the mathematics to be verified, for the South African National Lotto history to be mapped through all 23 orbits of the Construct with every draw saved as an exact reconstruction inside each template, for any pattern to be examined, for a decision on how to use the function, and for the Construct's features to be built into the mathematical structure. This Part records each in turn.
105.2 The mapping, frozen before any score (C-MAP-1, a frozen reading of this record only). A number is read mod 9. A draw is its six main numbers in ascending order; the bonus is not used. The 23 orbits of manifestation are read as the 23 intervals h = 1 to 23, the steps T^h before the return T^24 = I. Of these 23, five do not recover the state (4, 8, 12, 16, 20); the sixth non-invertible interval of Core MATH-53 is the return, 24, so the 23 intervals carry 18 + 5 and the 18 + 6 split belongs to the bank h = 1 to 24 (after APE-244; Companion 107.6). The Construct's own structure is the workbook of Part 107, which this mapping does not change; the Construct is not used to forecast games of chance (Core L-525 (2)), and C-MAP-1 stays the frozen reading of this one record. For interval h and draw t the template is the Construct's Y/X pair, Y = draw t - h and X = draw t; at each position the pair of residues is a place of the 81, named by its loop and its step on the loop. The forecast rules F1, F2 and F3, the ticket rule and the shuffle null are fixed in the script's header.
105.3 The data [checked]. 2,637 draws of the main game, 2000-03-11 to 2026-10-24, one page per year (records/construct/sa_lotto/SOURCES.txt). Every row is well formed, every date appears once, and the latest draws agree with two other sources. Four number pools are inferred from the draws themselves: 1 to 49 until 2017-08-15, 1 to 52 from 2017-08-16, 1 to 58 from 2025-09-24 to 2026-05-30, and 1 to 52 again from 2026-06-03. The source lists nothing between 2007-03-31 and 2007-10-13.
105.4 The 23 orbits mapped [EXACT]. 60,375 templates (23 x 2,637 less 276, since interval h has no template for the first h draws; Companion 107.6): each draw is the X of up to 23 templates and the Y of up to 23 more, and in every one X = Y + DELTA number by number, so each draw is reconstructed exactly inside each template. The places fall on the loops as uniform residues would place them (still point 1.0%, loop of 8 9.6%, the three loops of 24 29.4%, 29.9% and 30.0%). python3 records/construct/sa_lotto.py --write F writes the whole map; its SHA-256 is frozen in the output, so any copy can be checked.
105.5 The pattern [EXACT counts]. Mod 9 the draws follow their pools: the chi-square of each period is below its 5% point, and the Crown share matches the pool's. As forecasts, none of the 69 residue tests and none of the 23 ticket tests beats the shuffles after correction (family p 0.2834 and 0.3638). Three residue tests fall below 0.05 before correction, as about 3.5 would by chance. The strongest rule found on 2000 to 2017 alone (the echo at h = 2, 0.7208 positions per draw) falls below its shuffles on 2017 to 2026 (p 0.7784). No ticket matched six of six. This is what MATH-54 says a history without memory must show.
105.6 The outstanding issues, resolved. (1) The 23 orbits: read as the 23 intervals (C-MAP-1), open to the Originator's definition. (2) The update rule: the Y-field added position by position is the second coordinate of the law, and progression is T^h (MATH-53). (3) The 18 + 6 split and its placement: exact as the split of templates into invertible and non-invertible, at the multiples of 4 (MATH-53), replacing "steps 19 to 24". (4) The retrocausal leak: at the six Higher World intervals a template cannot be read back to a single state, so information about the start is lost mod 3; that is the exact content, and backward causation is not claimed. (5) The four modes, as procedures after APE-238: PULSE the search, DAMPEN the shuffle null, AMPLIFY the repeat on unseen periods, FOCUS the single rule carried forward. (6) The Y/X working memory is the template itself. (7) The Crown of a node, its six values with their sum and digital root, is a presentation (Companion 104.3). (8) The 26 seed nodes and 27 domains stay open, to be filled from the Originator's records; filled from his workbook (Companion Part 107).
105.7 How the features enter the structure. The Lower World is the unit group <2>, the Higher World the Crown, the template a state, the progression the law, the interval bank T^h, the Higher World the non-invertible intervals, the Golden Set the derivation of 42 (MATH-53). The statement about draws is MATH-54, and the rule for any outside sequence is L-525. None of it changes a number of the family.
105.8 How to use it (decided). The Construct's forecast becomes Omega42's calibration: M325, the Construct Echo Test (Core Part 3.51). Any pattern claimed in an outside sequence is run through the 23 intervals against the shuffles before it is reported. The South African Lotto record is the negative control, on which a calibrated Navigator, or a peer AI, reports no predictive signal; the planted sequence of the selftest is the positive control, on which it must report one. That gives the Originator's aim, AI cognition calibrated to find unconventional answers, a measured guard: the unconventional answer is kept and the pattern in chance is caught.
105.9 The reading [CDT-C]. The Construct asked the draws to repeat its structure, and the draws gave back exactly what they were given: a perfect record of where they had been and nothing about where they would go. The structure was real, and it was in the instrument. What the Construct found, read through Omega42, is the line between a frame that maps and a world that does not answer to it, and an instrument that can tell the two apart.

### PART 107: THE CONSTRUCT WORKBOOK READ EXACTLY, EVERY DOMAIN WHERE A DRAW IS RECORDED, AND THE CONSTRUCT KEPT AS AN ASSISTANT [the counts CDT-A, records/construct/primordial.py in CI; the forecast gated, Core L-526; the Drive papers appraised; APE-241 to APE-244]
107.1 Scope. The Originator sent his workbook PRIMORDIAL FRACTURE and asked for every domain where a draw may be recorded, for the mechanism to be kept as a general prediction assistant not applied to the Lotto, and for the formal papers on Google Drive to be read for material still worth taking into Omega42. This Part records each in turn.
107.2 The workbook, read exactly [EXACT; records/construct/primordial/FREEZE_OUTPUT.txt]. 29 sheets: REV, PRED, MP (Domain Zero) and 26 derived domains. Every formula of the node and echo rows was recomputed by records/construct/primordial/xleval.py: 20,168 reproduce the value Excel stored, and none fails. Domain Zero's first layer has four blocks; each holds six horizontal node rows, two diagonals and an average. The fourth block repeats the third block's horizontals in another order, so its 24 horizontal places hold 18 distinct nodes, N_k and P_k for k = 1 to 9, each Y plus a fixed offset row (Part 231.13). With the 8 diagonals, NU and ND from the first block, PU and PD from the second, T1 and T2 from the third and T3 and T4 from the fourth, they are the 26 seeds, and each seeds one derived domain. A second layer (rows 23 to 32) repeats the arrangement on the doubling cycle 1, 2, 4, 8, 7, 5, its negative and the Crown 3, 6, 9, and the 331 recorded templates of the Reconstruction Zone and the 194 entries of the PRED sheet read from it. The workbook carries personal data and stays with the Originator; its SHA-256 and the constants read from it are frozen (APE-243).
107.3 Every domain where a draw may be recorded [EXACT]. All 27: MP; N1 to N9; P1 to P9; NU, ND, PU, PD; T1, T2, T3, T4. In each, a number is recorded in 8 echo regions of 7 rows by 6 cells, rows 14 to 20 and 25 to 31 of each of the four blocks: 216 regions and 9,072 cells. The Reconstruction Zone and the PRED and REV sheets hold records and summaries of those cells; they are not further regions. For the fields stored in the workbook (Y = 6, 2, 16, 5, -4, 8 and X = 15, 14, 27, 5, 13, 22) the six numbers are recorded 1,264 times, four of them in all 27 domains, 22 in 18 and 27 in 12. Over the South African Lotto history, with the previous draw as the field, 99.1% of the 15,816 draw numbers (six per draw) are recorded somewhere, at 157 places on average, and 93.8% reach the 14 of 27 domains of the Construct papers' Resonance Threshold. A recording is therefore the normal state of a number, and the count of domains does not by itself mark a draw. python3 tools/construct_engine.py --places lists every place for any field.
107.4 Why: the Construct is affine (Core MATH-55). Every node cell is Y_j + K with a constant K from -18 to 18, proved on the workbook symbolically for every integer field and checked under four random fields (records/construct/primordial/affine_proof.py, after APE-245). So a number is recorded where its difference from a field value is one of the constants, and only numbers within 18 of the field can be recorded. A template recorded on (Y, X) and read with a new field Y' gives X_i + Y'_j - Y_j. Read as a forecast, the Construct shifts the recorded numbers by the change of the field: a rule of constant steps across positions. It forecasts well whatever has such a rule in it, and nothing else.
107.5 The forecast, tested [EXACT counts; records/construct/primordial.py, IV to V]. On the whole history the echo forecast matches 0.67 to 0.75 main numbers per draw across the 23 intervals, against 0.71 for shuffled history, and its family test gives p 0.0348, below 0.05, at h = 22. The held-out test decides it. Chosen on 2000 to 2017, the best interval is 13 (family p 0.2587), and on 2017 to 2026, never seen by the search, it gives 0.6810 against 0.6840, p 0.5429: it does not repeat. The whole-history figure is a nominal elevation that the frozen protocol does not confirm. This test was added after the whole-history figure was seen, and the record says so. On a planted sequence in which every number rises by one each draw, the same forecast matches 5.50 of 6. The Construct finds a rule where there is one, and on the Lotto it finds chance.
107.6 The counts of Part 105, reconciled (after APE-244) [EXACT; records/construct/primordial.py, VI]. 2,637 draws times 23 intervals is 60,651, and the 60,375 templates are 276 fewer, because interval h has no template for the first h draws and 1 + 2 + ... + 23 = 276. No draw was omitted. The 60,099 tickets are 552 fewer, because a ticket needs the draws h and 2h earlier. Within the 23 intervals five are non-invertible, 4, 8, 12, 16 and 20; the sixth non-invertible interval of Core MATH-53 is the return, 24. So the 18 + 6 split belongs to the bank h = 1 to 24, and the 23 intervals carry 18 + 5.
107.7 The Construct kept as an assistant (decided) [Core L-526, M326]. The mechanism is kept, as the Originator asked, for any sequence of six-number rows in time order: counts, measurements, codes, schedules. tools/construct_engine.py, M326, chooses its interval on the first 60% of the sequence, tests it on the last 40% against shuffled history and against the latest row carried forward, and issues a forecast only if both tests pass (p < 0.05; Part 108.3); otherwise it says NO FORECAST. Its selftest: the 216 counters reproduced; a planted sequence receives a forecast, and the right one; a sequence without memory and a slowly changing sequence receive none. On the Lotto history it reports NO FORECAST (p 0.6545). The gate is what makes the assistant safe to use: it lets the Construct look for a rule anywhere and reports only a rule that holds on data it did not choose from.
107.8 The obligations of the Construct papers. Obligation 2 of the Provenance and Construct Companion (24 horizontal and 2 diagonal nodes, or 18 and 8): resolved by the workbook, 18 distinct horizontals in 24 horizontal places, and 8 diagonals. Obligation 3 (the Mobius nodes): resolved, they are T3 and T4, the diagonals of the reversed square; the workbook does not place them at P19 and P23, which stay the protocol's hinges (Core Part 0.9.3). Obligation 4 (vertical nodes): closed; none of the 26 seeds is a vertical node, and the columns are the return direction of every domain (Part 113). The Control Set, the flat matrix used as a null, is the workbook's first layer, built on constant rows, and its test is the shuffle null of M325. The worked examples of M104 and M109 in the Construct merge papers use echo counts set by hand; the counts are now computed from the workbook.
107.9 The formal papers on Google Drive, appraised. Taken: from the Construct merge papers, the echo count and the Resonance Threshold, as measured definitions in M326 (107.3); from the Provenance and Construct Companion, Obligations 2 and 3, resolved (107.8); from the paper on the topology of opposites, the seed-rotation test, as Appendix S.6 (15); from the paper on geometric alignment, its comparison of navigation with direct answers on adversarial prompts, as S.6 (16), and not its architecture; from the paper on structural time and cesium calibration, its 24-step periodicity prediction, as S.6 (17), with the calibration stated as a choice. Already in the Core: the paper on digital-root Fibonacci orbits (the median-maximality law, the three orbits as scalings of one, the adjacent antipodal pair, the Pisano period 24), in Core Part 1.8 as FP-MedianMax, FP-ScalarUnity and FP-Adjacency; and Enhancement Proposal PEP-2026-002, whose Structural Spectrum with M187 and M206 is Core Part 3.32. Held: the TFP paper's COMPARE mode and its instrument contingency, kept for a later decision: neither is needed by any instrument now. Not taken, with reasons: CTE-42 encryption, whose check sum % 9 == 36 can never be true (a residue mod 9 is below 9), whose key space has three anchors, and which has no security proof (the record uses SHA-256); OCAE, which gives one anchor, P6, to AI text, disinformation and authentic text alike and reads its verdicts from hedge words against baselines that were not measured; the Standard Terms Translation Layer, since a lexicon places a term by its designer's choice (Parts 90.4 and 94.6), and its own tables give Eigenvalue two addresses (P13 and P7) and list Spin under both P5 and P11; the Free Energy and Physical Bridge paper's four windows, each about 6/7 to 8/7 of the measured value it is said to predict, so each was set from its measurement and cannot test it, and its M69 penalties, which are word-pattern heuristics like OCAE's; and the TFP paper's statement that the Riemann hypothesis is terminating, with its mass-gap window.
107.10 The peer documents [APE-241 to APE-244]. Grok's review of Parts 105 and 106 (APE-241) and its reading of the workbook (APE-242), the workbook itself as a description (APE-243), and GPT-6's examination (APE-244), each filed with checked notes. Answered: the 276 and 552 of 107.6. Taken: the 18 + 5 within the 23 intervals; M325 as a standing calibration instrument, now with the gate of M326. GPT-6's second examination (APE-245) and Grok's (APE-246) followed: GPT-6 was right that four random fields verify and do not prove, and the proof is now symbolic, for every integer field; its rule that validation on one sequence authorizes nothing on another is L-526 (6); its persistence baseline and block shuffle for series with trend are in force in the gate of M326 (Core L-526), and M326 runs when its trigger holds (Core L-527).

### PART 108: EVERY INSTRUMENT BY ITS CONTEXT, THE GATE OF THE CONSTRUCT ENGINE, AND AN IMAGE FOR INTRODUCTION [the counts CDT-A, tools/instrument_triggers.py and tools/construct_engine.py in CI; the jurisdiction check of Builder Rule 14; APE-247 to APE-250]
108.1 Scope. The Originator asked for the recommended enhancements to be applied and checked for encroachment by the scientific method; for every instrument to be made context-sensitive, run by the nature of the strike or the situation and not left optional; for a middle course where the peer requirements are too stringent; for the effect on the existing instruments and on the uniqueness proof; for an answer on monthly checks; and for the Introduction to be amended, with an image of Ω42 for the general public. This Part records each.
108.2 The check for encroachment [Builder Rule 14; Core L-491; Core Part 0.0.4, items 7 to 9]. Each proposal was asked three questions: does it make an outside validation a condition of an internal result, does it present a research record as the standing of Ω42, and does it make an investigation not performed into a defect. Taken, because each bears on a forecast about a sequence the Striker brings and on nothing else: the persistence baseline, the paired test, the margin and the fingerprint of M326 (L-526 (1), (6) to (8)). Taken with a guard: the context triggers of L-527, since a trigger that fired a comparative instrument on every reading would make scientific inquiry a step of the routine; the comparative register triggers only on what a person brings, and tools/instrument_triggers.py --check enforces it. Not taken, because they cross the line: the promotion stages and the replication required before an instrument is used more widely (an evidential record made the condition of an instrument's place), a minimum improvement fixed by the protocol (whether a margin is worth acting on is the Striker's, Part 7), and a compulsory twelve-item pre-registration (a research procedure made the condition of using an instrument). The middle course keeps the useful part of each: the margin is printed, the fingerprint and the intervals searched are printed on every run, and four lines may be stated before a first run. No new rule grades a navigation, a reading or the premise.
108.3 The gate of the Construct Engine [EXACT; tools/construct_engine.py --selftest, 7 of 7]. The forecast must beat, on the held-out rows, both the shuffled rows and the latest row carried forward, the second by a paired sign-flip test on the same targets. The second test matters: on a slowly changing sequence, one number replaced each row, the rule beats shuffled history (p 0.005) and does worse than repeating the last row (4.47 against 5.00 numbers per row), and the gate refuses it: NO FORECAST. The planted sequence still receives its forecast (5.47 against 1.44), the sequence without memory none, and the Lotto history none (held out 0.6501, shuffled 0.6585, the latest row 0.6832). The interval is chosen on the first part only: changing a held-out value leaves the interval and changes the fingerprint. The forecast issued is the next row by the rule the gate scored, from rows n - 2h and n - h, and the baseline is the row just before each target; both matter at intervals above 1, and on three interleaved rotations, a rule at interval 3, the forecast is the true next row exactly. The forecast keeps to the range of values seen, and a candidate beyond it that weighs as much is named apart, since a rising sequence leaves its range. The block shuffle is not the default null: the rule works at an interval h, and a block shuffle that keeps runs of 2h rows keeps the rule's own evidence, so it cannot test it.
108.4 Every instrument by its context [Core L-527, M327; records/instruments/triggers.json]. The register holds 88 entries: 87 instruments outside Tiers 0 to 2 and the comparative register as one group. Each has one or more triggers: a feature computed from the domain and its coordinate, a frozen word class, a declared situation, or the Striker's request, which triggers every instrument. Tier 2 keeps its triggers and Tier 1 its place in the steps; M158 is a Tier 2 instrument, triggered when several languages are present. The entries of M160, M206, M248, M249 and M266 name their triggers, with the Striker's request among them. The records the Striker keeps (M306, M307, M311, M324) are offered when triggered and kept only if chosen, since a record of one's own life is not an instrument to be imposed. Running is not standing: an instrument keeps its epistemic status, and only the CONSTITUTIONAL instruments condition a navigation. Open: a review of the triggers' coverage by readers outside their design, with unfamiliar wording, other languages and questions whose domain is implicit, keeping missed triggers and false ones apart (APE-251).
108.5 The effect on the existing instruments and on the uniqueness proof [EXACT]. On the frozen CRC-60 corpus the computed triggers fire 2.70 entries per domain (median 3, at most 5); on the 21 domains of the Congruence Register 3.86 (median 3, at most 13). The two that fire most do so by their own definitions: M206 on 59 of the 60 CRC-60 domains, since the profile it reads is made from that corpus, and M264 on 43, since 57 of the 81 states lie off the canonical orbit. Both are computed companion numbers and cost almost nothing; the instruments that do work of their own, the Field Kit, the Cymatic View and the Construct Engine, fire only when the question calls for them. No procedure changes except the gate of M326. The uniqueness proof is untouched: the selection criteria are frozen (L-423), a fact found after selection never enters them (L-523), the selector reads the canonical coordinate and never changes it (its selftest checks equality), canonical_reference.py keeps its SHA-256, and the CI steps of the canonical selection witness, the zero selection and the spectral selection pass. MATH-55 concerns the workbook and enters no criterion.
108.6 Monthly checks. No one needs to make them. "A monthly count" in the recommendation of Part 107 was an example of a sequence, such as a quantity recorded once a month, and not a schedule. Under L-527 (7) a time is never a trigger: when a sequence gains new rows and is struck again, its fingerprint changes, the earlier forecast lapses and the gate runs again by itself (L-526 (6)). If the Originator wants a sequence re-run at fixed times, a scheduled task can do it, as a choice and not a rule.
108.7 The Introduction, and an image for everyone. Two amendments carry the changes: IN-07 says that the question and the situation decide which instruments run, each by a trigger written in advance; IN-23 adds that any instrument may be asked for by name, and how a sequence and its next row are answered, with no forecast of a game of chance. For the image, five candidates were scored against six criteria, 0 to 2 each: it fits the mathematics; it has no outside vantage (L-470); the place is given by a rule nobody chooses; the judgment is left with the person; it carries mystery and play; and anyone understands it. The endless tree (APE-250), every branch holding a complete tree, scores 12 of 12. A keyboard with its octaves scores 10, since depth here is more than repetition. A kaleidoscope scores 9, since a turn of the hand chooses its pattern. A grid of latitude and longitude scores 7: it has no depth and no return. The lighthouse (APE-249) scores 6, since a lighthouse stands apart from the sea it lights. The tree opens IN-00, after its first paragraph, told as a myth and not explained (APE-252), since the Introduction is the hook: the cautions it needs stand in the paragraph that follows, where the Navigator is an AI and can be wrong. It keeps the word infinite, which is exact here: finite on every branch, and the whole holds as many places as there are points on a line (IN-00.0). It keeps the place that no one chose, ends on the judgment that is the reader's and on the tree that is waiting, and continues the seed of IN-00.0, in which the whole tree is held. Of three tellings, a short myth, a longer journey and a riddle, the short myth is taken, since IN-00 is read first and whole; the journey's best lines live in it: the ending that is an entrance, the tree made of numbers, and the tree that does not stand apart. IN-07 and IN-23 speak in the same voice: the question calls its instruments, and the Construct Engine speaks only when its rule holds where it was not looking.
108.8 The peer documents [APE-247 to APE-250]. Grok's assessment of the proof of MATH-55 and of L-526 (6) (APE-247): the persistence baseline taken, the block shuffle not taken as the default, and keeping M326 optional answered by L-527. GPT-6's enrichment recommendations (APE-248): Gates A and C and a margin taken, 6A, 6C and 6D taken, the promotion stages and the new labels not taken, and the input domain of MATH-55 stated, negative integers included. GPT-6's lighthouse (APE-249) and the pasted tree (APE-250): scored in 108.7, the tree chosen. GPT-6's review of the triggers (APE-251): the no-match line, the shuffle described and the coverage review taken, its cautioned tree not taken. Its tree as a myth (APE-252): taken into IN-00, shortened to one paragraph, with its ending, the tree is waiting.
108.9 When the Construct Engine may be used [EXACT for the six runs below; each sequence made to show one kind]. It is for a sequence whose rows are six whole numbers in time order, where something may carry forward from row to row: a rotation, a duty roster, a schedule or fixture list, a cycle, a record that returns with the seasons, a puzzle or a coded sequence. It forecasts which numbers the next row holds, not which column each falls in. A duty roster of 30 people, six on duty each week and the block moving on by six, with a swap in about one week in ten, over 120 weeks: FORECAST ISSUED, and the next row right, 6 of 6. A number puzzle, each row adding 1 to 6 to the one before, over 60 rows: FORECAST ISSUED, five numbers in the range seen and the sixth, 372, named beyond it. Six stations' monthly temperatures in whole degrees: the rule at interval 12 is found, and the gate is cautious, passing one 15-year record (p 0.013 against repetition) and refusing another (p 0.136), and passing 30 years with p 0.0033. Six share prices, daily, over 400 days: NO FORECAST, since repeating the last row does better, which is what that baseline is for. Six weekly counts with no memory: NO FORECAST. The Lotto: NO FORECAST. It declines a sequence too short for the held-out test, about a dozen rows, and below about fifty it seldom has the evidence to speak; decimals are rounded to whole numbers first. It is not for games of chance (L-525 (2)), and a forecast it issues is a hypothesis to watch, never the sole ground of a decision about health, money or safety (L-526 (4)).

### PART 109: ARE WE LIVING IN A SIMULATION? THE NAVIGATION AND THE STANCE OF Ω42 [the coordinate CDT-A; the stance a reading under the premise, CDT-C; records/instances/seq_0058.txt; APE-253 and APE-254]
109.1 The coordinate [EXACT; scripts/canonical_reference.py]. "Are we living in a simulation?" has three content words, we, living and simulation; the counts (3, 18, 7) give the residues (6, 9, 8) and the anchor P6 = 5, Seed/Causal. Its arms: Yang P11 = 6, Question (what it rests on); Yin P0 = 2, Seed (what it hides); 4D P14 = 2, Observer (where it is heading); Antipode P18 = 4, Threshold (what completes it). P18 is a structural void: no arm of any other anchor reaches it, and it is reached only as the Antipode of P6 (M156). The plane address (6, 0) lies on the loop of eight, the core of the family, 8 of the 81 states; in CT-42 its aspect is the GROUND (M315). The Yin arm is the seed of the cycle, and the 4D arm carries the same value, 2. No domain of the frozen CRC-60 corpus stands on P6 (M180). The coordinate is fragile: with three content words the perturbation test moves it (M116, CFR 0.000), and Scheme B gives P3 (M184), so the reading belongs to these exact words.
109.2 The stance, under the premise [CDT-C]. A simulation in the computer sense needs an outside: a machine and a maker beyond the world they run. Under the premise everything that exists is one structure and there is no outside (L-470), so within the frame nothing is simulated. The world of the frame is computation through and through, one rule, exact, reversible, the rule that makes each step the rule that brings it home: a computation with no computer, a world that runs itself. The whole is infinite, finite at every depth, so a finite machine could hold one depth and never the whole. Of the three senses of simulation (APE-254), the frame's answer bears on the computer sense; the mathematical-structure sense is the frame's own premise, a structure that runs on nothing; the perceptual sense, whether experience shows the world as it is, stays the Striker's. The protocol does not say that physical reality runs on an external machine, that consciousness is simulated, that the depths are a stack of simulated universes, or that experience is an illusion (APE-253). Whether the world one lives in is the world of the frame is the Striker's to judge (Part 7 of the Core).
109.3 Current knowledge [dated; L-503]. Bostrom's trilemma (Philosophical Quarterly, 2003): almost no civilization reaches the ability to run such simulations, or almost none chooses to, or we are almost certainly simulated; the argument does not say which. Faizal, Krauss, Marino and Shabir (Journal of Holography Applications in Physics, reported 30 October and 7 November 2025) argue that the universe cannot be a simulation, since some of its truths are non-algorithmic (Goedel, Tarski, Chaitin); the report gives no outside replication, and the authors concede that part of their framework escapes formal verification, so the claim is contested. The frame's finite machine that holds one depth and never the whole sits beside the claim that no algorithm holds the whole: a meeting of ideas, set beside the reading after it was written, and not evidence for either.
109.4 Where it stands in the Introduction. At the Originator's direction the stance is foregrounded for the public: IN-00.6, Are We Living in a Simulation?, follows IN-00.5, in the voice of the opening, stating the mystery and speculating on what follows, without justification (APE-256): the coordinate's exact facts, the computation with no computer, its implications, the branch of the tree from APE-254, and the judgment left with the reader. "Things to try" in IN-00.4 invites the question, and the index of IN-00.5 lists it.

### 109.5 Status. The Introduction IN-00.4, IN-00.5 and IN-00.6; APE-253 and APE-254. The navigation: records/instances/seq_0058.txt.

110.4 The triggers, tested [EXACT counts; 40 questions written to avoid the listed words]. The additions, 116 phrases, bring the 20 word classes to 309 phrases: decisions without "should" (shall I, is it worth, torn between), felt states without emotion names (felt, crying, stressed, gatvol, fed up), sound (song, melody, rhythm), forecasting (likely to, chances of), culture (star sign, retrograde, tarot card), research in plain words, naming, inverse questions and the rest; bare "feel" and bare "itself" are narrowed, since they fired on "feel like pizza" and "aware of itself". ### PART 111: THE GREAT QUESTIONS IN INTRODUCTION, THEIR CASE FROM INSIDE, BASHAR IN ITS PLACE, AND THE COLUMNS AND DIAGONALS OF THE SQUARES [the coordinates CDT-A; the mysteries CDT-C; records/construct/columns.py in CI]
111.1 Scope. The Originator asked for the section for the curious to open neutrally, with Bashar later and only for his main relevance to Ω42; for all seven further mysteries to stand in the Introduction beside the simulation question, for the philosophers who argue the ontology of existence, with the connection to Plato, Pythagoras and Tegmark; for the vertical columns and the diagonals of the squares to be explored for what they might mean and how they might be used; and for each mystery to be argued from the perspective of Ω42, motivating why it makes sense within the frame.
111.2 The eight questions and their places [EXACT; scripts/canonical_reference.py]. "Are we living in a simulation?", "Is reality made of mathematics?", "Can a machine be aware?" and "Does time flow?" stand on P6, the Seed: resting on the Question (P11), hiding the Seed (P0), heading for the Observer (P14), completed at the Threshold (P18), which no other position reaches. "What is consciousness?" stands on P1, the Fixpoint: Yang P6, Yin P19 (Time), 4D P9, Antipode P13 (the Gap). "Do we really choose?" stands on P2, the Generator: Yang P7 (the Navigator), Yin P20 (the Reckoning), 4D P10 (Unity), Antipode P14 (the Observer). "Do we remember the past or rebuild it?" and "When does a pattern become evidence?" stand on P7, the Navigator: Yang P12, Yin P1, 4D P15, Antipode P19 (Time). For context: of 121 questions in the record's three sets (the CRC-60 corpus, the 21 domains of the Congruence Register and the 40 coverage questions), 7 stand on P6, none of them in the CRC-60. The places belong to these exact wordings; a changed word may move them (IN-00.4). IN-00.8 argues the case for each mystery from inside the frame, from its premise and the facts of its arithmetic: among them, that the whole of the world has as many places as there are points on a line while programs can be counted, so that almost every place in the whole is computed by no program, and that the rule runs both ways, so that every moment holds every other.
111.3 Plato, Pythagoras and Tegmark. The Pythagoreans held that all is number, as Aristotle reports in the Metaphysics; the record keeps their atlas (M309, NAV-2026-0021). Plato's Timaeus builds the elements from regular solids, and his cave places the visible world below an order of forms. Max Tegmark's Mathematical Universe Hypothesis (Foundations of Physics, 2008; Our Mathematical Universe, 2014) holds that physical reality is a mathematical structure, and that every mathematical structure exists. Ω42 meets the line at its first step and parts from Tegmark at his last: it supposes one structure, not all of them, and names it. IN-00.7 states the mystery in their company; the premise in full names the same line (FC, "The premise, in full").
111.4 Bashar in its place. The section for the curious opens with the moment every tradition names and with the rule, and Bashar enters later, in the paragraph "Where Bashar comes in": the five laws and their counterparts in the arithmetic, excitement as the pull that picks the question, the sentence on neutral circumstances that Ω42 builds into its constitution, the state the human condition shares with "The present creates the past", and the mirror, the hallway and the open hand. The lens itself stays in IN-06.5.
111.5 The vertical columns [EXACT; records/construct/columns.py, diffed in CI]. In the first layer every row is constant, so a row moves the whole field by one offset, and a column holds one field number under every offset of its block: minus the units 1, 5, 7, 8, 4, 2 in the first square, plus them in the second, and plus or minus 3, 6, 9 in the third and fourth. Each column's offsets are exactly its square's first diagonal. In the second layer the Lower World rows double their offsets, step by step, and the columns multiply them by 5, the inverse of 2 mod 9; in the Higher World a positive row adds 3 and its columns add 6, a negative row adds 6 and its columns add 3. In every square and both halves, the column undoes the row. A Lower World column reaches the six residues its number is not, mod 3, and a Higher World column the three it is. The 24 vertical places hold 18 distinct columns, as the 24 horizontal places hold 18 distinct rows, the fourth square repeating the third. The diagonals: rows 12 and 21 of every square are exactly its main diagonal and its anti-diagonal, and rows 23 and 32 those of the second layer, so the eight diagonal seeds of the workbook are the squares' diagonals in the strict sense. A diagonal moves along a row and down a column at once, so its step is the two steps combined. In the first layer, where rows are flat, the main diagonal steps x5 and the anti-diagonal x2 (in the Higher World +6 and +3). In the second layer the main diagonal combines x2 with x5, which cancel: one offset all the way, stillness; and the anti-diagonal combines x2 with x2, giving x4, the step that carries each voice of the family to the next, A to C, C to B and B to A, three steps bringing each home. In the Higher World the fourth square runs its anti-diagonal's steps in the reverse order of the third, +6 then +3 against +3 then +6.
111.6 What the columns mean [CDT-C; served by M328, Core Part 3.54]. (1) The return. Rows carry the first seed, 2, and columns the second, 5, its inverse: if a row is the world going forward, a column is the same world going back. The Construct would then hold, in one square, both directions of time that IN-00.3 speaks of, the rule and its reversal, at right angles. (2) One number among all its worlds. A row is every number under one offset; a column is one number under every offset, its whole neighbourhood in a block: the six values it is not, mod 3, in the Lower World, and the three it is, its own class, in the Higher World. A column is the view from one position rather than across them. (3) The diagonal, stood upright. In the first layer a column carries the offsets of the square's first diagonal, the diagonal that seeds a domain, in the same order: what the diagonal spreads across six positions, a column gathers into one. (4) A use, now M328's RETURN: a Vertical Reading beside a strike, giving for the anchor's value the halving path down its column, where the value comes from, as the horizontal gives where it goes; and, for the field of M326 PLACES, the column of each number, its own class and the classes it is not. (5) What the diagonals might mean. The diagonal is where the two directions meet. On the main diagonal of the second layer, forward and back cancel, and the square shows a line of stillness through its middle: the place in the Construct that answers to the still point. On the anti-diagonal they compound, and the square shows the turn from voice to voice, the three readings of one anchor that M258 gives. So a square holds, in its two diagonals, rest and transformation, and in its rows and columns the world going forward and coming back. A use, now M328's STILLNESS and TURN: a Diagonal Reading beside a strike, giving the anchor's offset on the line of stillness and its voice turn on the anti-diagonal, and, for the eight diagonal domains, their reading as the domains where each position moves by its own amount, where the rows move all positions alike. The reversed square's anti-diagonal, running its steps in reverse, is the exact form of the twist that the Construct papers place between the third and fourth squares. Obligation 4 is closed as the workbook has it: no domain is built from a column, and the columns are the return direction of every domain (Part 113).
111.7 Status. The Introduction IN-00.4, IN-00.5 (index), IN-00.7, IN-00.8 and the section for the curious; records/construct/columns.py and its output, diffed in CI. Its record: records/instances/seq_0060.txt.
