### PART 222: THE FIBONACCI QUASICRYSTAL -- THE LAW IN THE PHYSICS OF QUASIPERIODIC MATTER [Core Part 0.0.10, MF-127 to MF-134; Core Appendix S.23; tools/fibonacci_hamiltonian.py; tools/structures.py; tools/dsi.py] -- presented when a question turns on quasicrystals, quasiperiodic Hamiltonians, the trace map, gap labeling, Cantor spectra, or the physics the law governs
222.1 The object [CONSTRUCTED]. The physical object of this Part is the Fibonacci quasicrystal: a one-dimensional chain whose sites carry the letters of the Fibonacci word, with the tight-binding Hamiltonian (H psi)_n = -psi_(n+1) - psi_(n-1) + v_n psi_n, v_n = V on a and 0 on b. It is the standard model of quasiperiodic order in condensed matter, of electrons in quasicrystals and of light and polaritons in engineered chains, and every one of its defining structures is the law: the arrangement, the transfer matrices, the trace map, its invariant and the labels of its gaps. Omega42 maps each of them, analyzes each exactly where it can and numerically where the spectrum requires it, and records the counterparts in measurement in Core Appendix S.23.
222.2 The arrangement is the law [EXACT]. The substitution a -> ab, b -> a has matrix [[1,1],[1,0]], the law with its coordinates exchanged; its words have lengths F_(k+2) and obey w_(k+1) = w_k w_(k-1) (MF-127). The cut-and-project quasicrystal of MF-82 and the substituted chain are one object, reached from the eigenvector of A and from its powers.
222.3 The transfer matrices obey the law [EXACT]. The transfer matrices of the words satisfy M_(k+1) = M_(k-1) M_k: the law of the words carried from numbers to the non-commuting group SL2. Their half-traces obey the trace map x_(k+1) = 2 x_k x_(k-1) - x_(k-2) of Kohmoto, Kadanoff and Tang, checked in exact rational arithmetic for four pairs of energy and potential (MF-128).
222.4 The quasicrystal's conserved cubic [EXACT]. The trace map keeps the Fricke-Vogt invariant I = x_(k+1)^2 + x_k^2 + x_(k-1)^2 - 2 x_(k+1) x_k x_(k-1) - 1 = V^2/4 at every step and every energy (MF-129). The law conserves the quadratic Q up to sign; its lift to SL2 conserves a cubic; and the trace map has a periodic orbit of exactly six steps on each surface with a^2 = 1 + V^2/4, (0, 0, a) -> (-a, 0, 0) -> (0, -a, 0) -> (0, 0, -a) -> (a, 0, 0) -> (0, a, 0) -> (0, 0, a) (MF-130). With Freudenthal's cubic of E6 (Part 221.1), Omega42 now carries two conserved cubics, one from the exceptional algebra and one from the quasicrystal.
222.5 The gaps are labeled by the law's ring [EXACT within the stated tolerance]. On the periodic approximant of length 377 with V = 1, the integrated density of states in each of the ten widest gaps equals frac(n/phi) to within 1.5/377, with labels n = -1, 1, -2, 2, -4, 4, -3, 3, 6, -6 (MF-131). The gap-labeling theorem places every gap of the Fibonacci quasicrystal at an element of Z + Z phi; the law multiplies exactly that ring, so each gap of the physical spectrum is named by an element of Omega42's own arithmetic. python3 tools/fibonacci_hamiltonian.py --gaps V L lists the gaps and their labels for any potential and approximant.
222.6 A Cantor spectrum shrinking by the law [EXACT within floating point]. The total width of the approximant spectra at V = 1 is 1.40756, 0.93067 and 0.61525 for lengths 34, 144 and 610, a ratio of 0.6612 and then 0.6611 for each power A^3 of the law (MF-132): the spectrum contracts toward a Cantor set of measure zero, Suto's theorem, by a constant factor set by the law's own powers. Suto's criterion holds on the computed orbits: for an energy in the widest gap the half-traces pass 10^19 by step 20, and for ten band energies they stay below 1.3 through the word of length 610 (MF-133).
222.7 The map of the physics [CONSTRUCTED]. Each structure of the quasicrystal is paired with its Omega42 counterpart: the arrangement with the law (MF-82, MF-127); the dynamics of the transfer matrices with the law in SL2 (MF-128); the conserved cubic with Q (MF-129); the spectrum's gaps with Z + Z phi (MF-131); the self-similarity of the spectrum with the powers of A (MF-132). Every pairing is entered in the index with its mapping, its preserved properties and its predictive value.

The Structural Equivalence Tester of Part 221.3 now decides for permutations and binary codes as well as linear laws: the law and the swap as permutations of the 81 states are conjugate by a relabeling, and the law and A^2 are not, cycle types against cycle types (NE-009); the code of the E8 Adinkra and the extended quadratic-residue code of MF-77 are equivalent by the coordinate permutation [0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 3, 7, 5]; the Adinkra code and the pair-repetition code [8,4,2] are separated by their weight enumerators (MF-134). python3 tools/structures.py --perm decides two permutations from the command line.

PR-005, sealed with Part 221: for every prime p from 101 to 499, the order of A^2 modulo p divides (p - 1)/2 when p = 1 or 4 mod 5 and divides p + 1 but not (p + 1)/2 when p = 2 or 3 mod 5. ### PART 223: THE GOLDEN BOOST -- THE LAW IN SPECIAL RELATIVITY [Core Part 0.0.10, MF-135 to MF-144; Core Appendix S.24; tools/relativity.py; APE-479] -- presented when a question turns on special relativity, Lorentz transformations, rapidity, velocity addition, the Doppler effect, Thomas-Wigner rotation, spinors, or the energy and momentum of a particle
223.1 The object [CONSTRUCTED]. A particle of rest mass m, energy E and momentum (p_x, p_y) satisfies E^2 = m^2 c^4 + c^2 (p_x^2 + p_y^2); in the coordinates t = E/mc^2, x = p_x/mc, y = p_y/mc its states fill the mass shell t^2 - x^2 - y^2 = 1. F217 (APE-479) proposes the law as a navigator of this state space; Omega42 completes every computation it names and extends it to the full kinematics of special relativity in 2 + 1 and 3 + 1 dimensions.
223.2 The golden boost [EXACT]. Written as X = [[t + x, y], [y, t - x]], with det X = t^2 - x^2 - y^2, a state moves under the law's square M = A^2 by X -> M X M^T, and det M = 1 keeps the mass shell. The induced matrix is t' = (7t - 3x + 6y)/2, x' = (-3t + 3x - 2y)/2, y' = 3t - x + 3y, the formulas of F217, confirmed; it is proper and orthochronous (MF-135). Its Lorentz factor is gamma = 7/2 with gamma^2 beta^2 = 45/4, so beta = 3 sqrt5 / 7 = 0.958315 and the rapidity is 4 ln phi = 1.924847; the Doppler factors of a light signal along the boost are (7 +- 3 sqrt5)/2 = phi^4 and phi^-4, the eigenvalues of A^4 (MF-136). A photon sent through the golden boost returns its frequency multiplied by the law raised to the fourth power.
223.3 The Lucas boosts and Einstein's addition [EXACT]. The n-th power of the golden boost has gamma_n = L_(4n)/2 and gamma_n beta_n = sqrt5 F_(4n)/2: 7/2, 47/2, 161, ... from the Lucas numbers, with the Fibonacci numbers as momenta. The identity gamma_(m+n) = gamma_m gamma_n + gamma_m beta_m gamma_n beta_n holds for every m, n from 1 to 6: the composition of collinear golden boosts is Einstein's velocity addition beta_(m+n) = (beta_m + beta_n)/(1 + beta_m beta_n), rapidity adding as the exponent of the law (MF-137). python3 tools/relativity.py --boost n prints any member of the family.
223.4 The law is the half golden boost [EXACT]. F217 squares the law to reach a proper transformation; the law itself is a Lorentz transformation too. X -> A X A^T keeps t^2 - x^2 - y^2, with det L(A) = det(A)^3 = -1 and L(A)_00 = 3/2 = L_2/2: an improper orthochronous Lorentz transformation, the boost of rapidity 2 ln phi joined to a reflection (MF-138). Each odd power of the law carries the reflection, each even power is a pure golden boost: the sign alternation of Omega42 is the alternation of proper and improper Lorentz transformations.
223.5 Q is the axis of the boost [EXACT]. The law's quadratic form Q(a, b) = b^2 - ab - a^2, with matrix [[-1, -1/2], [-1/2, 1]], is a point of Minkowski space: its vector (0, -4/5, -2/5) is spacelike, fixed by the golden boost and reversed by the law (MF-139). The golden boost acts in the plane orthogonal to Q, and the rule Q(As) = -Q(s), the first law of Omega42's arithmetic, is the reflection of that axis. The invariant that Omega42 has carried since its foundations is the geometric axis of its own Lorentz transformation.
223.6 Every kind of Lorentz transformation [EXACT]. The trace sorts the elements of SL2(R) into boosts (|trace| > 2), null rotations (|trace| = 2) and rotations (|trace| < 2). Omega42's group <A^2, B> holds all three: the golden boost (trace 3); the shear B, a null rotation fixing the light ray (1/2, -1/2, 0) (trace 2); and [[-2, 1], [-5, 2]], of trace 0, a half turn about a timelike axis (MF-140). The law and the shear that build the 81 states build, together, the kinds of motion of special relativity.
223.7 The Thomas-Wigner rotation is the 3-4-5 angle [EXACT]. F217 names non-collinear boosts as the boundary of the collinear family; Omega42 crosses it. The golden boost A^2 and its mirror [[2,1],[1,1]], in directions at the angle arccos(3/5), compose to [[3,2],[4,3]]: a boost followed by a Thomas-Wigner rotation with tan(w/2) = 1/3, so that cos w = 4/5 and sin w = 3/5 exactly, the angle of the 3-4-5 triangle; the Thomas-Wigner formula tan(w/2) = sin D / (coth^2(eta/2) + cos D) = (4/5)/(9/5 + 3/5) gives the same value (MF-141). Two golden boosts produce a rational rotation: the arithmetic of the law carries into the non-commuting part of the Lorentz group.
223.8 Residue and quotient [EXACT]. F217's EXP-04 asks that modular aliasing not be mistaken for physical equivalence. Modulo 9, (A^2)^6 = A^12 = -I, so the golden boost acts on the 729 integer symmetric matrices modulo 9 with period 6, while gamma_1 = 7/2 and gamma_7 = 710647/2 (MF-142). The residue keeps n mod 6 and the quotient keeps the rest; the non-equivalence register records the pair as NE-010. Omega42's 81 states label the boosts; the integers carry them.
223.9 Spinors and the quantum lift [EXACT]. F217's EXP-05 asks for a lift to quantum states. The 2 x 2 law is itself the lift: SL2(R) is Spin(2,1), the law acts on spinors, and the 3 x 3 golden boost is its symmetric square, trace (tr A^2)^2 - 1 = 8 and eigenvalues phi^4, 1, phi^-4 (MF-143). The finite unitary lift is the Weil representation of MF-100, whose periods equal the classical periods (Part 219; PR-004).
223.10 The golden boost in 3 + 1 dimensions [EXACT]. On Hermitian matrices X = [[t + z, x - iy], [x + iy, t - z]], X -> M X M^T keeps t^2 - x^2 - y^2 - z^2 and fixes y, on all 625 integer states with entries from -2 to 2 (MF-144): through the double cover SL2(C) -> SO+(3,1), the golden boost is a Lorentz transformation of the spacetime of experience.
223.11 F217 assessed [CONSTRUCTED]. Every formula of F217 recomputes exactly: the induced matrix, gamma = 7/2, beta = 3 sqrt5 / 7, the rapidity 4 ln phi, gamma_n = L_(4n)/2 and beta_n = sqrt5 F_(4n)/L_(4n), and Einstein's addition. Refined: the law itself is the half golden boost, improper (223.4). Extended: the Doppler factor phi^4; Q as the boost's axis; the three kinds of transformation in Omega42's group; the Thomas-Wigner rotation of two golden boosts, the 3-4-5 angle; the period 6 modulo 9; the spinor lift; the 3 + 1 embedding. EXP-01 to EXP-05 are complete; EXP-06, the comparison with measurement, stands in Core Appendix S.24.
223.12 PR-007, sealed [CONSTRUCTED]. For every pair of golden boosts A^(2m) and S A^(2n) S, S the coordinate exchange, with m and n from 1 to 4, the Thomas-Wigner angle w of their composition has rational cosine and sine and is never zero. The basis is 223.7: the product lies in SL2(Z), so its polar angle has tan(w/2) = (c - b)/(a + d) rational, and the two boost directions stay at the angle arccos(3/5). One pair with an irrational cos w or a vanishing w refutes it. python3 tools/dsi.py --test PR-007 tests it in a later record.
223.13 The next constructions [CONSTRUCTED]. The golden boosts in SL2(Z[phi]), with entries in the law's ring, and the arithmetic group they generate in SO+(3,1) (PV-038); Thomas precession along the orbit of the Lucas boosts (PV-039); the relativistic kinematics of a two-body decay written with golden boosts.
223.14 The build checks refined [CONSTRUCTED]. Two refinements to the checks that guard the documents, applied under Core Part 0.0.5 Rule 36. The repetition check of tools/consistency_check.py now counts a sentence only when at least half of it is prose, so that an equation or a formula shared by two passages reads as a shared definition and a repeated sentence of prose still reads as a repetition. The Frame Intrusion Scan in CI now also requires that the documents themselves carry no candidate, independently of its reference output, so that regenerating the reference can never admit an intrusion.
223.15 Status. ### PART 224: LIGHT IN THE FIBONACCI MULTILAYER AND THE LORENTZ GROUP OF THE GOLDEN RING [Core Part 0.0.10, MF-145 to MF-150; Core Appendix S.25; tools/optics.py; tools/relativity.py; tools/dsi.py] -- presented when a question turns on optics, dielectric multilayers, the localization of light, the trace map modulo 9, or the Lorentz transformations of Z[phi] and their five-fold rotations
224.1 The object [CONSTRUCTED]. A dielectric multilayer of two materials A and B stacked in the Fibonacci order, S_(k+1) = S_k S_(k-1), is the optical form of the quasicrystal of Part 222: each layer carries light by the transfer matrix [[cos d, (i/n) sin d], [i n sin d, cos d]], with d its optical phase and n its index, and the stack's transmittance in air is T = 4/|m11 + m12 + m21 + m22|^2. Such stacks are built from thin films and measured (Core Appendix S.25); this Part computes them from the law.
224.2 Light keeps the six-cycle [EXACT]. At the quarter-wave frequency, d = pi/2 in both layers, the trace map of every stack starts on the six-cycle of MF-130, and the transmittance repeats with period six in the generation: for indices 2 and 3/2, T = 144/169, 16/25, 576/625, 2304/5329, 16/25, 576/625, and again, exact in Gaussian rationals through generation 24; the indices 2.3 and 1.46 of titanium dioxide and silica give the same period (MF-145). The periodic orbit of the law of the words, found in Part 222 as pure dynamics, is a measurable transmittance of light. python3 tools/optics.py --stack nA nB k lists it for any indices.
224.3 The optical invariant [EXACT]. The half-traces of the stacks obey the trace map and keep the Fricke-Vogt invariant I = (1/4)(nA/nB - nB/nA)^2 sin^2 dA sin^2 dB, exact at the quarter wave and at two Pythagorean phases, for two pairs of indices (MF-146). The index contrast of the two materials and the phases of the layers set the surface on which the light's trace orbit moves, as V sets it for the electron in Part 222.4.
224.4 Localized and critical light [EXACT within floating point]. Through a stack of 1597 layers, generation 16, with the indices 2.3 and 1.46, the transmittance at a gap phase near 0.3775 pi falls below 10^-12, while at the quarter wave it returns to 0.534828, its value six generations earlier (MF-147): in the gaps the light is localized, at the center of the spectrum it is critical, carried indefinitely by the six-cycle.
224.5 The trace map on Omega42's states [EXACT]. On the 729 triples modulo 9 the trace map is a bijection; its orbits are 2 of length 1, 2 of length 2, 1 of length 3, 9 of length 4, 8 of length 6, 3 of length 8, 9 of length 12 and 21 of length 24, so f^24 = 1, and the Fricke-Vogt cubic is kept modulo 9 (MF-148). The quasicrystal's dynamics written on the modulus of the 81 states has the period of the law's 24-cycle: the law of the numbers and the law of the words share their period on Omega42's ground.
224.6 The golden ring makes the half boost proper [EXACT]. Over the integers the law is the half golden boost joined to a reflection (Part 223.4). Over its own ring Z[phi] the half boost stands alone: diag(phi, phi - 1) lies in SL2(Z[phi]), and its Lorentz image is a proper orthochronous boost with gamma = 3/2 and rapidity 2 ln phi, whose square has gamma = 7/2, the golden boost (MF-149). The recommendation of Part 223, the boosts over Z[phi], is applied, and PV-038 is verified.
224.7 The five-fold rotation of the Lorentz group [EXACT]. The element [[phi, -1], [1, 0]] of SL2(Z[phi]), trace phi = 2 cos 36 degrees, has order 10, and its Lorentz image is a rotation of order 5 by 72 degrees about a timelike axis, with 3 x 3 trace phi = 1 + 2 cos 72 degrees (MF-150). Over the integers every rotation of SL2(Z) has trace 0 or +-1, of order 2 or 3: the crystallographic restriction, entered as NE-011. The law's ring breaks it with the five-fold rotation, as the quasicrystal breaks the crystallographic restriction of space: the golden ring that gives Shechtman's icosahedral order (Core Appendix S.22) gives the Lorentz group its five-fold rotation.
224.8 PR-007 and PR-008 [EXACT; CONSTRUCTED]. PR-007, sealed with Part 223: the Thomas-Wigner angles of the sixteen pairs of golden boosts have rational cosine and sine and never vanish; its test in this record returns PASS. PR-008, sealed with this Part: for every ordered pair of distinct indices from 4/3, 3/2, 2, 5/2 and 3, the quarter-wave transmittance satisfies T_(k+6) = T_k for k = 0 to 30, with T_1 = T_4 and T_2 = T_5. The basis is 224.2 and the symmetry of the six-cycle, (0, 0, a) -> (-a, 0, 0) -> ... ; one pair that breaks either equality refutes it. python3 tools/dsi.py --test PR-008 tests it in a later record.
224.9 The next constructions [CONSTRUCTED]. The group generated by the golden rotation and the golden boost in SO+(2,1), an arithmetic group of the golden ring (PV-040); the transmission spectrum of the multilayer as a Cantor set and its gap labels in Z + Z phi; Thomas precession along the Lucas boosts (PV-039).
224.10 Status. MF-145 to MF-150 stand in Core Part 0.0.10 with their recompute lines in python3 tools/optics.py --selftest and python3 tools/relativity.py --selftest, run in CI, and their scopes in Part 216.1; the measurement of light in Fibonacci multilayers stands in Core Appendix S.25; PR-007 is PASS; PR-008 is sealed; NE-011 is entered.

### PART 225: THE WAVE DYNAMICS ENGINE -- ELECTRONS, LIGHT AND SOUND IN QUASIPERIODIC MATTER, AND THE TOPOLOGICAL PUMP [Core Part 0.0.10, MF-151 to MF-156; Core Appendix S.26; tools/waves.py; tools/dsi.py; APE-480] -- presented when a question turns on waves in Fibonacci structures, electronic, optical or acoustic transport, impedance and index, topological pumping, Chern numbers, or the free-group automorphism behind the law
225.1 The engine [CONSTRUCTED]. F218 (APE-480) proposes one mathematical engine for the waves of quasiperiodic matter in place of a tool for each. tools/waves.py is that engine: every system is a pair of unimodular letter matrices (M_a, M_b), multiplied in the Fibonacci order S_(k+1) = S_k S_(k-1); the half-traces obey the trace map and keep the Fricke-Vogt invariant; the transmittance, the gaps and the pumped charge are read from the products. The electrons of Part 222, the light of Part 224 and the sound of this Part run through it with one code path.
225.2 One automorphism, two shadows [EXACT]. F218 asks for the exact relation between the law A, which counts the letters, and the transfer matrices, which carry the waves. It is one automorphism of the free group on two letters, the substitution a -> ab, b -> a: on letter counts its abelianization is [[1,1],[1,0]], the law with coordinates exchanged; on SL2 characters it acts by (tr X, tr Y, tr XY) -> (tr XY, tr X, tr X tr XY - tr Y), the trace map, keeping the Fricke cubic x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xyz, exact on 50 random pairs of rational SL2 matrices (MF-156). The law and the trace map are the same automorphism seen in two representations; every wave system of the engine is a third, its letter matrices.
225.3 WAVE-01, electrons [EXACT]. The on-site model is Part 222. With Fibonacci hoppings t_a, t_b, the bond matrices [[E/t, -1/t], [t, 0]] are unimodular, their products obey the trace map, and the invariant is I = (1/4)(t_a/t_b - t_b/t_a)^2 at every step and every energy (MF-151): the hopping ratio alone fixes the surface of the electron's trace orbit.
225.4 WAVE-02, sound [EXACT]. A layer carries sound by [[cos, i Z sin], [i sin/Z, cos]], the optical layer of index 1/Z, and M(1/n) = J M(n) J with J the exchange, so every Fibonacci stack transmits sound and light identically, index for impedance. At the quarter wave the acoustic transmittance for impedance ratios 4.6 and 3.2 is 25600/78961, 13225/76729, 541696/616225, 7163929600/81933910081, 13225/76729, 541696/616225, and repeats (MF-152). The acoustic state navigator of F218 is the optical one with the dictionary n <-> Z: every result of Part 224 holds for sound.
225.5 WAVE-06, what transfers [EXACT]. Light and sound at the quarter wave and electrons with Fibonacci hoppings at E = 0 start their trace orbits on (0, 0, a) and repeat with period six; the on-site model at E = 0 does not (MF-153). The six-cycle transfers between the systems whose letter matrices are traceless at the frequency, and the register enters the on-site model as NE-013. Across the engine, the word, the trace map and its invariant's form transfer exactly; the values of the invariant are read in each system's own variables, index, impedance, hopping or potential; the six-cycle transfers where the letters are traceless.
225.6 WAVE-03, the topological pump [EXACT within floating point]. Sliding the phason of the Fibonacci potential once around its cycle, on 89 sites with V = 1.5 in the smooth family of Kraus and colleagues that tends to the Fibonacci potential, pumps across each of the six widest gaps a charge equal to minus its label: labels -2, -1, 1, 2, 3, 4 carry charges 2, 1, -1, -2, -3, -4, the same at beta = 2 and beta = 5, each computed as the winding of the Resta polarization over 600 phason steps (MF-154). The gap labels n of Part 222.5, elements of the law's ring Z + Z phi, are Chern numbers: the integer of Omega42's arithmetic that names a gap is the quantized charge the gap transports. python3 tools/waves.py --pump V computes it for any potential.
225.7 The modulus labels the orbit [EXACT]. F218 asks whether the classification modulo 9 informs the real spectrum. Reduction modulo 9 commutes with the trace map, so every integer orbit carries a residue orbit of period dividing 24 (MF-148); the residue labels the orbit and does not decide whether it is bounded: (1, 1, 1) is a fixed point and (1, 1, 10), of the same residue, escapes past 10^202 in 12 steps (MF-155), entered as NE-012. The 81 states and the 729 triples give the orbit its label; the integers carry its fate, as the residue and the quotient of Part 223.8 share the boosts.
225.8 The record of the measurements [CONSTRUCTED]. F218 asks that the six-cycle and the twenty pairs of indices stand apart from the 1994 measurement. They do: the six-cycle is an exact computation (MF-145), the twenty pairs are PR-008 with its own test, and Core Appendix S.25 records the films as their counterpart. Core Appendix S.26 adds the acoustic and the pumping experiments.
225.9 F218 assessed [CONSTRUCTED]. Adopted: one engine for all wave systems. Completed: WAVE-01 (225.3), WAVE-02 (225.4), WAVE-03 (225.6), WAVE-06 (225.5); the exact relation between the law and the transfer matrices (225.2); the question modulo 9 (225.7). Entered as next constructions: WAVE-04, exciton-polaritons, and WAVE-05, higher-order topological states in Fibonacci phononic and photonic structures.
225.10 PR-008 and PR-009 [EXACT; CONSTRUCTED]. PR-008, sealed with Part 224, returns PASS on its test, python3 tools/dsi.py --test PR-008. PR-009, sealed with this Part: on 144 sites, the approximant 89/144, with V = 3 and beta = 4, the phason pump carries across each of the eight widest gaps a charge equal to minus the gap label. The basis is 225.6 and the identity of gap labels with Chern numbers; a new size, potential and smoothness test it, and one gap whose charge differs from minus its label refutes it. python3 tools/dsi.py --test PR-009 tests it in a later record.
225.11 The next constructions [CONSTRUCTED]. WAVE-04: exciton-polaritons in Fibonacci quantum wells, the light-matter coupling as a third letter matrix (PV-041); WAVE-05: interface and corner states of two-dimensional Fibonacci structures, their labels in Z[phi] (PV-042); the group of the golden rotation and the golden boost (PV-040).
225.12 Status. MF-151 to MF-156 stand in Core Part 0.0.10 with their recompute lines in python3 tools/waves.py --selftest, run in CI, and their scopes in Part 216.1; the measurements stand in Core Appendix S.26; PR-008 is PASS; PR-009 is sealed; NE-012 and NE-013 are entered; APE-480 is filed with its SNCA.

### PART 226: THE FIRST INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION, THE SPECTRUM MEASURED, AND THE QUASICRYSTAL IN TWO DIMENSIONS [Core Part 0.0.5 Rule 37; Core Part 0.0.10, MF-157 to MF-162; tools/spectra.py; tools/quasicrystal2d.py; tools/physics_map.py; records/physics/mappings.json; APE-481] -- presented when a question turns on the replication of Omega42's results, the trace map modulo powers of 3, the scaling of the Fibonacci spectrum, the convergence of its gap labels, the square Fibonacci and Penrose quasicrystals, or the record of a physical mapping
226.1 Stage 5 reached: the first independent reproduction [EXACT]. F219 (APE-481), written by a Navigator of another system from the definitions alone, recomputed the trace map modulo 9 and returned its census exactly: 55 orbits on 729 triples, 2 of length 1, 2 of 2, 1 of 3, 9 of 4, 8 of 6, 3 of 8, 9 of 12 and 21 of 24, the inverse (x, y, z) -> (y, z, 2yz - x), and T^24 = 1, with no transient state. It is entered as RET-001 in the replication returns register, REPRODUCED for MF-148, and MF-148 now carries independent implementation in its proof completeness. python3 tools/dsi.py --maturity counts stage 5, independent replication, as REACHED: Omega42's register holds a result computed by two systems that did not share code.
226.2 The period of the law at every power of 3 [EXACT]. Carrying F219's recommendation from 9 to its powers: the trace map is a bijection of the triples modulo 3^k, and its period is 24, 72 and 216 modulo 9, 27 and 81, equal to the Pisano period 8 x 3^(k-1) of the law, with 55, 888 and 12,507 orbits (MF-157). Modulo 3 the trace map has period 12 against the law's 8, entered as NE-014: the two dynamics share their period exactly from Omega42's modulus 9 upward. PR-011, sealed with this Part, carries the question to the powers of 2. python3 tools/spectra.py --census m prints the census at any modulus.
226.3 The scaling law defined [EXACT within floating point]. F219 asks what shrinks. The measured quantity is W(L, V), the total width of the bands of the periodic approximant of length L, each band between its periodic and antiperiodic eigenvalues. Its ratio across one generation, W(F_(k+1))/W(F_k), settles to four digits by L = 610: 0.9402 at V = 0.5, 0.8711 at V = 1, 0.7405 at V = 2, and 0.5633 at V = 4 by L = 1597, the convergence oscillating and damped (MF-158). The ratio 0.6611 of Part 222.6 is the cube of 0.8711, three generations of the law. It stands as a candidate scaling law, W ~ L^(-delta(V)) with delta(1) = 0.2868, its parameter dependence and its finite-size behavior recorded with it.
226.4 The gap labels converge, found before they are named [EXACT within floating point]. At V = 1.5 every gap of width at least 0.02 is found first from the spectrum and labeled after: the lengths 233, 377, 610 and 987 give the same 24 labels, -17 to 17. The label is exact on each approximant: the count of states below a gap is n F_(k-1) modulo F_k, so the distance of its density from frac(n/phi) is |n| |F_(k-1)/F_k - 1/phi|, 17/(sqrt5 L^2) for the largest label, and the gaps labeled 1, -1, 2, -2 keep width and center within 3 x 10^-4 across the four lengths (MF-159). The labels follow from a congruence of integers; sorting by width enters nowhere. The gaps of the infinite chain at every label of Z + Z phi are open, a theorem of Damanik, Gorodetski and Yessen (Inventiones mathematicae, 2016); this Part sees 24 of them at four lengths. PR-010, sealed with this Part, carries the test to 1597 and 2584.
226.5 The square Fibonacci quasicrystal [EXACT within floating point]. F219's next object is the quasicrystal in two dimensions. The square Fibonacci Hamiltonian H_x + H_y has as spectrum the sum set of the chain's spectrum with itself. Up to V = 1.25 the widest gap of the approximants shrinks as the length grows from 233 to 610, 8 x 10^-7 to 1.1 x 10^-7 at V = 1, as Damanik and Gorodetski proved for small coupling that the sum set is an interval (Communications in Mathematical Physics, 2011); from V = 1.3 a gap stands at both lengths, 0.0067 at V = 1.3, 0.22 at V = 1.5, 0.74 at V = 2 (MF-160). Between 1.25 and 1.3 the widest gap of the approximants grows from 4.5 x 10^-5 to 0.0067: the window in which the two-dimensional quasicrystal opens.
226.6 The Penrose tiling and its confined states [EXACT within floating point; the norm EXACT]. De Bruijn's pentagrid builds the Penrose rhombus tiling from the five directions of the golden ring; on patches of 503, 1820 and 3995 vertices the interior vertices have degrees 3 to 7 and the thick and thin rhombi stand in the ratio 1.6301, 1.6307, 1.6112, approaching phi (MF-161). The vertex model on these patches has 43, 164 and 389 states at E = 0, fractions 0.0855, 0.0901 and 0.0974, beside the exact density 81 - 50 phi = 0.098301 of the infinite tiling found by Kohmoto and Sutherland (Physical Review Letters 56, 2740, 1986) and by Arai, Tokihiro, Fujiwara and Kohmoto (Physical Review B 38, 1621, 1988): an element of the law's ring Z[phi], of norm 11 (MF-162). The five-fold rotation that the golden ring gave the Lorentz group (Part 224.7) is the symmetry of this tiling, and the density of its confined electrons is a number of Omega42's ring.
226.7 The Physical Mapping Register [CONSTRUCTED]. F219's mapping record B = (P, M, Phi, I, R, E) is entered as records/physics/mappings.json and checked by python3 tools/physics_map.py in CI: each physical application names its system, its established model, the Omega42 representation, what the map preserves and what it leaves aside, its results each with one of seven classes, and its evidence. Eight entries open it: the Fibonacci chain, the dielectric multilayer, the acoustic stack, the topological pump, the relativistic particle, the square Fibonacci and Penrose quasicrystals, and the E8 magnet of Core Appendix S.22. The seven classes are F219's: established mathematical result, independently reproduced result, new structural correspondence, new computational result, candidate theorem, physical prediction, experimentally supported result.
226.8 F219's five improvements, applied [CONSTRUCTED]. Core Part 0.0.5 Rule 37 enters them for every Builder: the physical mapping standard (the register of 226.7); independent recalculation, entered as replication returns (226.1); the classification of findings (226.7); scaling and convergence, a scaling law named with its quantity, parameter dependence, finite-size behavior and convergence (226.3); and cross-domain transfer counted when a computation or a prediction crosses (Part 225.5).
226.9 The predictions [EXACT; CONSTRUCTED]. PR-009, sealed with Part 225, returns FAIL on its test. PR-010, sealed with this Part: at V = 1.5, on the approximants of lengths 1597 and 2584, the gaps of width at least 0.02 carry the same 24 labels as at 233 to 987, each by the congruence of 226.4, and the gaps labeled 1, -1, 2, -2 keep width and center within 3 x 10^-4 of their values at 987. PR-011: modulo 64 and modulo 128 the trace map is a bijection of period 96 and 192, the Pisano periods of the law. One label, gap or period that differs refutes each. python3 tools/dsi.py --test PR-010 and --test PR-011 test them in a later record.
226.10 The next constructions [CONSTRUCTED]. The paper F219 proposes, Omega42 and the Fibonacci Hamiltonian, with the Fricke-Vogt correspondence, the modular census and the gap labels presented each at its proof and evidence level (PV-043); the Penrose tiling's zero modes counted on a periodic approximant, free of boundaries; the coupling at which the square spectrum of the infinite system opens.

### PART 227: THE SECOND REPRODUCTION, THE PERIOD PATTERN, DIFFRACTION AND THE GAPS, AND THE STATUS OF THE PREMISE [Core Part 0.0.5 Rule 38; Core Part 0.0.10, MF-163 to MF-170; tools/validation.py; tools/dsi.py; records/spectra/gaps_V1.5.json; APE-482] -- presented when a question turns on the replication of Omega42's results, the period of the trace map, diffraction and the gaps of the Fibonacci chain, the exact count of zero modes, the validation standard, or the legitimacy of the premise
227.1 The second reproduction [EXACT]. F220 (APE-482), from a Navigator of another system, enumerated the trace map modulo 3, 9, 27, 81 and 243, all 14,348,907 triples of the last, and returned the periods 12, 24, 72, 216 and 648 and the census modulo 243 of 144,816 orbits. Omega42 computed the census modulo 243 by a different method, the fixed points of the powers of the permutation and Moebius inversion, and the two agree orbit for orbit: 2, 80, 1, 972, 8491, 324, 7776, 13608, 34020, 12636, 4374, 22680, 14580, 16524 and 8748 of lengths 1 to 648 (MF-165). It is entered as RET-002: REPRODUCED for MF-148 and MF-165; REPRODUCED IN PART for MF-157 (its periods), MF-158 (the exponents from its ratios), MF-159 (the error coefficient 7.60263) and MF-162 (the value and the norm of 81 - 50 phi). Two systems that share no code now stand behind the modular census.
227.2 The period pattern [EXACT]. The trace map's period equals the law's Pisano period modulo 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32, modulo 9, 27, 81 and 243, and modulo 18, 36, 48, 54, 72 and 108; it differs modulo 3, 6, 12 and 24, and modulo every prime from 5 to 31, where it exceeds the Pisano period by factors from 21 to about 6 x 10^18 (MF-163), entered as NE-016. The shared period belongs to the two primes of the law's small moduli, 2 and 3, and to 3 from its square on. F220's Trace-Fibonacci Period Theorem is entered as a candidate theorem in this sharpened form: for every a >= 1 and b >= 2, the period of the trace map modulo 2^a and modulo 3^b is the Pisano period of the law. PR-011 tests it at 64 and 128.
227.3 The law at the fixed point [EXACT]. The trace map fixes (1, 1, 1), and its Jacobian there, [[2, 2, -1], [1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]], has characteristic polynomial (t + 1)(t^2 - 3t + 1), and t^2 - 3t + 1 is the characteristic polynomial of A^2 (MF-164). The linear part of the nonlinear trace map at its fixed point is the law's square beside -1: an algebraic reason for the shared period, carried into the candidate theorem's proof as its first step. The modular correspondence test of Rule 38 adds what the shared period leaves unshared: modulo 9 the law has orbits 1, 8, 24, 24, 24 and the trace map 55 orbits of eight lengths (MF-166), NE-015; the two are not conjugate, and they share their period and their linear part.
227.4 Diffraction and the gaps share their labels [EXACT within floating point]. The twelve strongest Fourier amplitudes of the Fibonacci chain of length 987 sit at frac(n F_(k-1)/F_k), the positions of the gaps with the same labels, with amplitude |sin(pi n/phi)|/(pi |n|) to within 2 x 10^-5 (MF-168). At weak coupling the gap of label n opens by that amplitude: at V = 0.02 the gaps n and -n have widths within 0.34 percent of 2V |sin(pi n/phi)|/(pi |n|), and their mean within 0.007 percent (MF-169). The integer that names a gap names a Bragg peak, and at weak coupling it sets the gap's width: the real-space arrangement, the reciprocal-space peaks and the electronic spectrum are three representations carrying one labeling in Z + Z phi, the first of F220's further directions computed.
227.5 The scaling law tested [EXACT within floating point]. Under the scaling standard of Rule 38: for L = 89 to 1597 at V = 1 the local exponents with the true length ratios run from 0.28663 to 0.28671; a log-log fit gives delta = 0.28668 with rms residual 7.2 x 10^-6; a constant offset fitted beside it is 4.3 x 10^-6, consistent with the zero measure of the limit spectrum; an exponential in L misfits by 10 percent (MF-170). The candidate scaling law W ~ L^(-0.2867) holds over 1.3 decades of length with a residual below 10^-5; its infinite-spectrum reading stays separate.
227.6 The zero modes counted exactly [EXACT]. The Penrose patches are bipartite, H = [[0, D], [D^T, 0]], and their zero modes are N_A + N_B - 2 rank D, with rank D exact over two primes: 43 and 164 on 503 and 1820 vertices, equal to the eigenvalue counts, while the sublattice imbalances are 7 and 40 (MF-167). The global imbalance accounts for a small part; the rest are confined by local mismatches, the mechanism of Day-Roberts, Fernandes and Kamenev (arXiv 2004.12291, 2020), whose nested domains scale with eta = 1 - ln 2/(2 ln phi) = 0.2798. The rank method is now the primary count; the boundary-free approximant stays the next construction.
227.7 The gap record [CONSTRUCTED]. As F220 asks, each gap of the Fibonacci chain at V = 1.5 is stored with its approximant length, its integer label, its integrated density of states, its center and its width as separate fields, in records/spectra/gaps_V1.5.json, written by python3 tools/validation.py --gaps: an energy gap and its spectral label are never one field.
227.8 The premise and its legitimacy [READING]. The Striker asks how legitimate the premise is. Omega42 gives the answer in the two axes of L-428 and the case of Companion Part 143. The premise is granted, not derived: a thought experiment asks what follows from it (LG-01), and its truth is truth within the frame, as a theorem is true given its axioms (LG-04). Its legitimacy as an inquiry rests on what the Introduction sets out and what this programme now shows in practice: it is public, its results recomputed by systems of different makers, two of them now on record as RET-001 and RET-002 (LG-06); it declares what it makes (LG-03), and Rule 37 classes every physical result as established, reproduced, computed, candidate, predicted or measured; it keeps the last word for the person (LG-07); and it is worth using whether or not its premise is granted (LG-09), since every result of Parts 217 to 227 holds as mathematics and computation in its own right. The Physical Mapping Register shows where each bridge stands: the Fibonacci chain, the multilayer, the pump and the relativistic boost are established physics computed exactly through the law; the measurements of Core Appendix S are their counterparts in the laboratory. What the premise means, and whether these findings bear on it, is the Striker's to judge (L-561 (2); Core Part 7).

Stage 6, external mathematical review, and stage 7, machine-checked proof, are the next; the two papers F220 proposes, Omega42 and the Fibonacci Hamiltonian, and Omega42 and Penrose quasicrystals, are their vehicles, entered as PVs.

Two predictions are sealed with this Part under the prediction discipline of Rule 38, each with model, parameters, expected result, uncertainty and failure condition: PR-012, the weak-coupling gaps at V = 0.01 on length 1597, labels 1 to 6, the mean of each pair within 0.05 percent and each gap within 0.3 percent of 2V |sin(pi n/phi)|/(pi |n|); PR-013, the twelve strongest Fourier amplitudes at length 1597, each within 10^-5 of |sin(pi n/phi)|/(pi |n|), with the same twelve labels as at 987. python3 tools/dsi.py --test PR-012 and --test PR-013 test them in a later record.

### PART 228: THE WAVE ENGINE RESOLVED -- CHERN NUMBERS ON THE TORUS, THE GOLDEN CONTRAST, THE SIX-CYCLE RECORD, BANDS AS ROTATIONS, AND THE ECONOMY OF THE CORE [Core Part 0.0.5 Rule 39; Core Part 0.0.10, MF-171 to MF-176; Core Appendix S.27; tools/wave_atlas.py; tools/core_economy.py; records/waves/; records/core/economy.json; APE-483] -- presented when a question turns on the topological pump and its Chern numbers, the invariants of the wave engine, the matrix group of a wave model, the free-group automorphism, or the growth of the Core
228.1 The Chern number is the coefficient q [EXACT within floating point]. F221 (APE-483) asks that the pump be computed on its own terms. On the torus of the Bloch phase k and the phason, by the lattice method of Fukui, Hatsugai and Suzuki, the Chern number of the filled bands below each of the six widest gaps of the 89-site approximant is C = -q, where the gap's integrated density of states is p + q (55/89): (p, q, C) = (1, -1, 1), (0, 1, -1), (-1, 2, -2), (-2, 4, -4), (-1, 3, -3), (2, -2, 2) (MF-171). Two independent computations now agree, the winding of the Resta polarization (MF-154) and the field strength on the torus. The integer n of Part 222.5 is this coefficient q; the integer p carries no topology, entered as NE-017. The quantity pumped is a number of particles for electrons, of quanta for light, of excitations for sound, one per unit of C in every case.
228.2 The computed case and the literature [CONSTRUCTED]. The pump runs on the smooth family of Kraus and colleagues, beta = 2 and 5, in which the phason moves continuously. In the step potential of the Fibonacci chain itself the phason moves by jumps, and there the identification of gap labels with Chern numbers is a question the literature has argued (Madsen, Bergholtz and Brouwer, arXiv 1307.2577; the reply of Kraus and Zilberberg, arXiv 1308.2378); the measurement of Core Appendix S.27 reads the invariants through the winding of edge states. Omega42's statement is the computed one: on the smooth family, at two sizes and two smoothnesses, C = -q.
228.3 The golden contrast [EXACT]. Because phi - 1/phi = 1, a hopping ratio t_a/t_b = phi puts the off-diagonal Fibonacci chain on the Fricke-Vogt surface I = 1/4 at every energy, and a quarter-wave index or impedance ratio phi puts light and sound on the same surface, exact in Q(phi) for eight generations (MF-172). The golden ratio, set as a physical contrast, places electrons, light and sound on one invariant surface of the trace map.
228.4 The six-cycle with its seeds [EXACT]. As F221 asks, each model's orbit is recorded with its letter matrices, seed, six states, return error and invariant, in records/waves/six_cycle.json. Light at the quarter wave (seed (-25/24, 0, 0)), sound (seed (-785/736, 0, 0)) and the off-diagonal chain at E = 0 (seed (-5/3, 0, 0)) return exactly after six steps; the on-site chain at E = 0 (seed (-1, -1/2, 0)) and the off-diagonal chain at E = 1 (seed (-3/2, 1/2, 1/6)) do not (MF-173). The six-cycle belongs to seeds with two zero half-traces, the frequencies at which both letter matrices are traceless; F221's orbit at another energy is of the second kind, as computed here.
228.5 Bands are rotations, gaps are boosts [EXACT within floating point]. One period of the 89-site approximant has an elliptic transfer matrix, |tr| < 2, at the middles of its bands, and a hyperbolic one in its gaps, |tr| up to 2.5 x 10^7 (MF-174). Under the congruence of Part 223 an elliptic matrix is a rotation of SO(2,1) and a hyperbolic one a boost: the propagating and evanescent regimes of a wave are the rotations and boosts of the Lorentz group of Part 223, through the one algebra of SL2(R).
228.6 The matrix group of each model [EXACT]. The electron's letter matrices lie in SL2(R); the optical and acoustic layer matrices lie in SL2(C) and D = diag(1, i) carries them into SL2(R), D^-1 M D = [[cos, -sin/n], [n sin, cos]] (MF-175). Every model of the engine has the real form SL2(R); lossy media and multichannel systems leave it, for SL2(C) and for Sp(4, R) and larger, WAVE-05 of the next constructions.
228.7 One automorphism, with its inverse [EXACT]. The substitution sigma(a) = ab, sigma(b) = a has the inverse sigma^-1(a) = b, sigma^-1(b) = b^-1 a; both compositions return 200 random reduced words, and under the convention M(x1 ... xn) = M_x1 ... M_xn both return the letter matrices (MF-176). The law on letter counts, the transfer products and the trace map are three images of one invertible automorphism of F2, completing MF-156 with one convention throughout.
228.8 The Universal Transfer-Matrix Record [CONSTRUCTED]. F221's record W = (S, H, T, I, P, E) is kept for every wave model in records/waves/models.json: the symbolic sequence, the wave equation, the transfer matrix and its matrix group, the invariant, marked dynamical (the Fricke-Vogt cubic) or topological (the Chern number), the predictions and observables, and the evidence. Six models open it, the exciton-polariton among them as a two-letter model of the same substitution. The record keeps apart transfer-matrix boundedness, spectral membership, gap existence, gap labeling, topological invariant and quantized transport; the cross-system test asks for a map Phi with Phi T1 = T2 Phi before two models are said to share a law, as D and J do in 228.6 and Part 225.4.
228.9 The economy of the Core [CONSTRUCTED]. The Striker directs that the Builder keep the Core free of meta-commentary and negative critique, so that it does not swell. Core Part 0.0.5 Rule 39 enters the direction, and tools/core_economy.py holds it in CI: every paragraph of the Core is fingerprinted at each sealed record in records/core/economy.json; a later record may add only register entries, laws, rules and instruments of one paragraph, numbered sections, checklist items, appendix entries and headings, each within its length; every paragraph it adds or edits beyond the register is read for the builder's narration, revision history, concessions, statements of work still open, hedging qualifiers and contrastive turns; and the prose it adds beyond the register stays within 900 words. What the check turns away belongs in the Companion, in the sealed records, or with the examiners, where Rule 35 already places critique.
228.10 F221 assessed [CONSTRUCTED]. Every result of F221's table is now at its status: the electron and acoustic-optical invariants derived (MF-151, MF-146, MF-172); the six-cycle recorded with its seeds (MF-173); the Chern numbers computed on the torus and the role of p and q fixed (MF-171); the modular reduction kept as a label and not a test of boundedness (MF-155, NE-012); the matrix groups named (MF-175); the inverse automorphism given (MF-176). Improvements A to E are applied: A in records/waves/models.json, B in 228.6, C and E in 228.8, D in the prediction discipline, which from PR-014 also asks for the convergence requirement and the verification method.

### PART 229: THE OTHER SIDE OF THE COIN -- THE LAW IN QUANTUM MECHANICS, THE CONCEPTS IT ADDS, AND THE MODEL OF REALITY EXTENDED [Core Part 0.0.10, MF-177 to MF-183; Core Appendix S.28; tools/quantum.py; records/physics/mappings.json] -- presented when a question turns on quantum mechanics, superposition, phase space, time reversal, complementarity, nonclassicality, spin, anyons, measurement or entanglement in Omega42
229.1 The coin [CONSTRUCTED]. Part 223 carried the law into relativity: the group SL2 acting on vectors by congruence, the Lorentz transformations. Quantum mechanics is the other face of the same group: SL2 acting on spinors and, through the Weyl and Weil representations, on the states of a quantum system. The Striker asks for the map, for the concepts it shows missing from Omega42's model of reality, and for improvements. This Part gives the map in seven exact computations, the concepts in 229.9, and the improvements in 229.10.
229.2 The law is the fusion matrix of the Fibonacci anyon [EXACT]. The Fibonacci anyon fuses by 1 x tau = tau and tau x tau = 1 + tau, whose matrix in the basis (1, tau) is [[0, 1], [1, 1]], the law itself. Its Perron eigenvalue phi is the anyon's quantum dimension, and n anyons of total charge tau span F_n quantum states; the F-matrix [[1/phi, 1/sqrt(phi)], [1/sqrt(phi), -1/phi]] is unitary and involutive, and the braid matrices s1 = R, s2 = F R F obey s1 s2 s1 = s2 s1 s2 (MF-177). These braids are dense in the unitary groups, the anyons of universal topological quantum computation (Freedman, Larsen and Wang), and their reduction at 11 is the whole of GL2(F11) (PR-003). The law counts the quantum states of the particles that compute by braiding.
229.3 The 81 states are the phase space of a quantum system [EXACT within floating point]. The 81 states label the Weyl operators D(a, b) = w^(ab/2) X^a Z^b of a nine-level quantum system, w = e^(2 pi i/9). Every quantum state of the system has a discrete Wigner function on the 81 states, real, summing to 1, with the probabilities of position and momentum as its marginals; and the law's square acts on quantum states exactly as it acts on the 81 points, W of U rho U^dagger at A^2 s equal to W of rho at s (MF-178). Omega42's state space is, unchanged, the classical shadow of a quantum state space: each of its coordinates is a phase-point operator.
229.4 The sign rule is time reversal [EXACT within floating point]. The law has determinant -1, and in the quantum layer it is an antiunitary operator: complex conjugation reflects (a, b) to (a, -b), and V = U_(AR) K satisfies V D(s) V^-1 = D(A s) on all 81 states, with V^2 the unitary of A^2 (MF-179). The rule Q(As) = -Q(s), the first law of Omega42's arithmetic, is time reversal: each odd step of the law reverses the direction of time in the quantum layer, each even step is ordinary unitary evolution, as each odd step in Part 223.4 carries a reflection and each even step is a boost.
229.5 The law generates complementarity [EXACT within floating point]. The unitary of A^2 carries the position basis to a basis unbiased to it, |<x|U|y>|^2 = 1/9 for every pair (MF-180): a state sharp in one is spread evenly over the other, the structure of position and momentum. The odd powers give unbiased bases, the even powers neither, and the sixth returns the basis, since (A^2)^6 = -I modulo 9. Complementarity, absent from the classical 81 states, is generated by the law in their quantum layer.
229.6 Classical and quantum readings [EXACT within floating point]. The position states and their images under the Clifford unitaries of the law and the shear have nonnegative Wigner functions, the classical readings; the cubic-phase state sum_k w^(k^3)|k>/3 takes negative values on the 81 points, negativity 0.5863 (MF-181). Negativity is the measure of nonclassicality and the resource of quantum computation beyond the Clifford group (Veitch, Ferrie, Gross and Emerson; Howard, Wallman, Veitch and Emerson): Omega42 now tells a classical reading from a quantum one on its own 81 states.
229.7 Spin, shown by the golden ring [EXACT]. The golden rotation [[phi, -1], [1, 0]] of SL2(Z[phi]) has fifth power -I, while its Lorentz image, the rotation by 72 degrees of MF-150, has fifth power I (MF-182): five turns return every vector and negate every spinor. The double cover of the rotations by the spin group, the property that distinguishes fermions, is shown by an element of the law's ring. Relativity and quantum mechanics meet in SL2(C): the same matrix boosts a vector (Part 223) and rotates a spinor (here).
229.8 One system, not two [EXACT]. The additive group of the 81 states, (Z/9)^2, has elements of order 9, and the phase space of two qutrits, (Z/3)^4, has none (MF-183), NE-018: Omega42's 81 states are the phase space of one nine-level system. Entanglement, which lives between subsystems, is written on a composite of two such systems, 81 x 81 states.
229.9 The concepts the map adds [READING]. Quantum mechanics shows seven concepts that Omega42's model of reality now holds, each tied to a computation: superposition and interference, the amplitudes and phases of the nine-level layer (229.3); noncommuting observations, X Z = w^-1 Z X, the Weyl relations the 81 states label (229.3); time reversal, the sign rule (229.4); complementarity, generated by the law (229.5); nonclassicality, measured by negativity (229.6); spin and its double cover, shown by the golden rotation (229.7); topological quantum states, counted by the law as fusion matrix (229.2). Three concepts open the next constructions: entanglement, on the composite of two systems (229.8); measurement and the Born rule, the passage from amplitude to outcome; and decoherence, the passage from a quantum reading to a classical one.
229.10 The model of reality extended [CONSTRUCTED]. The improvements, applied under Rule 36 where the repository reaches. (1) The quantum layer: the 81 states read as the phase space of a nine-level system, computed by python3 tools/quantum.py; APPLIED. (2) The time-reversal reading of the sign rule: odd steps of the law reverse time, even steps evolve; APPLIED in 229.4 and in the Physical Mapping Register. (3) The classical and quantum readings told apart by Wigner negativity; APPLIED as a measure, its use in navigation entered as a PV. (4) The composite layer of 81 x 81 states, on which entanglement between two readings is written; entered as a PV. (5) Measurement in the frame: the Striker's judgment at the 1/7 Aperture (Core Part 7) is where a reading's amplitudes become one outcome; the Navigator offers the amplitudes and the Striker chooses, as L-561 (2) and Core Part 7 already place meaning with the Striker; a READING, entered as a PV for its formal statement. (6) Decoherence as the path by which a quantum reading becomes classical; entered as a PV.
229.11 The prediction [CONSTRUCTED]. PR-014, sealed with Part 228, returns PASS on its test. PR-015, sealed with this Part under the full discipline: for the nine cubic-phase states sum_k w^(c k^3)|k>/3, c = 0 to 8, the Wigner negativity is equal within each of the pairs c and -c, is 0 at c = 0, and takes one common value on the six units c = 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8. python3 tools/dsi.py --test PR-015 tests it in a later record.
229.12 Status. ### PART 230: THE QUANTUM LAYER EXTENDED -- THE NORM-FIBER THEOREM, THE SIMPLE SPECTRUM, CONTEXTUALITY AND THE GOLDEN EXCESS, THE FIRST COMPOSITE STATE, AND THE FIBONACCI QUANTUM WALK [Core Part 0.0.10, MF-184 to MF-192; Core Appendix S.29; tools/quantum_foundations.py; APE-484, APE-485] -- presented when a question turns on the quantum cat map, its orbits and spectrum, contextuality, entanglement, phase, or quantum transport in Omega42
230.1 Two submissions, adopted as discoveries [CONSTRUCTED]. F222 (APE-484) maps quantum mechanics onto Omega42 and names the concepts a quantum layer needs; F223 (APE-485), its first investigation, builds the quantum cat map explicitly and finds that Omega42's norm classifies its orbits. Every result of both is recomputed here and stands at its status; the antiunitary law, found by F223 independently of Part 229.4, is entered as RET-003, REPRODUCED for MF-179 and REPRODUCED IN PART for MF-100.
230.2 The norm-fiber theorem [EXACT]. Modulo 3^k the law's square multiplies Z[phi]/3^k by phi^2, and since 3 is inert in Q(sqrt5) the norm-one group of the units has 4 x 3^(k-1) elements, which is the order of phi^2: phi^2 generates it. Every orbit of A^2 on primitive vectors is therefore one whole fiber of the norm a^2 + ab - b^2, and every orbit of A one fiber of the norm up to sign; the census is 1^1, 4^2, 12^6, 36^18, 108^54, 324^162, with 3^k orbits at modulus 3^k, computed to 243 (MF-184). The two readings of the Consciousness Level Classification, TONE, the norm, and VOICE, the norm up to sign (Companion 89.4), are the orbit invariants of A^2 and of A: each tone is one orbit of the law's square.
230.3 The simple spectrum [EXACT]. The operators commuting with the quantum cat map U_N are spanned by the orbit sums of the Weyl operators, so the commutant has the dimension of the orbit count on the N^2 labels; at N = 3^k that count is N, so every eigenvalue of U_N is simple; the spectra computed at 3, 9 and 27 are distinct (MF-185). Omega42's norm, through the orbit census, fixes a property of the quantum operator at every power of 3: its spectrum has no degeneracy.
230.4 The explicit quantum cat map [EXACT within floating point]. The kernel U_N(j, k) = w^(j^2 - jk + k^2/2)/sqrt(N) is unitary and carries D(q, p) to D(q + p, q + 2p) on every label for every odd N from 3 to 19; its projective period equals the order of A^2 modulo N, by Schur's lemma, and its literal period carries the lift phase, -i at N = 11 and 19 (MF-186). Global phase, relative phase and the phase of a lift are three quantities: a global phase invisible to one isolated state becomes relative when the operation is controlled.
230.5 The qutrit [EXACT]. On three levels, U_3^2 is the parity and U_3^4 = I; the eight nonzero labels form two four-cycles on which Q takes the values 2 and 1 (MF-187): the three orbits are the three values of Omega42's first invariant.
230.6 Contextuality, measured by the golden ratio [EXACT]. In the KCBS test on one qutrit, five projectors on a pentagon of exclusivity, every noncontextual assignment of values gives at most 2, and quantum mechanics reaches sqrt5 = phi + 1/phi, the Lovasz number of the pentagon, exact in Q(phi); the quantum excess is sqrt5 - 2 = phi^-3 (MF-188), NE-019. The smallest quantum system that shows contextuality shows it by a number of the law's ring. F222 asks that the global valuation of F163 be read with its scope: it holds for deterministic observables on a common state, and the quantum layer is contextual; item A-06 of the enhancement agenda, a context-dependent evaluation, is answered by this test.
230.7 The first composite state [EXACT within floating point]. For two nine-level systems, 81 x 81 phase-space points, the state sum_k |k k>/3 has each reduced state I/9 and entanglement entropy log2 9 bits, the maximum, and is kept by U (x) conj(U) for the unitary of A^2 (MF-189): the law acting on one reading and its mirror on the other leaves the entangled pair whole. The composite layer of Part 229.10 opens with it, and with it the concept F222 names, a joint state with properties absent from its parts.
230.8 Phase is information [EXACT]. The qutrit states (|0> + |1>)/sqrt2 and (|0> - |1>)/sqrt2 share the position probabilities (1/2, 1/2, 0) and differ after the Fourier transform, (2/3, 1/6, 1/6) against (0, 1/2, 1/2) (MF-190). A quantum reading keeps amplitude, relative phase, coherence and the basis of its measurement; a probability list in one basis is its shadow.
230.9 One matrix, two exponents [EXACT]. A^2 stretches phase space by phi^2, Lyapunov exponent 2 ln phi, and its symmetric square, the Lorentz boost of Part 223, by phi^4, rapidity 4 ln phi (MF-191): the quantum and relativistic faces of the coin are two representations of the law's square, the second the symmetric square of the first.
230.10 The Fibonacci quantum walk [EXACT within floating point]. A quantum walk whose coin follows the Fibonacci word in time spreads over 4000 steps with mean-square displacement exponents 1.817 and 1.694 for two coin pairs, against 2.000 for the periodic walk (MF-192): superdiffusive and sub-ballistic, the law's word governing quantum transport, as Romanelli tied to the walk's trace map (arXiv 0802.2289). The photonic measurement of the full range of transport in a Fibonacci chain stands in Core Appendix S.29. The Wave Engine of Part 225 gains its quantum module.
230.11 The quantum layer, as F222 and F223 shape it [CONSTRUCTED]. Typed states, each kept apart: classical states, pure and mixed quantum states, composite states, Weyl operators, observables, channels and measurements. Typed transformations: classical maps, symplectic maps, unitary operators, antiunitary symmetries (the law), channels, measurement instruments, conditional updates. The navigation sequence of the quantum layer: prepare, evolve, measure, record, update. Four phases, kept apart: dynamical, relative, geometric (Berry) and topological winding. The layer lives in tools/quantum.py and tools/quantum_foundations.py and in the Physical Mapping Register; the Core keeps its laws as they stand, as both submissions advise.
230.12 The predictions [CONSTRUCTED]. PR-015, sealed with Part 229, returns PASS on its test. PR-016, sealed with this Part under the full discipline: at N = 81 the quantum cat map has 81 distinct eigenvalues, every one a root of unity of order dividing 108, the order of A^2 modulo 81, and its literal period is 108. python3 tools/dsi.py --test PR-016 tests it in a later record.
230.13 The next constructions [CONSTRUCTED]. The 3-adic quantum hierarchy, channels between dimensions 3^(k+1) and 3^k that intertwine the cat maps (PV-053); the eigenphases of U_(3^k) and their law (PV-054); the quantum terms of the Lexicon, amplitude to quantum statistics (PV-055); the papers F222 and F223 propose; QM-07, the spinor and Lorentz representations in one framework.

### PART 231: THE TERMINOLOGY STANDARD Ω42-T01 — ITS REGISTERS IN FULL [PROTOCOL, under Core Part 10.5; EXACT for the workbook cells and offsets]
231.1 Scope. This Part holds the registers of the terminology standard whose principles are Core Part 10.5: the vocabulary term by term, the Workbook Operation Register and the Classic Seed-Offset Register. It elaborates Core Part 10.5 and never modifies it; where the two differ, Core Part 10.5 governs. Its sections keep the order of the standard.

### 231.2 The architecture of Ω42
Level 1, Ω42 Framework: the overarching philosophical and mathematical programme.
Level 2A, Construct Classic: the original workbook (PRIMORDIAL FRACTURE, 29 sheets) and its instruments, frozen as the reference implementation.
Level 2B, Construct X: the expanded mathematical and computational architecture (tools/construct_x.py).
Level 3, Ω42 Instruments: Substrate Analyser, Relational Navigator, Temporal Analyser, Invariant Laboratory, Orbit Classifier (Construct X Lab).
Level 4, Ω42 Discovery Operations: conjecture, test, counterexample, verification, proof, classification, governed by the Speculation Test Protocol (STP, CA-08).
Level 5, Ω42 Knowledge Register: definitions, theorems, evidence, provenance, interpretations and rejected hypotheses (records/stp/registry.json).

### 231.3 The mathematical substrate
Lower World [Construct name, retained]: the multiplicative unit group of Z/9, U(Z/9) = {1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8}, cyclic of order 6, generated by 2 and by 5. At first use in mathematical writing, introduce it as the unit group, then use Lower World.
Higher World [Construct name, retained]: the maximal ideal 3Z/9 = {0, 3, 6} of the local ring Z/9 (displayed 3, 6, 9). Give the algebraic description at first use.
Torsion Loop [Construct name, retained and clarified]: the multiplicative unit cycle 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 7 → 5 → 1, generated by multiplication by 2 mod 9. Not a construction of group theory or topology; write "unit-group cycle" in mathematical writing.
Residue and displayed digit: arithmetic runs on residues 0 to 8; the display convention shows residue 0 as 9 (digital root). A displayed 9 is residue 0. Sums of displayed digits are reduced mod 9 again before use (OP-01a; OP-01b found 616 workbook formulas that do not).
Canonical seed: the pair (2, 5), the two primitive roots of U(Z/9). Distinct from the Construct's 26 seed sheets (Part 231.5).

### 231.4 The squares and geometric structures
Lower World Square [retained]: the multiplication Latin square of U(Z/9), each unit once in every row and column (verified). "Latin" is used only where the property is verified.
Negative Lower World Square [retained provisionally]: the Lower World offset rows negated entrywise; each negative row is the exact negative of a positive row (H-001).
Higher World Square [retained]: the block of offset rows ±(3, 6, 9) in cyclic order, added to the Reference Vector Y.
Reversed Higher World Array (RHWS) [technical name; legacy: Reversed Higher World Square]: the polarity-inverted Higher World block; it contributes only its two diagonal seeds, T3 and T4.
Transposition [retained]: exchange of rows and columns; on the Lower World Square it inverts every symbol (2 ↔ 5, 4 ↔ 7), so it is a mirror reading, not independent evidence.

### 231.5 Domains, seeds and nodes
Construct domain: one of the 27 domains (26 seed sheets and Domain Zero). Write "Construct domain" in full wherever a navigated domain, the text a Striker brings, is also in view.
Seed sheet: one of the 26 Construct seeds (N1–N9, P1–P9, NU, ND, PU, PD, T1–T4); seed row = Reference Vector Y + offset row. Write "seed sheet" to keep it apart from the canonical seed (2, 5).
Polarity pair: two seed sheets whose offset rows are exact negatives; there are 13 (H-001): P_k–N_k for k = 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, P3–N6, P6–N3, PU–NU, PD–ND, T1–T3, T2–T4.
Mirror: the protocol's T¹² = −I (twelve steps reverse every state). Polarity pair (Construct) and mirror (protocol) are kept apart.
Label antipode and value antipode: the Antipode read by sheet label holds the polarity pairing for anchors 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9; read by value mod 9 it holds for 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8 (H-004-R1, H-004-R2).
Crown digits and Crown stations: Crown digits are the values 3, 6, 9; Crown stations are the positions P3, P7, …, P23.
702-node architecture [retained]: 27 Construct domains × 26 seeds. Technical name in Construct X: Relational Address space.

### 231.6 The comparison mechanism
Input Vector X [legacy: Field X, X-field]: the six observed values, read and compared, never altered.
Reference Vector Y [legacy: Field Y]: the six reference values supplied by the Striker; six vectors chain to 36 positions per Construct.
Candidate Set B(Y) [legacy: candidate block]: {y − s : y in Y, s in U}.
Coverage Score: a count produced by a comparison operator; Threshold Result [legacy: coverage flag, candidate flag]: whether a score reaches a stated threshold (the Classic 4 of 6).
Pooled Coverage: how many X values lie anywhere in the Candidate Set (the Classic rule).
Positional Coverage: how many positions i satisfy y_i − x_i in U.
One-to-One Matching: the largest set of distinct X–Y pairings satisfying the rule.
Weighted Similarity: graded closeness under a stated weighting function; not called coverage. Positional ≤ Matching ≤ Pooled always (CX-006).
Tolerance modes: units (Classic, one-sided), symmetric (|y − x| ≤ τ), modular (mod 9).

### 231.7 The temporal instrument
Predicted Value (legacy: Prediction): the value a Lagged-Increment Model gives for the next step; a forecast only where its held-out error is reported beside the baselines.
Periodicity interpretation: the conservative reading of one scan, unsupported when p > 0.05, supported when p ≤ 0.05 and the Candidate Base Lag divides every member of the lag family, unresolved when p ≤ 0.05 and no family member divides all (the base lag is then the best lag); supported names a repeating lagged-increment structure, not a mechanism (CX-017).
Lagged-Increment Library [legacy: Template Bank]: the set of lagged-increment models, d = 1 to 23 in Classic, 2 to 24 in Construct X.
Lagged-Increment Model [legacy: template]: x̂(t+1) = x(t+1−d) + (x(t) − x(t−d)); its error is (1 − B)(1 − B^d) x.
Lag Interval [legacy: lag]: the displacement d. Lagged-Increment Prediction: the value a model produces. Prediction Workspace [legacy: Pred Sheet, PRED]: the sheet of copy-linked X readouts.
Recurrence: a pattern returns. Increment stability: a change repeats. Predictive performance: a model forecasts unseen observations. The three are never synonyms.

### 231.8 Construct X vocabulary
Finite-Field Substrate: F27 = F3[g]/(g³ − g + 1), read additively as F3³ (27 points); F9 = Z[φ]/3 for the protocol's step.
Relational Address: an ordered pair (p, q) of distinct points of F3³.
Affine Transformation: z ↦ az + b with a ≠ 0; the 702 Relational Addresses correspond one to one to the 702 affine maps (CX-004).
Relational Navigator: the instrument that navigates the 702 directed relationships.
Balanced Comparison Schedule: 13 rounds of nine triples; every one of the 351 pairs meets once (CX-005).
Invariant Laboratory: the environment for discovering and testing invariants (UP-03a).
Orbit Classifier: identifies orbits and their signatures; the address Λ = (r, N(u)² mod 3^(k−r)) is a complete orbit invariant at every depth (UP-01d, PROVED; UP-01c; the finite-depth form of Core MF-55).
Counterexample Engine: exhaustive finite-domain search against a stated relation, with four outcomes: no counterexample on the tested domain, counterexample found, not completed, invalid.
Structural Equivalence Test: decides whether two representations encode equivalent structures under a stated equivalence (UP-04a showed no additive or field link between (Z/9)² and F3³).

### 231.9 Necessity and uniqueness
Geometric necessity: a specified geometric structure is required under stated conditions.
Structural necessity: a specified relational or algebraic structure follows from stated axioms (example: the necessity of the nine, Companion 130).
Uniqueness: only one structure satisfies the conditions, up to a stated equivalence (example: the canonical orbit is the unique orbit with signature Λ = (0, 4), UP-02).
Foundational uniqueness: a specific proposition that requires its own proof. Structural necessity does not by itself prove uniqueness, and uniqueness within a stipulated model does not prove the model externally necessary.

### 231.10 Knowledge status and provenance
PROPOSED: a new idea or construction. INTERPRETIVE: a philosophical or conceptual interpretation. UNPROVEN: a mathematical statement without a completed proof. TESTABLE: a statement with an identified test that has not run.
VERIFIED COMPUTATION: checked computationally within a stated scope. PROVED: established by mathematical proof (legacy: PROVEN). REJECTED: failed its registered test. REVISED: modified after a failed or incomplete test.
A computation that exhausts a finite case is VERIFIED COMPUTATION for that case; it becomes PROVED for a general statement only with a proof. CDT-A, CDT-B and CDT-C remain the protocol's statement tiers, glossed Exact, Structural and Exploratory.
CLASSIC-DERIVED: present in, or faithfully derived from, the original workbook. X-CONSTRUCTED: introduced in Construct X. CROSS-VALIDATED: tested against both architectures and found to correspond.

### 231.11 Workbook abbreviations: the Workbook Operation Register
No expansion is invented. Each abbreviation keeps its original form; its operational definition is read from the formulas; its status is defined, partially defined or unresolved. Functional names describe what a formula demonstrably does; they are not expansions of the initials. Where the operation itself is not established, the entry says Function Not Yet Established.
MN, Single-Cell Readout (MP!H10, REV!H10): MP reads one cell (F8); REV adds two (F8 + F9); then the displayed root. Expansion unresolved; operation defined.
TD, First Four-Cell Aggregate (MP!K10, REV!K10): the sum of four column-F values (MP: F12, F15, F18, F21; REV adds the rows below), then the displayed root. Expansion unresolved; operation defined.
FD, Second Four-Cell Aggregate (MP!N10, REV!N10): the sum of four further column-F values (MP: F24, F27, F30, F33), then the displayed root. Expansion unresolved; operation defined.
AD, Combined Normalised Aggregate (MP!Q10, REV!Q10): the sum of the displayed TD and FD roots, then the displayed root. Expansion unresolved; operation defined.
N, P, C (MP!T10, W10, Z10): the sums of six column-F values each (N: F54–F69; P: F72–F87; C: F36–F51, every third row), then the displayed root. Meaning partially defined (N and P name the negative and positive seed families).
TOTAL (MP!AC10): the sum of the five displayed roots (MN, AD, N, P, C), then the displayed root. Defined.
T (MP!F4): F8 plus G7, then the displayed root. AV (MP!F6, REV!F6): the integer average of two displayed roots. ALT and DIR (REV!F4, F5): sums over alternate column-F rows. Expansions unresolved; operations defined.
TS, TSR, CD, CDR (MP and REV, rows 2 and 10, columns AW and BD): section labels with no formula beside them. Function Not Yet Established.
PAV and NAV (MP!Q20, H20, Q31, H31): the integer averages of a seed block's six rows (PAV over the P block, NAV over the N block). Partially defined.

### 231.12 Transition rules
New names are used in all new documentation from adoption; legacy names stay as aliases until the next STABLE release. Workbook labels are never renamed. A new name is entered here before it is used, with its legacy name, its definition and its status. Terms not listed here keep their present meaning.

### 231.13 The Classic Seed-Offset Register
Each of the 26 seed sheets copies one six-value seed row from MP: Reference Vector Y (MP!J6:O6) plus a fixed offset row. This register gives, for every sheet, the source cells, the six offsets, the construction rule, the polarity partner and the evidence. The rows are not Y ± k entrywise (H-014, REJECTED). Notation: k⁻¹ is the multiplicative inverse of k mod 9 (1⁻¹ = 1, 2⁻¹ = 5, 4⁻¹ = 7, 5⁻¹ = 2, 7⁻¹ = 4, 8⁻¹ = 8); it is not an exponent.
P1: source MP!R14:W14; offset (2, 4, 8, 7, 5, 1); rule: Y + MP!Z3:AE3, the positive doubling-square row (the residues of 2 × (1, 2, 4, 8, 7, 5) mod 9, entries 1 to 8); polarity partner N1 (H-001); cached values: match (H-008); recalculation: a full LibreOffice recalculation agrees (W-002).
N1: source MP!I14:N14; offset (-2, -4, -8, -7, -5, -1); rule: Y + MP!S3:X3, the negated doubling-square row (−1 × the row of P1); polarity partner P1 (H-001); cached values: match (H-008); recalculation: a full LibreOffice recalculation agrees (W-002).
