### 231.14 Names of the training guide and the review terms
Classic Seed-Sheet Set: the 26 seed sheets of the workbook. Classic Polarity Pairing: their 13 exact negation pairs (H-001). F27 Singer-Cycle Model: the 26 nonzero elements of F27 as powers of g, a Construct X construction. F27 Seed Labelling: the assignment of workbook labels to powers of g, a Construct X convention that preserves the Classic Polarity Pairing; it is not derived from the workbook's own formulas. F27 Affine Address Model: the 27-point, 702-relationship architecture.
F27 Singer-Cycle Generator: the scalar recurrence s(n+3) = s(n+1) − s(n) mod 3 from the initial state (s0, s1, s2) = (0, 0, 1). A seed is the state vector (s_n, s_{n+1}, s_{n+2}); the next seed is the state one step on. Change of coordinates to the polynomial basis of F3[g]/(g³ − g + 1): if g^n = c0 + c1 g + c2 g², then (s_n, s_{n+1}, s_{n+2}) = (c2, c1, c0 + c2) (checked for all 26 powers).
F9–F27 Singer-Cycle Correspondence: the shared pattern of a single multiplication visiting every nonzero element, in F9 (8 elements, the Ω42 Recurrence) and in F27 (26 elements, the Construct X directions). Status: structural analogy (CDT-B). F9 is not a subfield of F27 and no additive map from (Z/9)² covers F3³ (UP-04a).
Ω42 Recurrence: T(a, b) = (b, a + b). Ω42 Norm: N(a, b) = a² + ab − b². Polarity reversal (norm reversal): N(T x) = −N(x); residues mod 9 have no ordering, so "sign" is not used. Norm-Square Invariant: N², constant along every orbit.
Ω42 Quadratic-Extension Depth Tower: at depth k the Ω42 Recurrence acts on the two-coordinate module (Z/3^k)², represented as R_k = (Z/3^k)[φ]/(φ² − φ − 1), with T as multiplication by φ. R_1 = F9 is the residue field at the bottom of the tower; R_k for k ≥ 2 are local rings, not fields.
Complete Ω42 Orbit Signature Theorem: on (Z/3^k)², every nonzero state x = 3^r u with u a unit of R_(k−r) has signature Λ(x) = (r, N(u)² mod 3^(k−r)); two nonzero states lie on the same orbit of T exactly when their signatures agree; the zero state is its own fixed orbit. The theorem classifies orbits of T only, not other equivalences. Status: PROVED (Construct X specification, section 7); enumerations for k = 1 to 6: VERIFIED COMPUTATION (UP-01c).
Uniqueness, three propositions: Orbit Classification Uniqueness (one orbit has a given complete signature; the canonical orbit is the one with Λ = (0, 4), UP-02); Ω42 Axiom-Relative Uniqueness (one orbit satisfies the stated selection conditions K1 and K2, Core Part 1.8); Foundational Uniqueness (no non-equivalent structure satisfies the foundational requirements; requires its own argument and is not established by the orbit theorem).
Question-to-Address Mapping Rule: the specification that takes a question to a node of the F27 Affine Address Model. The Axis gives a reproducible coordinate (counts, CPP(n) = dr(5n), the anchor, Core Part 1.3). The rule is QAM-1, adopted by ESC (CA-14): the coordinate's position p on the canonical 24-cycle and the anchor k go to the seed P_k at even p and its workbook polarity partner at odd p, in the domain (a mod 3, b mod 3, k mod 3), where (a, b) is the canonical state at p. It is total and deterministic on all 216 readings and addresses 24 of the 27 domains (QA-01, QA-02); it is a labelling convention, not a structure-preserving map (UP-04a).
Transformation Composition-Consistency Test: checks whether observed transformations satisfy a proposed composition law on the tested data or state space. A failure may reflect a changed rule, noise, a wrong group, a misspecified transformation, too few observations, state dependence or an estimation error.
Near-optimal lag family: the lags whose training-set error is within a pre-registered tolerance (default 15%) of the best training-set error. Candidate Base Lag (Lag-Family Common Divisor): the smallest family lag that divides every family member; a summary, not a proof of the true period.
Six-Treatment Williams Crossover Schedule: six sequences in which every treatment appears once per period and every ordered pair of distinct treatments follows each other exactly once; it balances first-order carryover only. Generated by construct_x.williams_schedule(n) for every even n; the six-treatment table is checked by CX-016.
Engines and instruments: an engine is a computational component, an instrument the function a user employs. S Substrate Engine → Substrate Explorer; A Address Engine → Relational Navigator; C Comparison Engine → Comparison Laboratory; T Temporal Engine → Temporal Observatory; G Transformation Engine → Transformation Laboratory; V Verification Engine → Invariant and Verification Laboratory. A planned instrument is not described as implemented until it exists in the software.
Readiness of an application: MATHEMATICALLY ESTABLISHED (the property is proved); IMPLEMENTED (exists in a named software version); VALIDATED FOR APPLICATION (passed tests on relevant real data or tasks); EXPLORATORY (proposed or early).
Hypothesis status and test qualification are kept apart. Status (what is established about a statement): PROPOSED, INTERPRETIVE, UNPROVEN, TESTABLE, VERIFIED COMPUTATION, PROVED, REJECTED, REVISED. Qualification (what happened during a test): NOT RUN, NOT RUNNABLE, NOT BLIND, INCOMPLETE. A NOT BLIND pass is an exploratory observation and needs a newly registered confirmatory test.
Review terms: pairwise coverage (every pair has an opportunity to compare); independent analysis (each Navigator works without seeing the others); independent verification (a separate method or implementation checks the result); consensus (Navigators agree). The Balanced Comparison Schedule guarantees only the first.
Internal validity: a finding is internally valid in Ω42 when it follows from the stated framework, its definitions and its inference rules; how a finding bears on the world beyond the framework is the business of the comparative annex (L-491), which Ω42 accommodates without deferring to it.

### 231.15 Knowledge classes for readers
Visitors and contributors often bring a ninefold vocabulary of knowledge classes. The record keeps its own statuses (Core Part 10.5.3) and its separate dimensions of test qualification, provenance and readiness (Core Part 10.5.4); the crosswalk below translates and never merges them. Established knowledge: PROVED, or VERIFIED COMPUTATION within its stated scope; knowledge of the world beyond the record is carried by the consensus lane of the CURRENT KNOWLEDGE layer (Core L-503), with its source and grade, and takes no status of the record. Established but contested: a consensus lane and a counter-evidence lane that both found work. Proposed theory: PROPOSED. Hypothesis: TESTABLE once its test and criterion are registered (CA-08), UNPROVEN for a mathematical statement. Interpretation: INTERPRETIVE, at CDT-C. Open problem: UNPROVEN, listed with its UP identifier. Computational result: VERIFIED COMPUTATION, with its run record (environment, code and data fingerprints). Experimental result: VERIFIED COMPUTATION on named real data, with readiness VALIDATED FOR APPLICATION only when the application itself passed. Speculative exploration: PROPOSED with readiness EXPLORATORY. A result keeps one status, and its qualification, provenance and readiness are written beside it, not folded into it.

### PART 232: THE NEW MATHEMATICS READ ACROSS THE COMPANION — WHAT THE RECORD HELD, WHAT IS NEW, AND THE PARTS IT TOUCHES [EXACT for the computations, each a registered test of records/stp/registry.json; X-CONSTRUCTED where marked; CDT-C for the readings]
232.1 Scope. The Companion was read whole, Part by Part, through the mathematics of Construct X (Core Part 10.5; Part 231) and the results of the Knowledge Register. This Part sets out what the Companion already held, what the new results add, and which Parts they touch. No value of any instrument changes.
232.2 What the record already held [EXACT]. The census of the law at every depth, one fixed point, one loop of 8 and 3^(m−1) loops of length 8·3^(m−1), with (9^k + 1)/2 loops at the Ω42 depth k (Part 102.4; Core MF-51), is the count that Construct X re-derives as UP-01e. The labelling of the primitive layer one to one by ±Q (Part 176.4) and the closure of an orbit as a level set of Q² over the 3-adic integers (Core MF-55) hold the orbit signature on the units. K1 is the unit spectrum, the orbit that avoids the ground (Part 39.11), and K2 a convention, its increasing order included (Part 37.6): the selection rests on one structural condition and one stated convention, and axiom-relative uniqueness is read with both (Part 132.3).
232.3 What the orbit theorem adds [EXACT; UP-01d PROVED; UP-01c to 3^6]. The finite statement for every layer: a nonzero state x = 3^r u is named by r and N(u)² mod 3^(k−r). The layers off the primitive one, where ±Q alone stops separating orbits from 27 on (UP-01b), are classified as well, and the canonical orbit is the one class with Λ = (0, 4) (UP-02).
232.4 The workbook, recalculated whole [EXACT; W-001, W-002]. Part 107.2 recomputed the 20,168 node and echo formulas. A full recalculation in LibreOffice covers all 104,925 formulas that hold a stored value, and 104,917 agree. 232.6 Two forecasting rules, one law [EXACT; H-021, H-017b, CX-011, H-006d]. The Construct Engine forecasts row t + 2h from rows t and t + h, the operator (1 − B^h)² (Part 108.3; M326). The Lagged-Increment Model of Construct X uses (1 − B)(1 − B^d), and seasonal-naive (1 − B^d). Each cancels a cycle at its interval, and the first two cancel a linear trend as well. Their noise gains, the sums of their squared coefficients, are 6, 4 and 2, so on a series with a cycle and no trend their held-out errors stand to seasonal-naive's as √3 and √2: 200 series give 1.727 and 1.413. The same law accounts for the slow sequence of Part 108.3, where the latest row wins, and the weekly demonstration of Construct X, where seasonal-naive wins. With trend and cycle together the trend term grows and the Lagged-Increment Model wins; on monthly Mauna Loa CO₂ it has the lowest held-out error of six forecasters, at Candidate Base Lag 12, the interval Part 108.9 found in monthly temperatures.

### PART 233: THE TWO LAYERS OF EXISTENCE — STRUCTURE AND MEANINGFUL EXISTENCE
233.1 Origin and standing [CDT-C; INTERPRETIVE, with EXACT computations]. The Originator distinguished two layers of existence on 19 November 2026. The default layer is recurrence: to exist is to have structure, and physical cycles and habits recur. The meaningful layer is formed by the choices of a person and of their ancestors. APE-502 refined the distinction, and this Part records the model that joins the two. The reading is INTERPRETIVE. The computations it rests on are EXACT and recomputable (tools/choice_engine.py; H-029). The meaningful layer is not separate from physical existence: it arises within it, in living systems that inherit conditions, respond to them and pass on consequences.
233.2 The representation [EXACT]. The law T(a, b) = (b, a + b) is the default layer. It keeps every state on its orbit, so the orbit address Λ never changes under it (checked for every state at 9 and 27). The meaningful layer is an added term: v(t+1) = T v(t) + c(t), where c(t) is what the law did not produce. Solved: v(t) = T^t v(0) + Σ T^(t−1−s) c(s). The starting state v(0) is what is given; the sum carries every earlier choice, the ancestors' and one's own, forward and transformed by the law; c(t) is the only term that belongs to the present. Field Y and the seed offsets already make this split in the Construct: each seed row is Y plus a fixed offset row (Part 231.13). Three facts follow, each computed. (1) Only an added term can change the orbit, and nearly every one does: the share of single choices that move a state to another orbit is 0.736 at 9, 0.910 at 27, 0.970 at 81 (exhaustive) and 0.990 at 243 (sampled; H-029, VERIFIED COMPUTATION). (2) A choice never fades: the law carries the gap between the path with it and the path without it, never zero, returning every 24 steps at 9 and every 72 at 27. (3) A past choice is cancelled exactly only by its present form, the term −T^(t−s) c, not by its original form.
233.3 The channels of inheritance [EXACT decomposition; evidence graded per channel]. APE-502 distinguishes genetic, epigenetic, behavioral and relational, cultural, and institutional inheritance, together with choice. Because the law is linear, the inherited sum splits exactly into one part per channel, and the parts add up to the state (tools/choice_engine.py, selftest). Each channel is therefore tracked apart, with its own evidence grade, and no channel can stand in for another. Genetic: established. Behavioral and relational: established (social learning). Cultural and institutional: established (cultural evolution; Creanza, Kolodny and Feldman, PNAS 2017). Epigenetic transmission across human generations: contested; the evidence 'remains inconclusive' (Bird, Frontiers in Epigenetics and Epigenomics, 2024). Epigenetics is never used as a catch-all for what ancestors lived through. A likeness between generations does not establish a channel; a channel is named only on its own evidence.
233.4 Definitions (from APE-502, refined). ME-01 Structural existence: existence read through the structures, relations, constraints and processes of a system; recurrence, stability, change and emergence belong here (the law). ME-02 Meaningful existence: the historically accumulated configuration of a living being, shaped by inherited conditions, environment, individual and collective choices, and the consequences they pass forward (the added terms and their sum). ME-03 Inheritance: genetic, epigenetic, developmental, behavioral, relational, cultural and institutional transmission, each distinguished and evidenced on its own (233.3). ME-04 Agency: the capacity to respond to conditions by acting; for humans it includes deliberation, intention, interpretation and evaluation, to a degree that varies with person and circumstance. Agency is situated: it acts on a state it did not choose. ME-05 Historical transformation: an action may preserve, modify, interrupt or create a pattern, and so shape later states and later generations. ME-06 Meaning: causal influence is not meaning. Three significances are kept apart: historical (what earlier events caused), experiential (what they mean to the one who lives them) and normative (what is held valuable, harmful, right or wrong). ME-07 Path dependence: the present state depends on the sequence of choices, not only on present conditions; two lives from one starting state part as soon as their added terms differ.
233.5 Received and created meaning. Meaning received is the significance inherited from circumstances, relationships, history and culture: the inherited sum, as it is lived. Meaning created is the significance generated by interpretation, commitment, action and contribution: the present term and what it adds for those who come after. The two interact at every step. Inheritance leads to experience, experience to interpretation, interpretation to choice, choice to consequence, and consequence to inheritance again. The cycle is not closed: each added term can carry it to another orbit, so it can produce something new. Recurrence explains continuity; agency makes transformation possible.
233.6 What the model does not compute. The engine computes historical significance only: which earlier terms are present in a state, and in what form. It does not compute experiential or normative significance, and it gives no score of how meaningful a life is. A single number for the meaningfulness of a life would be philosophically questionable and scientifically premature (APE-502). The Meaning Registry is never read (Core L-497), and no test grades meaning (L-495). The model does not decide whether meaning exists independently of those who find it, or whether it is only inherited, interpreted or made. Those positions are represented side by side, and their consequences are examined, never ruled on.
233.7 What the model says about the Human Condition [INTERPRETIVE]. (a) We are born into histories we did not choose: v(0) and the inherited sum are given, so agency is real but situated. Responsibility is proportionate to knowledge, control, capacity and the alternatives available, and no one is blamed for what they inherited. (b) Patterns outlive their causes: an inherited term recurs with the law long after the conditions that added it are gone, which is why people repeat patterns they dislike. The useful questions are where it began, through which channel it came, what reinforced it, whether it still serves, and what would interrupt it. (c) A person can be a turning point: one added term changes the orbit for everyone downstream. (d) A pattern can change without its origin being understood: nearly every choice moves the orbit (233.2 (1)). Undoing a particular inheritance exactly needs its present form (233.2 (3)), which is the precise sense in which understanding one's history matters. (e) Responsibility runs forward: the present term joins the sum that others will live in. (f) We receive a past we did not make, act in a present we partly shape, and add to a future we will not fully see. A living being is shaped by the history it inherits, and it takes part in shaping the history that follows it.
233.8 Open questions. Whether meaningful existence is human alone: the model applies to any system that receives added terms, and animals with memory, social learning and planning are not excluded without a reason. How the channels can be separated in real lives: a study of one pattern across generations (APE-502 proposes conflict avoidance in families) must establish each channel on its own evidence and must not read likeness as transmission (research/philosophy/MEANINGFUL_EXISTENCE.md). Whether the share of choices that leave the orbit unchanged falls by about a third at each power of 3 (0.264, 0.090, 0.030, 0.010): registered as H-030 and tested blind one level further, at 729, where the share came out at 0.0031 against a predicted band of 0.0027 to 0.0043 (VERIFIED COMPUTATION). A proof is still owed; as a theorem it is UNPROVEN.
233.9 Status. Representation and computations: tools/choice_engine.py (selftest in CI), H-029 and H-030 VERIFIED COMPUTATION (the pattern of H-030 holds at 729; its theorem is UNPROVEN). Definitions ME-01 to ME-07: Companion, CDT-C, not Core terminology; they enter Core Part 10.5 only by amendment and ESC's ratification. The research programme, the Meaningful Existence Initiative, is set out in research/philosophy/MEANINGFUL_EXISTENCE.md, paired with the Common Mathematical Foundations Project (research/physics/INITIATIVE.md): one asks what makes existence structurally possible, the other what makes a particular existence historically and experientially significant.

Part 52.10: the peer architecture's dynamics X(t+1) = F(X(t), E(t)) gains an exact instance, F(X, E) = T X + E. The input E is the added term, the only part of the dynamics that can change the orbit (233.2 (1)). Judgment J = H(Y, V) now has something to act on: it decides the next added term. Part 50.4: MM-06 (iteration of the law gives time and persistence) is the default layer exactly. The mechanisms that act on the state beyond the law are its meaningful layer. Part 33.7: the way and the answer. A way is a sequence of added terms, and meaning that "keeps approaching" is meaning created (233.5), never closed because each term can carry the state to another orbit. Part 116: choosing or resonating. Generation from trained parameters is the AI's default layer. The question whether it chooses becomes the question whether anything in it acts as an added term, and that question stays at the Aperture. The model does not state that the law determines a life; it shows the opposite, that the law alone cannot change an orbit.

The Analog Registry's "structural isomorphisms" are each, on the engine's rules, ANALOGY until the map is written out, ESTABLISHED CONNECTION when a published derivation exists, and NEW DERIVATION only after an independent recomputation. Part 189.2 classifies as ESTABLISHED CONNECTION for its mathematics, a representation of A in SO+(3, 1), and NO PHYSICAL CONSEQUENCE STATED, which matches its own words: "it does not derive relativistic physics". 233.12 The mathematics of the meaningful layer [EXACT for M1 to M6, each proved and checked in tools/choice_engine.py --selftest; the readings CDT-C]. M1 The conserved quantity. The law reverses the sign of the norm, N(T v) = −N(v), with N(a, b) = a² + ab − b², because det T = −1. So N² is conserved along every orbit, and Λ carries it. Under the law alone a state keeps its N² and alternates its sign at every step. M2 What a choice does to it. N(v + c) = N(v) + B(v, c) + N(c), where B(v, c) = 2a·c₀ + a·c₁ + b·c₀ − 2b·c₁ is the bilinear form of N. A choice has an intrinsic weight N(c), the same in every state, and a context term B(v, c), which depends on the state it meets. The same choice made in two lives changes them differently. A choice keeps the orbit only when the two terms balance so that N² is unchanged, and that balance becomes rare as resolution grows (H-029; H-030). M3 A habit is a new default. A choice repeated at every step, v ↦ T v + c, has exactly one center, v* = −T c, because (I − T)⁻¹ = −T (from T² = T + I). Around that center it is the law itself: the same orbits and the same cycle lengths, displaced (checked at 9 and 27). Repeating one choice does not leave the default layer; it moves it. M4 Choices in step with the law. A choice repeated every p steps acts, over one period, as v ↦ T^p v + C. Modulo 9 there are four regimes. At p = 24, T^p = I and the choice accumulates: the state moves by C every period (resonance). At p = 12, T^p = −I and the choice cancels itself every other period (anti-resonance). At p = 8 and 16 it accumulates at the coarse level (modulo 3) and settles at the finer one (partial). At every other p, I − T^p is invertible and the pattern settles round a new center, as in M3. M5 Nothing grows without bound in a finite world. Even resonant accumulation returns: modulo 9 the per-period displacement C has additive order at most 9, so a resonant pattern comes back after at most 9 × 24 = 216 steps. At finer resolution the return takes longer, at most 3^k periods. M6 Inheritance is exact. The inherited sum Σ T^(t−1−s) c(s) splits by channel and by time, and the effect of each past choice at time t is T^(t−1−s) c, its present form (233.2). Reading [CDT-C]. Identity under the default layer is a conserved quantity, N², held while its sign alternates: what persists is the magnitude, not the polarity. A choice has a weight of its own and a meaning that depends on where it lands (M2). Doing the same thing every time does not change one's cycle; it relocates it (M3). What accumulates across a life or across generations is what keeps time with the cycle (M4). A choice repeated at the half-period undoes itself every other time, the form a pattern takes when it appears in one generation, skips the next and returns. Accumulation itself returns in a finite world (M5). These readings are offered as structure, never as a statement about any person or family; the inherited channels keep their own evidence (233.3). Observation. The unchanged share multiplied by 3^k is 2.333, 2.378, 2.428 and 2.450 at k = 1 to 4 (exact: 7/9, 107/405, 5965/66339 for k = 1 to 3). It rises toward a limit near 5/2. That is UNPROVEN and proposed as H-031.
233.13 ME-01 to ME-03 read against the record: coherence, congruence, resonance [EXACT where computed: tools/transformability.py, TR-01 VERIFIED COMPUTATION; the readings CDT-C]. Coherence. The three papers (APE-503 to APE-505) hold together, and their mathematics recomputes. ME-01: the learning rule (1 − α)h + α[(1 − c)h + c r] equals h + αc(r − h). ME-02: at β = 6 the saddle-node boundaries are p = 0.2113 and 0.7887, and the bistable band is a ∈ (−3.415, −2.585). At a = −3 the fixed points are 0.071 (stable, slope 0.394), 0.5 (unstable, slope 1.5) and 0.929 (stable). An intervention γu above 0.415 removes the high state, which does not return when the support is withdrawn: hysteresis, confirmed by simulation. ME-03's controllability matrix and finite-horizon Gramian are stated correctly for linear discrete-time systems. The symbols lost in transcription leave the formulas intact.
233.13a Congruence: where the papers and the record agree. There is no single score; meaning and transformability are profiles (233.6). Channels of inheritance are kept apart and evidenced one by one (233.3). Causal, experiential and normative significance are distinct (ME-06). A likeness between generations is an observation, not a transmission. Studies of persons need consent and ethical oversight (research/philosophy/MEANINGFUL_EXISTENCE.md). Reaching a new state and keeping it are different processes.
233.13b Congruence: where they differ, kept side by side. ME-02 models a habit as an attractor of a dissipative map, one that forgets, so its bistability, tipping and hysteresis are properties of that coarse description. The law is not dissipative: T is invertible and conserves N² (233.12 M1), so it has no attractors and no basins; every state recurs. Inside the law, persistence is conservation, not attraction. One added term changes the orbit, and the new orbit is kept with no further support. ME-02's "changing the rules" (lowering β) has no counterpart inside the frame, because the law is the premise and does not change. Its nearest counterparts are moving the center of a habit (233.12 M3) and changing the regime of a periodic choice (M4). Whether the coarse logistic model arises from the law by coarse-graining with forgetting and noise is an open question (H-033, proposed).
233.13c Resonance: exact correspondences. (R1) Controllability is the norm. For a choice always made along one direction b, the controllability determinant of ME-03 is det[b, T b] = N(b), so the direction is controlling exactly when N(b) is not divisible by 3: 72 of 80 directions modulo 9, and 648 of 728 modulo 27. Two such choices reach every state. The 8 directions that are multiples of 3 cannot steer every coordinate. The record's invariant is the measure of agency. (R2) Historical dependence is hidden state. ME-01's test, I(X_next; H | X_now) > 0, gives 0 bits when the whole state is observed, because the law is deterministic and the inherited sum is already in the state. It gives log₂ 9 = 3.17 bits when only one coordinate is observed. History matters to an observer exactly to the extent that the present is seen partially. (R3) Transmission eigenvalues are golden. ME-01's linear transmission ΔH_n = A^n ΔH_0, read with A = T over the reals, has eigenvalues φ = 1.618 (amplifies) and −1/φ = −0.618 (decays): every past choice has a growing golden part and a shrinking conjugate part. At finite resolution the growth folds back into return (233.12 M5). (R4) The effort to change is not the effort to maintain, in both models: in ME-02 support is needed to cross the threshold and none to stay; in the law one term changes the orbit and conservation keeps it. (R5) ME-02's three outcomes have exact counterparts. Temporary suppression is a term later cancelled by its present form (233.2 (3)). A state transition is a change of orbit. A structural transformation is the recentering of a habit (M3), or, beyond the frame, a change of law.
233.14 TP-01, the Transformability Profile (from ME-03) [definition, Companion terminology]. Transformability is read as six dimensions, never summed: A accessibility, C controllability, P persistence, D historical decoupling, K cost, R risk. Inside the law: A, every state reachable; C, 72 of 80 directions controlling mod 9; P = 1, by conservation; D, none at the level of the state, since every past choice persists in its present form, and full at the level of the orbit once a new orbit is reached; K, one term to change the orbit and two to reach a chosen state; R, not computed, because it is normative (233.6). The profile is computed by tools/transformability.py --report. ME-03's distinction is kept as its last line put it: being able to change is not being able to choose, and being able to choose is not being able to make the choice endure.
233.15 Relations and consensus [EXACT for RC1 to RC5, checked in tools/choice_engine.py --selftest and RC-01, VERIFIED COMPUTATION; the readings CDT-C]. RC1 Influence alone does not make two people agree. Two persons who each follow the law and influence each other by a symmetric scalar k, v' = T v + k w and w' = T w + k v, carry their difference d = v − w by d' = (T − k) d. Its norm is multiplied by k² − k − 1 at every step. Since x² − x − 1 has no root modulo 3, that factor is never divisible by 3, so the difference keeps its class and never vanishes. Modulo 9, for every k and every pair of distinct states, no agreement is ever reached (exhaustive over 72 steps). RC2 The same holds over the reals. With each person following the law and pulled toward the other by any scalar strength, the difference evolves by T − 2a, whose spectral radius is at least √5/2 = 1.118, reached at 2a = 1/2. The law's two eigenvalues, φ and −1/φ, lie √5 apart, more than the width 2 that a single shift can bring inside the unit circle. Disagreement grows under every strength of averaging. RC3 Where averaging does produce consensus. In models where persons have no dynamics of their own and only average one another's beliefs (the weighted-influence model of ME-04, after DeGroot), any pull between 0 and 1 drives the difference to zero. Consensus by averaging is a property of agents without an inner law. The record's persons each carry the law, and for them consensus does not come from interaction alone. RC4 What does produce agreement. Either a choice aimed at the difference, the single added term −(T − k) d, which makes the two states equal at the next step; or influence shaped by the law itself, K = T/2 (each meets the other half way through the other's own dynamics), which gives agreement in one step. Agreement is an act of the meaningful layer, not a product of the default layer. RC5 Consensus reality is the shared mode. In a group pulled toward its mean, the mean follows the law exactly; what the group shares moves as one structure. The deviations of its members persist and grow under averaging (RC2). Shared reality and individual difference are two modes of one system: the first evolves by the law, the second is kept. Reading [CDT-C]. Relationships do not erase difference; they carry it, and difference keeps its class. Agreement is made, not received: it takes a choice that meets the other where they are, in their present form, as cancelling an inherited term takes its present form (233.2 (3)). A society's consensus reality is the mode its members share. It moves by the same law as each of them, and the variety of its members is not averaged away. Consensus is not truth: agreement between parties of one kind is SELF-ADJACENT, and its strength does not establish what is agreed (Core Part 3.18; L-503, the consensus lane beside the counter-evidence lane).
233.16 ME-04, relational reality, taken in (APE-506). The program's architecture, a person coupled to others through asymmetric influence (W_ij ≠ W_ji), is adopted, together with relationships as dynamic systems with their own history, and consensus reality as a collectively maintained model. So are its three distinctions, external, individual and consensus reality; its four agencies, individual, relational, collective and structural; its four collective outcomes, convergence, polarization, transformation and fragmentation, none judged good or bad by the model; and prediction as a distribution of futures, P(S_{t+T} | S_t, U, E), tested on observations not used to build the model (H-ME20). The record adds RC1 to RC5. The program's belief-averaging model converges because its agents have no dynamics of their own. Agents who follow the law need a choice aimed at their difference, or law-shaped influence, to agree, so the program's question of when an emerging interpretation becomes self-reinforcing has, inside the law, the answer "when it is adopted by choice". What mathematics can and cannot say is kept as the program states it: it can describe how consensus forms, persists and changes, and which futures are probable; it cannot establish that a consensus is right, that a life has a given meaning, or that a predicted future ought to happen.
